questions.title: Can I change my CPF nomination? Is there a limit to the number of times I can change my nomination?
questions.text:
Yes, you can change your CPF nomination by making a new nomination. Your new nomination will supersede your existing nomination.
There is no limit to the number of times you can change your nomination.

questions.title: Can I still make a CPF nomination if I am seriously ill?
questions.text:
Yes, you can do so provided you are conscious and must not lack mental capacity when making the nomination.
You can consider appointing a doctor to be one of your witnesses in your nomination. You can request your doctor to write a memo stating that you have the mental capacity to make a CPF nomination and submit it to us.

questions.title: My nominees have changed their personal particulars (e.g. names, addresses or passport numbers). Do I need to update the changes in my CPF nomination?
questions.text:
If your nominee is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
You do not need to update the changes in your CPF nomination.
For name changes, the Board will request your nominee to present document(s) e.g. Deed Poll, as proof of their name change when they apply to withdraw the CPF monies after your demise.
If your nominee is a foreigner
You should make a new CPF nomination with their latest particulars. This will help us identify and contact your nominee easily to distribute your CPF savings.
We also encourage CPF members to indicate the NRIC equivalent of their nominee’s home country in their nomination. This is because passports do expire and nominees may not retain possession of their expired passports when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.

questions.title: What if I am unable to find two witnesses to witness my nomination online?
questions.text:
You can make an appointment at any of our CPF Service Centres to make a CPF Nomination if you cannot find two witnesses online. Our Customer Service Executives will assist you to complete your nomination, and also act as your witnesses. Alternatively, you may visit any of the ServiceSG Centres to make your online CPF nomination.
View the list of ServiceSG Centres locations and its operating hours.

questions.title: Can I make a CPF nomination if I am a bankrupt?
questions.text:
Even if you are bankrupt, you should make a CPF nomination if you want your CPF savings to be distributed according to your wishes.
If you do not make a CPF nomination, your CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution to your family member(s) in accordance with the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims). This ensures that the welfare of your dependants is provided for.

questions.title: What is online nomination? How is it different from submitting a hardcopy nomination?
questions.text:
Online nomination allows you to submit your CPF nomination online, anytime, anywhere, without the need for your witnesses to be physically present to sign the hardcopy form. The process is simple and takes place entirely online:
You log in with your Singpass and submit the online nomination form with the required details.
Inform your witnesses so that they are aware of your intention to make this nomination.
Your appointed witnesses are notified by email and/or SMS to perform witnessing.
The appointed witnesses log in with their Singpass and affirm your intention to make the nomination.

questions.title: Why should I make my CPF nomination online?
questions.text: Online nomination is convenient – you can make your nomination anytime, anywhere. Your personal information is protected as your witnesses will not be able to see your nomination details.

questions.title: What are the things I need to prepare to make an online nomination?
questions.text:
To make an online nomination, you will need:
A valid Singpass
Witnesses’ particulars:
NRIC
Full name** as per NRIC
Email and/or Singapore registered mobile number (for receiving of SMS notification to perform witnessing)
Nominee(s)’ particulars:
NRIC/FIN* (e.g. passport or foreign identification card number)
Full name** as per NRIC/foreign identification document
Mailing address*** (for foreigners only)
Email address (optional)
* While you can indicate passport numbers as the identification number for your nominees, we encourage you to provide your nominee’s NRIC equivalent number in his/her respective home country instead as passports can expire.
** It is important to provide full names of your nominees and witnesses as indicated on their NRICs, including comma, hyphen and space accordingly. However, you should exclude the Hanyu Pinyin, Alias and married name. See examples of NRIC names.
*** Mailing address is required for foreigners to facilitate us in contacting them when distributing your CPF savings. Mailing address for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will be based on the address registered with Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).

questions.title: Is it safe to make my CPF nomination online?
questions.text:
There are multiple layers of checks in place so that CPF members can make their nomination online in a safe and secure manner.
A Singpass is required to log in securely to my cpf digital services to make your online nomination. Singpass has multiple layers of security measures in place, including Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) login. We will also send SMS and email notification alerts to your registered mobile number/email address when you make your nomination online.
The combination of these measures will provide a safe and secure environment for you to make your nomination online.
You are also encouraged to adopt good security practices such as not sharing your Singpass credentials with others and changing your passwords regularly.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my nomination?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your online nomination at cpf.gov.sg/Activities using your Singpass.
We will send you an email/SMS once your nomination is routed to your witnesses. Upon the completion of witnessing by your witnesses, we will generally process your nomination within four working days. You will also receive an email/SMS of the status.
Once your online nomination has been processed, you will receive one more email/SMS notification on the final status of your nomination.
If you wish to view the details of your nomination, you can then access the information at cpf.gov.sg/viewnomdetails.

questions.title: How many nominees can I specify in my online nomination?
questions.text: You can specify up to 15 nominees. If you wish to nominate more than 15 nominees, you can make a nomination at our CPF Service Centres.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to amend an online nomination I have submitted?
questions.text:
You can amend your nomination if either or both your witnesses have not witnessed your nomination. You can do so by withdrawing your nomination and submitting a new one.
If both your witnesses have already witnessed your nomination, you will not be able to withdraw and amend the nomination. However, you can submit a new nomination after your earlier nomination is processed. Your new nomination will supersede your earlier nomination.
You can only submit one nomination within the same day. This includes the nomination that has had its witnessing process completed that day.

questions.title: How can I withdraw my online nomination?
questions.text:
You can withdraw your application so long as at least one of your witnesses has yet to complete the witnessing:
Log in to my cpf digital services using your Singpass at cpf.gov.sg/Activities.
In transaction details, click on “withdraw this application” and confirm your intent to withdraw the application.
Please note that after you withdraw your online nomination, your existing nomination status remains unchanged. If both your witnesses have completed their witnessing and you wish to make a new nomination, you can submit one via this link.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the name I keyed for my nominee was different from his NRIC/CPF Account No. How can I resolve this?
questions.text:
For Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident nominees, you must enter their full name exactly as shown on their NRIC, including all punctuation marks like commas (,), hyphens (-), slashes (/) and the arrangement of how the name is spelt.
Do not include Hanyu Pinyin, aliases, or married names.
If you are still facing submission issues, here are some troubleshooting steps:
Name Format
Ensure correct spacing between characters (e.g., "John⎵Tan" should not be indicated as "John⎵⎵Tan" or "John⎵Tan⎵")
Write relationship indicators without spaces (e.g., "D/O" not "D / O", and likewise for "S/O")
John Tan should be indicated as John Tan and not Tan John
Technical Tips
Type the nominee's details directly instead of copy-pasting from other sources to avoid hidden characters
For iOS users (such as iPhone or iPad): Disable “Smart Punctuation” under Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation
Use only one browser tab and clear your browser cache
Try using a different device if the problem persists
If the error continues, you can:
Write to us with the following details:
A screenshot of your nominee's name
The error occurrence time and date
Your device details
Visit any Service SG Centres for assistance with your online nomination
Make your nomination at our CPF Service Centres

questions.title: I am using an iOS device (iPhone or iPad) to submit my online nomination, and I was not able to submit my nominee's particulars. How can I resolve this?
questions.text: If you are using an iOS device (such as iPhone or iPad) to submit your nomination, the “Smart Punctuation” feature in iOS may prevent you from submitting your nomination. You can disable the feature by performing the following steps on your device: Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation.

questions.title: How do I submit an organisation as my nominee in my online nomination?
questions.text: If you would like to nominate an organisation, select 'Registration No.' under the ‘Select identification type’ field and indicate the organisation’s unique corporate registration number (such as Unique Entity Number (UEN)) in the ‘Registration number of organisation’ field.

questions.title: What should I do if I encounter problems with the online nomination service?
questions.text:
If you are encountering problems, you can troubleshoot most errors by performing the following steps:
Avoid copy-pasting the details from another program or app as there might be hidden characters that might get copied. Key in the nominee’s particulars directly instead.
If you are using an iOS device (such as iPhone or iPad), disable the “Smart Punctuation” feature in iOS (iOS device Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation). This feature might create unrecognisable characters in the application form.
Avoid opening multiple browser tabs. Use only one browser tab and clear your browser cache.
Consider using a different device to submit your nomination if submission via your original device is still unsuccessful.
If you are still facing problems after performing the above troubleshooting steps, you can write to us so that we can look into it.
Alternatively, you may visit any of our CPF Service Centres to make a nomination in-person.

questions.title: Is there an administrative fee when I submit my nomination online?
questions.text: There is no administrative fee to make a CPF nomination.

questions.title: How long will CPF Board take to process my online nomination?
questions.text: If you submit your nomination online, the Board will process it generally within four working days from the date that both your witnesses complete the witnessing of your nomination. You can check the status of your online nomination under “Activities” by logging in to my cpf Online Services using your Singpass.

questions.title: What information relating to my witnesses do I need to provide when I make a nomination online?
questions.text:
You will need to provide the following information of your witnesses when making an online nomination:
NRIC
Full Name* as per NRIC
Email and/or Singapore registered mobile number (for receiving of SMS notification to perform witnessing)
*It is important to provide your witnesses' full name as indicated on his NRIC, including comma, hyphen and space accordingly. However, you should exclude the Hanyu Pinyin, Alias and married name. See examples of NRIC names.

questions.title: Am I allowed to submit another online nomination if my previous nomination is still pending action from my witnesses?
questions.text:
You cannot submit another nomination if you have an existing nomination pending witnessing. However, if any of your witnesses has not completed their witnessing, you can withdraw your nomination and submit a new one.
How can I withdraw my online nomination?

questions.title: Can I submit more than one nomination online within the same day?
questions.text:
You can only submit one nomination within the same day. This includes the nomination that has had its witnessing process completed that day.
If you wish to submit a new nomination, you may withdraw the current one if your witnesses have not witnessed it. If both your witnesses have already witnessed your nomination, you can submit a new nomination after your earlier nomination is processed. Your new nomination will supersede your earlier nomination.
How can I withdraw my online nomination?

questions.title: Who is eligible to make a nomination online?
questions.text: CPF members who are aged 16 and above, and have a valid Singpass, are eligible to make a nomination online.

questions.title: I have been requested to witness an online nomination. What do I need to do?
questions.text:
As a witness, you will need to declare that you are aware of the CPF member’s intention to make a nomination and specify how the request was communicated to you.
If you are ready with this information, please login with your Singpass to complete your witnessing.
You can view the video guide for more information on being a witness for a CPF nomination online.

questions.title: Why can't witnesses view the CPF member's nomination details?
questions.text: The role of a witness is to affirm the CPF member’s intention to make a CPF nomination. There is no need for witnesses to know the nomination details to perform their role as witnesses.

questions.title: Is there a deadline for me to witness an online nomination?
questions.text:
Yes, you have seven calendar days from the time you receive the SMS/email notification request to complete the witnessing.
If you cannot complete the witnessing in time, please inform the CPF member, as the nomination application will expire and the CPF member will need to submit a new application.

questions.title: Why can't I access the online nomination witnessing request that was sent to me?
questions.text:
You will not be able to access the online nomination witnessing request if:
the nomination application had expired (after seven calendar days from application date);
the member making the CPF nomination has withdrawn the nomination; or
you have already completed witnessing the nomination.

questions.title: How can I be sure that I'm witnessing a legitimate nomination?
questions.text: It is your responsibility as a witness to ensure that the CPF member making the nomination has specifically requested for you to witness his nomination. You should check with the member to affirm his intention to make a CPF nomination before proceeding to witness his nomination.

questions.title: I received a request to witness an online nomination from someone I do not know. What should I do?
questions.text: Do not complete the witnessing process. Please contact us immediately so that we can follow up with the CPF member.

questions.title: What supporting documents do I need if I am making a nomination at the CPF Service Centre?
questions.text: You are strongly encouraged to bring along photocopies of your nominee(s)’ identification documents (such as NRIC or foreign identification document) indicating their particulars.

questions.title: Do I need my own witnesses to be present if I am making my nomination at any CPF Service Centre?
questions.text: Our Customer Service Executives can act as your witnesses.

questions.title: How can I check my CPF nomination details?
questions.text:
You can view your CPF nomination details using your Singpass. However, please note that nominations made more than 30 years ago cannot be viewed online.
If your nomination is over 30 years old, we strongly recommend making a new nomination even if you wish to nominate the same nominees:
Allow your CPF savings to be distributed in accordance with your latest wishes
Update your nominees' personal information for swift identification and contact
Enable convenient online access to your nomination details
Making a new nomination is a simple process. Find out how you can make a CPF nomination.

questions.title: My elderly parent would like to check his/her existing CPF nomination. How can I help him/her do so?
questions.text:
Your parent can view his/her CPF nomination details online with his/her Singpass.
If the details (i.e. nominee and nominee share) of the nomination cannot be viewed online, this would mean that the CPF nomination was made more than 30 years ago.
Instead of retrieving the nomination details, which may be outdated as it was made some time back, CPF members should make a new nomination. This is because bequeath intentions may have since changed. The particulars or contact information of the nominees may also be outdated. It is recommended for CPF members to review their nominations annually and make a new nomination (if necessary) to update it.
Making a new nomination allows CPF members to update their latest bequest intentions so that their CPF savings can be distributed in accordance with their latest circumstances. Providing the Board with the nominee’s latest particulars and contact information will enable the Board to identify them easily and contact them promptly to claim the CPF savings upon the member’s demise.
Making a new nomination is easy and convenient. Find out how a CPF member can make a CPF nomination.

questions.title: Do I need to authorise specific person(s) to access my CPF account information when I pass away?
questions.text:
From 1 February 2024, nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws will be allowed to access your CPF account information, after your passing.
With this change, there is no longer a need for you to authorise your loved ones to access your CPF account information upon demise.

questions.title: I have appointed authorised person (AP) in my nomination to access my CPF account information upon my demise, but I can no longer see the appointed AP under my nomination dashboard. Do I need to make a new nomination to appoint AP again?
questions.text:
From 1 February 2024, nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws will be able to access your CPF account information after your passing.
This change brings greater convenience to members and makes it easier for their loved ones to settle matters relating to the deceased member’s CPF accounts.
Your appointed authorised persons will still be able to access your CPF account information upon your demise if they are your nominees or eligible family member. Else, your information will not be disclosed to them.

questions.title: What CPF account information can my nominees and eligible family members under intestacy laws access, upon my demise?
questions.text:
Your nominees and eligible family members can access the following information:
CPF account balances and past 15 months' transaction history
Nomination details
CPF schemes which you have participated in

questions.title: Can anyone access my CPF account information while I am still alive?
questions.text: No. Your CPF account information is confidential. No one will be able to access your CPF account information while you are alive.

questions.title: Can I instruct CPF Board to disallow my nominees or family members from accessing my CPF account information, upon my demise?
questions.text:
No. Allowing your nominees and family members to access your CPF account information make it easier for them to reconcile your CPF account information and settle any post-demise matters relating to your CPF account.
This practice is also aligned with industry standards on matters such as for estate distribution under wills and distribution of assets by the Public Trustee’s Office, where details of the distribution can be provided to all beneficiaries.
Please be assured that your CPF information remains confidential while you are alive. Your nominees and family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws can only access your CPF account information after you have passed away.

questions.title: Can I instruct CPF Board to allow person(s) who are neither my nominees nor family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws, to access my CPF account information, after my death?
questions.text: No, you cannot instruct the Board to allow any other persons other than your nominees or family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws to access your CPF account information, upon your demise.

questions.title: Who are the family members eligible to access the CPF account information of a deceased CPF member?
questions.text:
Family members, as defined under the Intestacy or Inheritance law distribution rules, will be eligible to access the information.
a. If the deceased member is a Muslim:
The eligible family members under the Muslim Inheritance law will be based on the Certificate of Inheritance issued by the Syariah Court.
b. If the deceased member is a non-Muslim:
The eligible family members will be based on the Intestate Succession Act distribution rules, in the following order:
If the deceased member hasEligible family members will be
Spouse and childrenSpouse and children[1]
No spouseChildren[1]
No childrenSpouse and parent
No children
No parentSpouse
No spouse
No childrenParents
No spouse
No children
No parentsSiblings[2]
No spouse
No children
No parents
No siblingsGrandparents
No spouse
No children
No parents
No siblings
No grandparentsUncles and aunts
[1] If children have passed away, the eligible family members will be their children
(i.e. Grandchildren) instead.
[2] If siblings have passed away, the eligible family members will be their children
(i.e. Nephews and nieces) instead.

questions.title: Will I be able to access the CPF account information of a deceased CPF member?
questions.text:
If CPF Board is notified* of the death before 1 February 2024
If the deceased member had appointed authorised persons in his/her CPF nomination, only the authorised persons can access his/her CPF account information.
If CPF Board is notified* of the death on or after 1 February 2024
Nominees and family members who are eligible beneficiaries under intestacy laws will be able to access a deceased member's CPF account information.
*Please note that the notification date may not be the same as the actual date of death of the CPF member.

questions.title: I am a nominee of a deceased CPF member. How can I access the member's CPF account information?
questions.text:
If CPF Board is notified of the death of the member on or after 1 February 2024
If you are a nominee of the deceased CPF member, you can view the deceased member's CPF information on the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard, by logging in with your Singpass. Please wait at least 10 working days from the notice of death.
If you do not have Singpass, please submit a request instead.
If you are a family member but not a nominee, you can visit this FAQ to find out how you can also access the deceased member's CPF account information.
If CPF Board is notified of the death of the member before 1 February 2024
Only authorised persons appointed by the deceased member can view his CPF account information. If you are an authorised person, please submit a request to view the deceased member’s CPF account information.

questions.title: I am a family member of a deceased CPF member, but I am not a nominee. How can I access the member's CPF account information?
questions.text:
If CPF Board is notified of the death of the member before 1 February 2024
Only authorised persons appointed by a deceased member can view the deceased member’s CPF information. If you are an authorised person, please submit a request to view the deceased member’s CPF information.
If CPF Board is notified of the death of the member on or after 1 February 2024
Family members are encouraged to discuss this matter and submit one request to access the deceased member’s account information. An eligible family member can be appointed by the family as the representative to submit the request. The representative family member may then share this information upon approval to access the deceased member’s CPF account information.
Please note that requests should only be submitted four weeks after the death of the member. The representative family member can submit a request with supporting documents to prove the relationship with the deceased member. The Board will review the request within 10 working days and inform the representative how to access the deceased member’s CPF account information.
If you do not have Singpass, you can apply for a Singpass online.
If you are not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please submit a request.
To check your eligibility to access the deceased member’s CPF account information, please refer to the FAQ.

questions.title: Can I make or revoke a CPF nomination on someone's behalf?
questions.text:
A CPF nomination must be made or revoked by the CPF member personally.
However, if a CPF member lacks capacity under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act ("MCA"), only the Courts are allowed to make or revoke a CPF nomination on behalf of the member.
An interested party can apply to the Court to do so, and the court would decide in the interest of the member who is lacking capacity, whether to accept the application to make or revoke a CPF nomination on his behalf.

questions.title: How can a donee/deputy make or revoke a CPF nomination for members who lack mental capacity?
questions.text: For CPF members who lack capacity under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act ("MCA"), only the Courts can make or revoke a CPF nomination on their behalf.

questions.title: What are the documents that CPF Board requires if the Court has accepted an application to make or revoke a nomination and how should these documents be submitted?
questions.text:
Make a CPF nomination for members who lack mental capacity
If the Court accepts the application to make a CPF nomination on behalf of a member, the court may appoint a person to carry out the making of the nomination.
If you are the person appointed by the Court to carry out the making of the nomination, please complete the relevant CPF nomination form and indicate that you are the authorised person ordered by the Court to make the CPF nomination on behalf of the member who lacks capacity. The CPF nomination form must be affixed with the Court's Seal.
The witnesses to the nomination may be our Customer Service Executives (CSEs) at any of our Service Centres. If 2 other witnesses are chosen, please note that the witnesses to the CPF nomination must be at least 21 years old and not lack capacity. Please note that the witnesses cannot be the nominees or the authorised person signing on behalf of the member.
We encourage you to hand-deliver the completed CPF nomination form (affixed with the Court's Seal), with a certified true copy of the Order of Court and your NRIC to any CPF Service Centre. Alternatively, you may wish to send the documents to the Board by post. You can mail the documents to:
Attention: Nominations Department
Central Provident Fund Board
PRIVY Box No 920651
Singapore 929292
Revoke a CPF nomination for members who lack mental capacity
If the Court accepts your application to revoke the CPF nomination, and makes the order revoking the CPF nomination, please furnish the Board with a copy of the Order of Court and your NRIC (both documents to be certified as true copies by your lawyers).
We encourage you to hand-deliver the completed CPF revocation form (affixed with the Court's Seal), with a certified true copy of the Order of Court and your NRIC to any CPF Service Centre. Alternatively, you may wish to send the documents to the Board by post. You can mail the documents to:
Attention: Nominations Department
Central Provident Fund Board
PRIVY Box No 920651
Singapore 929292
You should seek your lawyer's advice as an application to court is required.

questions.title: How does CPF Board ensure that changes to CPF nomination of members who lack mental capacity, are done in their best interest?
questions.text:
The treatment of CPF nominations has been aligned with that of wills under the Mental Capacity Act 2008 (MCA).
Safeguards are in place under the MCA as the Court in making decisions on behalf of a member who lacks capacity, has to take into account what is in the member's "best interests". This includes taking into consideration the member's past and present wishes and feelings, his beliefs and values that would likely influence his decision if he had the mental capacity. The Court will also have to take into account the views from persons who were close to the member.

questions.title: What happens if the CPF Board finds out that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity?
questions.text:
If the Board is informed of any facts or circumstances which may affect the validity of the CPF nomination and has evidence and supporting documents to ascertain the fact that the member lacked capacity at the time of making the CPF nomination, the Board will invalidate the CPF nomination made by such a member.
Anyone, who is of the view that the CPF nomination is invalid on the grounds that the member lacked capacity at the time the said CPF nomination was made, could also apply to Court to set aside the nomination.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF nomination if I lose mental capacity after making my nomination?
questions.text: Your CPF nomination will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity.

questions.title: Can I appoint someone to make or revoke my CPF nomination on my behalf before I lose mental capacity?
questions.text: No. Only the Court is allowed to make or revoke a CPF nomination on behalf of the member, under Section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008.

questions.title: What happens if the CPF Board deems that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity?
questions.text: If the CPF Board deems that the CPF nomination was made whilst the member lacked capacity within the meaning of section 4 of the Mental Capacity Act 2008, the Board will invalidate the nomination. The previous CPF nomination (if any) made by the member would remain valid (assuming the member did not lack capacity when he made the previous CPF nomination). The member's CPF savings would be distributed in accordance with the intention of the member in his previous valid CPF nomination. If there is no previous valid CPF nomination, the CPF savings would be paid to the Public Trustee for distribution in accordance with intestacy laws.

questions.title: Can both parents nominate the same child with disabilities?
questions.text: Both parents of an eligible child with disabilities can participate in the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS). The child with disabilities will then receive separate streams of payout from each parent’s CPF savings upon the parent’s demise.

questions.title: Can parents cancel their Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination after making one?
questions.text:
Parents can cancel their Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination by making a new CPF nomination.
The new nomination will supersede the SNSS nomination which they have made earlier.
To make a nomination, you can do so online using your Singpass.

questions.title: Will there be a charge levied on members for Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)?
questions.text: There will be no charge levied on members for making a CPF nomination under Special Needs Savings Scheme.

questions.title: Apart from Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), how else can parents set aside money for their child under the CPF system?
questions.text:
Parents can also set aside money for their child by topping up to the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nominee's CPF accounts based on current CPF rules. These top-up monies will enjoy CPF interest rates and will be set aside specifically for the child's retirement needs instead of being disbursed under the SNSS.
For parents who are under the CPF LIFE scheme, and have made a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination, they can opt not to receive their monthly CPF LIFE payouts, and retain the monies in their Retirement Account (RA).
To do so, members can inform the Board of their intention in writing at least 2 months before their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) or anytime after they have reached their PEA. In the request, members should indicate their name, NRIC number, signature and their intention to retain their CPF LIFE payouts in their CPF Retirement Accounts (RA) for the benefit of their SNSS nominee(s).

questions.title: Can parents determine the amount of monthly payouts for their nominated child with disabilities?
questions.text: Parents can determine the amount of monthly payout for their nominated child with disabilities at the point of application, subject to a minimum payout of $250 per month with a minimum duration of at least one year.

questions.title: I would like to change how much my child can receive monthly under the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), how can I make the change?
questions.text: Under the Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), parents can revise the monthly payout by submitting a new nomination indicating the new amount.

questions.title: How do I make a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nomination?
questions.text:
The Special Needs Saving Scheme (SNSS) caters to Persons with Special Needs (PSN) who are nominated by their parents to draw a fixed monthly payout from the parents' CPF savings upon the parents' demise.
For more details on SNSS, please visit SNTC's website.

questions.title: What is the Special Needs Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
The Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) allows parents of children with special needs to nominate their child to receive a regular stream of fixed payouts from their CPF savings in the event of the parent’s demise.
CPF members interested to nominate their children under SNSS can approach the Special Needs Trust Company for more information.

questions.title: How is Special Needs Savings Scheme different from CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Unlike a CPF nomination, where the member’s CPF savings are distributed in one lump sum, CPF savings under Special Needs Savings Scheme will be distributed to the nominee on a monthly basis, based on the amount specified by the CPF member, until the bequeathed savings run out.
This enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long term care of children with special needs.

questions.title: Can I nominate part of my CPF balances under the Special Needs Savings Scheme, while nominating the rest under the CPF cash nomination?
questions.text: Yes. You can decide the percentage of your CPF balances to be nominated under the Special Needs Savings Scheme, and the remaining CPF savings to be nominated under the cash nomination rules for other beneficiaries.

questions.title: What interest rates will be paid on the monies for Special Needs Savings Scheme nominees?
questions.text:
The nominated monies will continue to earn the same CPF interest, including extra interest, in the SNSS nominee’s account, as the rate earned by CPF members.
Extra interest is paid on the first $60,000 of the combined balance of the parent(s) who nominated the child under SNSS and the child’s own CPF savings, with up to $20,000 from the child’s Ordinary Account.
Please refer to CPF interest rates for more information on the CPF interest rates.

questions.title: Who should I contact if I want to know more information on the Special Needs Savings Scheme?
questions.text:
You may contact the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) who is the appointed scheme administrator.
Parents can visit SNTC’s SNSS website. Alternatively, SNTC can be contacted via phone at 6278 9598 or via email at enquiries@sntc.org.sg for more information.

questions.title: What is the sequence of disbursement for Special Needs Saving Scheme's monthly payout from CPF account? (i.e. which of the deceased's CPF account will be disbursed first?)
questions.text: The CPF savings nominated under Special Needs Savings Scheme will be paid via monthly payouts, starting from the lowest interest earning account, i.e. the Nominee Ordinary Account (NOA) first before moving to Nominee Special Account (NSA) and then Nominee Retirement Account (NRA).

questions.title: How fast can a Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS) nominee receive the fund into their bank account after the death of member?
questions.text: For Special Needs Savings Scheme cases, the payment will commence in the following month upon receipt of the completed application form and supporting documents. The payment is generally processed on the 12th of every month until the monies due to the nominee are exhausted.

questions.title: What is required before making an SNSS nomination?
questions.text:
Before you apply for SNSS nomination, you are required to obtain an eligibility letter from Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC). SNTC will issue the letter to you after confirming your nominee’s eligibility for the SNSS. You may then proceed to any of our Service Centres to make the SNSS nomination.
For more details on SNSS, please visit SNTC’s website.

questions.title: What happens to a member's CPF savings when he passes away?
questions.text:
The distribution of a deceased member's CPF savings depends on whether he had made a valid CPF nomination before his passing. Find out what is covered under CPF nomination.
If the deceased member had made a valid CPF nomination, his remaining CPF savings and discounted Singtel shares (if any) will be distributed in cash to his nominee(s) according to his CPF nomination.
If the deceased member had not made a valid CPF nomination, his remaining CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution according to the intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws. Find out how you can claim the deceased member’s discounted Singtel shares if he did not make any nomination.
Under this process, beneficiaries will need to provide documentation to prove their relationship with the deceased member. As time and effort is required to identify and verify the eligible beneficiaries, the entire process may take up to six months, and will incur an administrative fee. PTO will deduct this fee from the deceased member's CPF savings, which means beneficiaries will receive a lesser amount of CPF savings.
Make a CPF nomination so that your CPF savings are swiftly distributed to your loved ones when you are no longer around.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What are the CPF monies and assets of a deceased member covered under a CPF nomination?
questions.text:
The table below shows which of a deceased member’s CPF monies and assets are covered/not covered under a CPF nomination:
Covered under CPF nomination
Not covered under CPF nomination
CPF savings in Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts
CPF LIFE premium balance, if any
Discounted Singtel shares
Properties bought using CPF savings
Payouts from Dependants’ Protection Scheme
Investments under CPF Investment Scheme
For more information, you can refer to the Losing a Loved One (PDF, 1.4MB) brochure.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How will the deceased member's CPF monies and assets be distributed if he was a bankrupt?
questions.text:
The treatment of a deceased bankrupt member's CPF monies and assets depends on whether there is a valid nomination.
If the deceased member had made a valid nomination, his remaining CPF savings and discounted Singtel Shares (if any) are protected and, will be distributed in cash to his nominee(s).
If the deceased member had not made a valid nomination, his remaining CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee's Office (PTO) for distribution according to the intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws. However, his discounted Singtel shares (if any) are due to his estate and the Official Assignee may lay claims on the shares.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Will the deceased member's CPF savings continue to earn interest after his death?
questions.text: The deceased member's CPF savings will continue to earn base interest in the respective accounts for up to six months. However, the CPF savings will not earn extra interest once we are notified of the member's death. Nominee(s) have the right to claim the nominated savings at any time but they are encouraged to submit the withdrawal application as early as possible.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to a deceased member's discounted Singtel shares?
questions.text:
The treatment of the deceased member's discounted Singtel shares depends on whether he had made a valid nomination before his passing.
If the deceased member had made a valid nomination, his discounted Singtel shares will be distributed to his nominee(s) in the proportion he had indicated in his CPF nomination form. The nominee can either instruct the Board to sell the shares or transfer the shares to his Central Depository (Pte) Ltd securities account.
If the deceased member had not made a valid nomination, his discounted Singtel shares will form part of his estate. Find out how you can claim the deceased member's un-nominated discounted Singtel shares.
The dividends and proceeds stop earning CPF interest upon the member's passing, as they are not CPF monies but assets held on behalf of beneficiaries or as part of the deceased member's estate.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's CPF LIFE premium?
questions.text: The deceased member's CPF LIFE premium balance (if applicable) will be paid to his nominee(s) together with his CPF savings.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Can the deceased member's MediSave be used to pay his final hospitalisation bill?
questions.text:
Yes, the deceased member’s entire MediSave can be used to pay the last hospital bill if he had signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), which authorises the use of the deceased member’s MediSave to pay the hospitalisation bill, before his passing.
Any remaining MediSave after the payment of the last medical bill will be distributed to the deceased member’s nominee(s) if he had a valid nomination. This is provided that the MediSave deduction is completed before the distribution of the deceased member’s CPF balances.
If the deceased member had not signed the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF), his spouse, parents, child (if age 21 or older), or donee/deputy can sign the form at the hospital. You are encouraged to do this as soon as possible as hospitals have to submit the MediSave claim before the deceased member’s MediSave is distributed (typically within two weeks of the member’s passing). If the deceased member’s MediSave has been distributed, you will not be able to use his MediSave for the last hospital bill.
If there is no immediate family or donee/deputy, a caregiver who has been taking care of the deceased member during his lifetime may write to the Ministry of Health through the hospital to seek approval for the use of the deceased member’s MediSave for the last hospital bill.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Will the deceased member's CPF savings be used to pay his income tax liabilities?
questions.text: No, the deceased member’s CPF savings will not be used to pay his income tax liabilities. This is because CPF savings do not form part of the deceased member’s estate.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's investments bought using his CPF savings?
questions.text:
CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) investments are not covered under CPF nomination. When a member passes away, his CPFIS investments* and any cash balance in his Investment Account will form part of his estate. Doing so allows beneficiaries of the estate to decide how best to manage these assets, including the preferred timing for the sale of assets such as unit trusts and stocks. These decisions should be made by the beneficiaries as the decisions could affect the value of the CPFIS investments. CPF monies covered under CPF nomination can then be disbursed quickly without having to await the beneficiaries’ decision on the CPFIS investments.
The estate administrator/executor can contact the respective product providers or agent bank to claim the investments and cash balance. These investments, cash balance and death benefits may be used to settle the deceased member’s debts in accordance with the Probate and Administration Act.
* Except for insurance policies where the member had made an insurance nomination with the respective insurance company. The nominated beneficiaries can contact the insurance company to claim the death benefits.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's property bought using his CPF savings?
questions.text: The CPF savings used to buy the property need not be refunded to the deceased member’s CPF account. The property will form part of his estate if it is held in tenancy-in-common or passed on to the remaining surviving owner(s) if it is held in joint tenancy.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the deceased member's CPF savings used for CPF Education Loan Scheme?
questions.text: If the deceased member’s CPF savings had been used under the CPF Education Loan Scheme for himself or someone else, the withdrawn monies, including accrued interest, do not have to be refunded to his account.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How do I report the death of a foreigner who was a CPF member?
questions.text:
You can report the death of a foreigner who was a CPF member by making an appointment to visit our CPF Service Centre, with the following documents:
Deceased member’s original death certificate and current passport duly cancelled due to his passing
Letter from an official authority showing the deceased member’s identity number, (if not shown on death certificate)
Evidence of your relationship with the deceased member
Your identity card or passport, and contact details
Alternatively, you can submit the documents above via post. If you are posting the documents overseas, please make sure that the copies are certified by an official from a Singapore Overseas Mission with their official seal/stamp.
Please mail the documents to:
Central Provident Fund Board
Nominations and Accounts Closure Department
238B Thomson Road
#08-00 Tower B Novena Square
Singapore 307685
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: I have applied to withdraw the deceased member's CPF savings. Can I change my payment details?
questions.text:
You can change your payment details for your application to withdraw the deceased member’s CPF savings by submitting the form applicable to you:
If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please update your bank account details with CPF Board via my cpf digital services - Account settings with your Singpass.
If you are not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please complete the form “Change payment details (for withdrawal of deceased member’s CPF savings or account closure)” (Form NAC/SUPP/F) and mail it back to us.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Is there a deadline for me to claim the deceased member's CPF savings?
questions.text: You are encouraged to claim the deceased member's CPF savings as early as possible as the deceased member's CPF savings will cease earning base interest in the respective accounts six months after the Board is notified of the member's demise. You can do so anytime by submitting an online application.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: I am an appointed nominee. How will the deceased member's CPF savings be paid to me if I am bankrupt?
questions.text: By operation of Singapore’s bankruptcy laws, if you are an undischarged bankrupt at the time of the member’s death, the nominated monies vest in the trustee in bankruptcy, for the benefit of your creditors. We will notify the Official Assignee (OA), who maintains the Bankruptcy Estate Account on behalf of all trustees, and transfer the nominated monies to the OA upon his instructions.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: What happens to the CPF savings if the nominee passed away before he could receive the CPF savings of the deceased member?
questions.text:
The CPF savings would form part of the deceased nominee's estate and would be paid to the Executor/Administrator appointed under the Grant of Probate (GP)/Letters of Administration (LA). For more information on how to apply for a GP or LA, visit Singapore Courts' website.
If there is no Executor/Administrator appointed, the CPF savings may be paid to a proper claimant if the estate does not exceed $50,000. Write to us for more details about the application via the proper claimant route.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: Who is a proper claimant and when can they claim monies due to the deceased member/nominee's estate?
questions.text:
A proper claimant is a beneficiary, usually a family member, of the deceased member/nominee. The proper claimant can claim monies due to the deceased member/nominee's estate via an application process. This applies when no executor or administrator has been appointed for the deceased member/nominee’s estate and the estate does not exceed $50,000, covering two scenarios:
Dividends, sale proceeds and other monies in respect of discounted Singtel shares belonging to a deceased member who passed away without a nomination; or
Nominated CPF savings that would have been paid to the deceased nominee who had passed away before he could receive it.
Write to us for more details about the application via the proper claimant route.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How will the deceased member's CPF savings be distributed to a nominee who is certified to lack mental capacity permanently?
questions.text: If the nominee has a donee appointed through a Lasting Power of Attorney or a deputy appointed via a court order under the Mental Capacity act, the donee and deputy can submit the withdrawal application and receive payment on the nominee's behalf.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: How do I claim the CPF savings of a family member who has been missing for many years?
questions.text:
You will first need to obtain a presumption of death certificate, which declares the person as presumed to be dead, from the Court. This is in line with industry practice where a person is treated as alive until the person has been officially reported as deceased. For any financial assistance in obtaining the presumption of death certification from the Court, you can contact the Legal Aid Bureau.
If the missing person is a Singapore citizen or Permanent Resident, after having obtained the presumption of death certificate, the missing person should be reported as deceased with the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Once this is done, his CPF savings will be distributed to his appointed nominee(s) if he has a valid nomination. Otherwise, his CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution according to intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.
If the missing person is a foreigner who holds a CPF account, the following documents have to be submitted at any of our CPF Service Centres:
i. the original presumption of death certificate;
ii. the missing person’s original passport (if any);
iii. an original letter from the relevant authority confirming the missing person’s identity number (if the presumption of death certificate does not bear the missing person’s identification details);
iv. documentary evidence of your relationship with the missing person; and
v. your original identity card/passport and contact details.
If the death reporting is submitted via post from outside of Singapore, all the documents mentioned above have to be certified true by an official from a Singapore Overseas Mission with their official seal/stamp duly affixed.
Once the missing person is officially reported as deceased, his CPF savings will be distributed to his appointed nominee(s) if he has a valid nomination. Otherwise, his CPF savings will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution according to intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.
topics: Account Services / Distribution of CPF savings upon member's passing

questions.title: If I am currently using my Special Account (SA) for Dependants' Protection Scheme premiums, how would I be impacted by the closure of SA?
questions.text:
After your Special Account (SA) closes at age 55, your Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) premiums can only be paid from your CPF Ordinary Account (OA), subject to available balance, or in cash directly to the appointed DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life.
Transition measures are in place to provide short-term support to members immediately affected by the SA closure. These members will be notified directly and advised on the necessary steps to take.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What is the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
The Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) is a term-life insurance that provides financial support to insured members and their families during the initial years following the member’s death, terminal illness diagnosis or total permanent disability.
The scheme offers coverage of $70,000 until the end of the policy year in which members turn 60 years old. From the policy anniversary when they reach age 60 until the end of the policy year in which they turn 65, the sum assured reduces to $55,000.
CPF members who are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged between 21 and 65 are automatically extended a DPS cover upon a valid CPF working contribution, subject to good health.
Individuals below 21 years of age, but 16 or older, may apply for DPS coverage.
The scheme is optional and insured members may choose to terminate their coverage by submitting an opt-out form to the appointed insurer. CPF members who have previously opted out must apply for a new coverage if they wish to re-join the scheme.
DPS is currently solely administered by Great Eastern Life.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Am I covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Dependants' Protection Scheme coverage via:
- your yearly CPF Statement of Account
- the "Providing for your loved ones" dashboard by logging in with your Singpass
If you do not have a Singpass, you can apply for one at the Singpass website.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What is the purpose of the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: CPF members who are working and earning an income may have dependants who are reliant on their income. If such CPF members suddenly meet with an accident or contract a terminal illness that results in the loss of their income, the dependants who are reliant on them may be left in the lurch. The impact is greater when the member has not yet accumulated enough CPF or other savings which could be bequeathed to their dependants to tide them over the first few years of their untimely demise. Therefore, Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is useful to such working CPF members. This is also the reason why DPS coverage is automatically extended to members upon their first CPF contribution between age 21 and 65.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Who will be covered under Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
All Singaporeans and Permanent Residents between age 16 and 65 can be covered under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS).
DPS coverage is automatically extended to Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents upon a valid CPF working contribution between 21 and 65 years old.
Members aged 16 and above who were not extended a DPS cover automatically but wish to be insured can apply to join DPS with Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Is Dependants' Protection Scheme compulsory?
questions.text:
Coverage under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is not compulsory. Insured members can contact their existing insurer, Great Eastern Life or NTUC Income, to terminate their DPS cover any time by completing the opt out form.
Members should consider the benefits of DPS carefully before he/she terminates his/her DPS cover. Continuing with the DPS cover will provide some financial protection for the member’s family. If members decide to rejoin DPS in the future, they will need to submit a health declaration again and the cover will be provided subject to them being in good health then.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Who do I contact for enquiries on Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: For enquiries relating to the Dependants’ Protection Scheme, you may contact Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Do all CPF members need Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
Not all CPF members need Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS). Members should consider whether there are persons who are reliant on their current income. Some examples of members who may not need DPS include:
Those whose dependants have already grown up and become financially independent, e.g. children who reach adulthood and started working.
Those who have already built up enough CPF or private savings, as such savings could be bequeathed to their dependants directly, to tide them over the first few years of expenses in the event of an untimely death.
Those who already have their own private term or life insurance, which provides enough insurance protection and payout to tide dependants over the first few years of expenses in the event of an untimely death.
Insurance premiums, including for DPS, become more expensive with age. Should members decide that they wish to opt out of DPS, they may do so by informing Great Eastern Life to terminate their DPS cover any time by completing the opt out form. Opting out of DPS will allow such members who may not need DPS to retain more of their CPF savings for their retirement income.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I am a Singaporean or a Permanent Resident but I am not living in Singapore. What will happen to my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text: You will remain insured under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) as long as premiums are paid. DPS coverage is worldwide and a claim can be made when a member meets the claim criteria.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I am no longer a Singaporean or a Permanent Resident. What will happen to my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
Your Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage will be terminated as the scheme is only available to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
Your DPS insurer will refund any unused DPS premiums for the current policy year to your CPF account. The unused DPS premiums will be paid to you together with your CPF savings when you transfer your CPF savings to your bank account.
If you wish to find out more, please contact your DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My family member has passed on. How do I check if he was covered under the Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text:
If your family member was covered under the Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS), their coverage status will be made available for viewing by their CPF nominee(s) on the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard.
Alternatively, you may contact Great Eastern Life to verify whether your family member was covered under the DPS.
Great Eastern Life can be contacted at greateasternlife.com > Contact us.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: What do I need to do to restore my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover after I have obtained Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency again?
questions.text: You may wish to contact Great Eastern Life at greateasternlife.com > Contact us for further information regarding your eligibility to re-join the Dependants’ Protection Scheme after regaining Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Residency.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: I was issued a bonus sum assured in 2003 and/or 2005. Will it be carried over to my Dependants' Protection Scheme policy under the newly enhanced scheme?
questions.text:
CPF Board distributed surpluses in the form of bonus sum assured to the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) members insured before DPS was privatised in 2005. Members can contact their DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life to check if they qualified for the bonus sum assured previously.
To standardise the sum assured for all insured members to the new amount of $70,000 from 1 April 2021 under the newly enhanced DPS, existing members who were eligible for the bonus sum assured will receive a one-time premium rebate in lieu of the bonus sum assured. The one-time rebate has been credited into members’ CPF Ordinary Accounts in May 2021.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Can I terminate my Dependants' Protection Scheme cover?
questions.text:
Coverage under the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is not compulsory. You can terminate your DPS cover any time by completing the opt out form. Please approach your DPS insurer, Great Eastern Life for the form.
Please consider the benefits of DPS carefully before you terminate your DPS cover. Continuing with your DPS cover will provide some financial protection for your family. If you decide to join DPS again in the future, you will need to submit a health declaration again and the cover will be provided subject to you being in good health then.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) is covered by NTUC Income prior to 1 April 2021. When my DPS cover is transferred over to Great Eastern Life from 1 April 2021, do I need to declare my health?
questions.text: No, members who are already insured under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) prior to 1 April 2021 do not need to submit a new health declaration form for illnesses that developed on or after the commencement of their DPS covers under NTUC Income. Great Eastern Life is required to take over all obligations of DPS covers issued under NTUC Income. This means that Great Eastern Life will continue to cover any medical conditions that had developed on or after the commencement of members’ DPS covers under NTUC Income.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: My Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) cover was issued by NTUC Income. Will Great Eastern Life take over all obligations when my cover is transferred? What if I have developed medical conditions on or after the commencement of my cover under NTUC Incom
questions.text: Great Eastern Life is required to take over all obligations of Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) covers issued under NTUC Income. This means that Great Eastern Life will continue to cover any medical conditions that had developed on or after the commencement of members’ DPS covers under NTUC Income.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I apply to be insured under Dependants' Protection Scheme?
questions.text: You may do so by submitting your Dependants' Protection Scheme application to Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I pay my Dependants' Protection Scheme premiums?
questions.text:
The Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) premium will be automatically deducted from your CPF savings when DPS coverage is first extended to you upon a valid CPF working contribution, and subsequently on your annual policy renewal date.
If your available CPF savings are insufficient for the full sum assured
Partial premiums will be deducted from your CPF savings, and the sum assured will be reduced proportionately (minimum sum assured is $5,000). If you wish to restore to full coverage, you will be required to make a cash top-up to the appointed insurer, Great Eastern Life (GEL). Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
If your available CPF savings are insufficient for the minimum sum assured
A full cash top-up to the appointed DPS insurer, GEL, will be required. Visit GEL’s website for detailed instructions and forms.
To ensure your DPS coverage is renewed in a timely manner, you may wish to consider paying your DPS premiums in cash via GIRO. To set up GIRO payments, please refer to “How do you stay covered under DPS” on GEL’s website.
For further assistance, you may contact GEL directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants
