questions.title: Are corporate service buyers required to make MediSave contributions under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) for vendors who are both an employee and self-employed person?
questions.text:
Corporate service buyers are required to make MediSave contributions via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) for vendors who provide their services as self-employed persons, regardless of whether they are concurrently an employee.
If payment is made to the vendor’s company (which hires the vendor as an employee), CAYE is not required. The vendor will continue to receive employee CPF contributions from his/her employer.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are all corporate service buyers required to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: It is mandatory for all Government Procurement Entities (GPEs), including all Ministries, Departments, Organs of State and Statutory Boards as corporate service buyers, to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE).
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What are corporate service buyers required to do under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Under Contribute As You Earn, corporate service buyers are required to deduct and transmit a portion of the service fee to the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave account, before paying the SEP the remainder of the service fee. This is done through either the bank or online submission modes.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What are the payment modes available under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
Corporate service buyers (CSBs) can make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions via two payment modes:
PACE (PayNow for CAYE)
CSBs submit a payment file to CPF Board.
CPF Board returns an acknowledgement file to CSBs within one working day.
After CSBs process the acknowledgement file, CSBs submit a corporate payment file to OCBC via their existing bank payment service.
Once CSB’s bank transmits the gross service fee to the CAYE bank account, OCBC will pay the net service fee to the self-employed person (SEP)’s bank account via PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address), and credit the required CAYE contribution to the SEP’s MediSave Account.
Online submission mode (GIRO DDA)
CSBs will log into the CAYE Digital Services using their Corppass and key in the service fee to be paid to the SEP.
The CAYE Digital Services will indicate the CAYE contribution required for each SEP.
CSBs will only pay the CAYE contribution to SEP’s MediSave account via DDA.
CSBs will pay the net service fee to SEP’s PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) separately.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What is the deadline to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions must be paid to the self-employed person (SEP) no later than the day that the service fee was paid to the SEP. For example, if you pay your SEP vendor his net service fee on 8 March 2023, you will need to pay his CAYE contributions by 8 March 2023.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Is there a need to amend the conditions of contract for contracts signed before the inception of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: As Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is mandatory under the law, there is no need to amend the conditions of contract for contracts signed before the inception of CAYE. For new contracts signed moving forward, the Ministry of Manpower and CPF Board will work with the Ministry of Finance to inform new vendors of the CAYE requirements.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if corporate service buyers fail to pay the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers (CSBs) are required to self-rectify if any non-compliance is detected. Please refer to the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) implementation guide issued by the CPF Board. CPF Board has conducted briefings to CSBs and will work closely with CSBs to ensure full adoption and compliance of CAYE.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), corporate service buyers will only pay the net service fee directly to self-employed persons. Are there any legal implications?
questions.text:
Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), corporate service buyers (CSBs) will still be paying the full amount stated in the contract to the self-employed person (SEP), with a portion of the service fee credited to the SEP’s MediSave Account and the remainder paid to the SEP's bank account registered to PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address). CSBs would be legally obliged to participate in CAYE under the CPF Act.
For audit purposes, CSBs will be able to view the transaction details and amount of CAYE contributions made on the CAYE Digital Services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are companies who bid for jobs with corporate service buyers required to participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), even if it is operated by a single person?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn is not applicable to companies registered under the Companies Act, based on Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority’s (ACRA) definition.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Will payments to sub-contractors be under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn is not applicable to sub-contractors because they do not have a direct contractual relationship with corporate service buyer.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Which payments are under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
All tax-liable payments to freelancers and sole proprietors are under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), except this list of payments.
These requirements will be communicated to corporate service buyers (CSBs) through legislation and implementation guides.
To facilitate the implementation of CAYE, Vendors@Gov will automatically identify vendors who are under CAYE when they log in through Corppass or Singpass. These vendors will be notified of their obligation via prompts.
For invoices outside of Vendors@Gov, CSBs will need to identify self-employed persons covered under CAYE through:
the NRIC used by the vendor to transact, or
the Unique Entity Number (UEN) issued by ACRA. CSBs can use the Enterprise Data Hub (EDH) to check whether the vendor’s business entity type is a sole-proprietorship or partnership.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are directors who receive director fees covered under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: No. Under the Income Tax Act, directors of companies are considered as “employee” for income tax purposes. Directors’ fees are therefore taxable as employment income and would not be covered under Contribute As You Earn.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are small value payments exempted from Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
No, the payments from small value purchases are not exempted from Contribute As You Earn (CAYE).
However, buy-and-claim purchases are exempted from CAYE. This is because such purchases are usually for goods or services that are very small in value which the staff is prepared to pay in advance and seek reimbursement thereafter.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Which self-employed persons must participate in Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Freelancers and sole-proprietors who are Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and who have completed jobs/ projects with Government procurement entities as their service buyers, will automatically be enrolled onto Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). Self-employed persons (SEPs) who logged on to Vendors@Gov will see pop-up prompts informing them of their CAYE requirements.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How will corporate service buyers know how much Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution to deduct from the service fee?
questions.text:
The amount of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution to be deducted from the service fee depends on the self-employed person (SEP)’s CAYE contribution rate. The SEP’s CAYE contribution rate is automatically computed by the CAYE system based on the SEP’s MediSave contribution rate, estimated revenue and estimated expenses.
From 7 Jun 2024, please submit a corporate payment file to your corporate bank. Your corporate bank will then credit the total gross service fees to the CAYE bank account. OCBC will check with CPF Board’s CAYE system for the amount to be deducted and credited to the SEP’s MediSave Account (MA).
Under the online submission mode, you can key in the total service fee in the CAYE Digital Services, and the amount to be deducted and credited to the SEP’s MA would then be provided. You can then pay the MediSave contributions through the CAYE Digital Services and the service fee amount directly to the SEP.
If an SEP queries about his/her CAYE contribution amount or rate, please direct the SEP to the CAYE Digital Services for SEPs where the SEP can log in to view his transaction details.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What will be the applicable Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate used?
questions.text:
Both the bank and online submission modes will use the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution rate applicable as at the date of submission for consistency. If the self-employed person logs in to the CAYE digital services to update his CAYE contribution rate, the rate will only be effective the next day.
Corporate service buyers using the online submission mode are to log in to the CAYE digital services to compute the CAYE contributions only when they are ready to transmit the service fee.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How can corporate service buyers using the bank mode check the breakdown of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee to the self-employed person?
questions.text:
Corporate service buyers can view the status of the payment made and the amount split between the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee made to the self-employed person by:
Referring to the return file provided by the appointed bank, OCBC; or
Logging onto the CAYE online digital services with your Corppass ID and select View Transaction History > Transaction Type > Make CAYE Contributions.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Would Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) be applicable on invoices for goods provided by self-employed vendors?
questions.text: Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) will apply to all taxable revenue, including profits made on goods provided. To avoid over-collection of CAYE contributions, self-employed persons (SEPs) can log in to the CAYE digital services to adjust their estimated expenses to include the costs of goods. The SEP’s CAYE contribution rate will then be adjusted accordingly.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For GST-registered sole proprietors, are the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions computed based on the full service fee, inclusive of GST?
questions.text: Yes, Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) will apply to the full amount of the service fee inclusive of GST. To avoid over-collection, self-employed persons can include the GST as part of their estimated expenses on the CAYE digital services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), what happens if the self-employed person has contributed up to the maximum mandatory contributions for the year?
questions.text: There will be no further Contribute As You Earn deduction and the full service fee will be paid to the self-employed person.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), what happens if the self-employed person is not registered on Vendors@Gov?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers should ask the self-employed person to register at Vendors@Gov so that they are able to submit an e-invoice for the purpose of Contribute As You Earn.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Are there any changes required to the corporate service buyer's payment system/process to reconcile the payments made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
You may consider changing your payment system/ process to reconcile payments made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), if necessary.
If you’re using the online submission mode (DDA mode), you may download the CAYE payment file via the CAYE Digital Services to reconcile the payment made to the SEPs.
Generally, if you’re using PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you will receive a return file from CPFB within five working days from the Funds Deduction Date.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For corporate service buyers who currently do not have an account with OCBC, are they required to open an account with the appointed bank, OCBC, if they wish to opt for bank mode payments?
questions.text: You do not need to have a bank account with OCBC for Contribute As You Earn (CAYE). However, you'II need to obtain and complete a Host-to-Host (H2H) application form from OCBC to establish a H2H file transfer link-up with the bank.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For corporate service buyers using OCBC accounts, is there still a need to set up a Direct Debit Authorisation arrangement with OCBC to facilitate the deduction of service fee for bank mode payments?
questions.text: You’ll need to sign up for GIRO with OCBC to authorise OCBC to deduct the full service fees from your agency’s bank accounts for the purpose of Contribute As You Earn.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do corporate service buyers know if the payment to self-employed persons is successful?
questions.text:
Generally, for payment via PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you will receive a return file from CPF Board within five working days of the Fund Deduction Date indicated in your corporate payment file to the appointed bank, OCBC. This return file will indicate the amount of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions and net service fee, the payment status, and rejection reason (for any unsuccessful payment).
For payment via the online submission mode, you can log into the CAYE Digital Services to view the payment status and CAYE contributions made to the self-employed person.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under what scenarios will monies transmitted via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) bank mode be returned to the corporate service buyer?
questions.text:
An admin fee of $0.55 per transaction will be deducted from the gross service fees before the remainder is returned to the corporate service buyer if:
the self-employed person (SEP)’s bank account is closed or invalid;
the SEP’s NRIC is invalid; or
the CPF submission number in the bank file is invalid.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Would payments made via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) online submission mode be debited from the corporate service buyers' bank account?
questions.text: Yes, payments made via the Contribute As You Earn online submission mode would be debited from the corporate service buyers’ bank account via direct debit.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How do corporate service buyers identify if the vendor is under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text:
For self-employed persons (SEPs) who submit e-invoices, Vendors@Gov will automatically identify vendors covered under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) who log in through Corppass or Singpass. These vendors will be notified of CAYE via prompts. The e-invoice file format will be modified to store two additional columns, CAYE indicator and SEPs’ NRIC, which will subsequently be loaded into NFS@Gov and interfaced to agencies.
For invoices outside of Vendors@Gov, corporate service buyers (CSBs) need to identify and tag SEPs manually via:
the NRIC used by the SEP to transact; or
the Unique Entity Number (UEN) issued by ACRA. CSBs can use the Enterprise Data Hub (EDH) to check whether the vendor’s business entity type is a sole proprietorship or partnership. If it is a sole proprietorship, CAYE will apply.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Do corporate service buyers with existing CPF Submission Number (CSN) for making CPF contributions to employees need to register for a Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) CSN?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers (CSBs) with existing CPF Submission Number (CSN) are required to register for a Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) CSN for CAYE transactions. This is because the existing CSN that CSBs have is only for the purpose of making CPF contributions to employees. A CAYE CSN will enable self-employed persons (SEPs) to identify CSBs who made CAYE contributions on their behalf. The CSN for employee transactions cannot be used for CAYE transactions, and vice versa. CSBs who need to apply for a CAYE CSN may do so via CAYE digital services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Do corporate service buyers need to factor in an approving authority to ensure accuracy of records submitted under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE)?
questions.text: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), corporate service buyers are advised to factor in an approving authority within their internal processes before making payment to ensure accuracy of records submitted (i.e. no fraudulent transactions, no error in payment amount or self-employed person to be paid). Once submitted, CAYE payments are considered correctly paid.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: With the additional step to split the service fee under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), would this result in a delayed payment of service fee that may exceed the credit terms?
questions.text:
Under PACE (PayNow for CAYE), please submit the payment file to OCBC at least five working days before the service fee is due, to ensure timely payment. This is because the earliest corporate payment value date that you can select will be one working day from the date of file transmission to OCBC using FAST. Using GIRO, it will take two working days for funds to be credited to the CAYE bank account from the date of file transmission to OCBC. Thereafter, it will generally take four working days for the CAYE contribution to be deposited into the SEP’s MediSave account.
(Note: If the service fee payment to the SEP exceeds $200,000, the payment will be rejected and the full service fee payment minus $0.55 per transaction as a rejection fee will be returned to the corporate service buyer’s PayNow-registered bank account.)
Please refer to this document for the illustration of the PACE (PayNow for CAYE) process.
If you are using the online submission mode (DDA mode) to make payments, please log into the CAYE Digital Services at least four working days before the service fee is due to ensure timely payment. This is because the earliest deduction date that you can select will be two working days later (if the submission was made before 5pm). Payment to SEP will generally take up to two working days from the date of deduction.
Please refer to this document for the illustration of the digital submission mode process.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: For PACE (PayNow for CAYE) payments, when do corporate service buyers need to submit a payment file to CPF Board to make Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions by the stipulated deadline?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers using PACE (PayNow for CAYE) need to submit the payment file to CPF Board at least five working days before the service fee payment due date to ensure timely payment to the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave Account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Does CPF Board accept credit notes to offset future payments if there have been erroneous payment of Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: CPF Board does not accept credit notes for the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions. If the corporate service buyer (CSB) has made an erroneous payment, the CSB can request a refund of the CAYE contribution from CPF Board within one year from the time the contribution was credited into the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave account. The CSB will have to seek a refund of the remaining service fee made from the SEP directly and re-transmit the CAYE contributions.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What if the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution was paid in error (i.e. paid wrong amount, or paid to the wrong self-employed person)?
questions.text: Corporate service buyers (CSBs) can request a refund of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution from CPF Board within one year from the time the contribution was credited into the self-employed person’s MediSave account. After receiving a refund of the CAYE contribution paid in error, the CSB will be required to re-submit the correct CAYE contribution via the CAYE digital services.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can corporate service buyers recover the overpaid Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions due to overpayment of full service fee?
questions.text:
If there is over-payment, corporate service buyers (CSBs) can request a full refund of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions from CPF Board within one year from the time the contribution was credited into the self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave Account (MA). The CSB will have to seek a refund of the remaining service fee made from the SEP directly. After receiving a refund of the CAYE contribution paid wrongly, the CSB will be required to re-submit the correct CAYE contribution via the CAYE Digital Services.
Example:
CSB A paid Mr Tan, their SEP vendor, a service fee of $120 through the bank mode. The bank deducted and paid $12 to Mr Tan’s MA and the net service fee of $108 to Mr Tan’s bank account. However, CSB A subsequently realised that the correct service fee amount agreed upon by both parties was $100. CSB A should:
Put in a request on the CAYE digital services for a refund of the CAYE contribution ($12) by selecting the transaction that was made in error (e.g. based on Mr Tan’s NRIC and the payment reference number) and providing the relevant supporting documents.
Seek the remaining $108 from Mr Tan directly.
Submit another CAYE contribution transaction for Mr Tan based on the correct gross service fee of $100.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if payment to the self-employed person via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) bank mode is unsuccessful?
questions.text: For unsuccessful payments made via PACE (PayNow for CAYE) (e.g. due to invalid bank account number or invalid NRIC provided), the full service fee minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) will be returned to the corporate service buyer’s bank account via FAST. If the full service fee exceeds S$200,000, the payment will be rejected and the full service fee minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) will be refunded to the corporate service buyer’s bank account.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if the corporate service buyer provided an invalid NRIC for crediting of the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions?
questions.text: Under Contribute As You Earn, if the NRIC provided is invalid, you will be prompted to amend the NRIC if you are using the online submission mode. If you are using PACE (PayNow for CAYE), you’ll automatically receive a refund minus $0.55 per transaction (admin fee) for that record as a rejection fee as the bank will reject the payment.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What happens if the amount of MediSave contributions the self-employed person has made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is higher than his MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
The self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave payable for income earned in the year will be computed after the SEP has declared his actual income in the following year.
If the self-employed person (SEP) has outstanding MediSave payable from previous years, his excess CAYE contributions will be used to offset those payables1. Any excess thereafter will be refunded to him. He can also choose to retain the excess CAYE contributions in his MediSave Account (MA).
Example:
Based on his estimated income of $22,000 for 2023, Sam contributed $2,200 via CAYE. In the following year, he declared that he earned a lower Net Trade Income of $19,000 for 2023. As such, Sam’s MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $1,900. Hence, he has excess CAYE contributions of $300 for the year. Sam also has an outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022 which would be offset by the excess CAYE contributions, leaving a final excess amount of $200. This amount will be refunded to him2. He can also choose to keep this $200 in his MA.
This example is illustrated within the table below:
Estimated 2023 NTI
$22,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,200
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$19,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$1,900
Outstanding MediSave payable for 2022
$100
Amount Sam will receive as a refund
$200
(i.e. $2,200 - $1,900 - $100)
1This will take effect for CAYE contributions made from 2023. The SEP may write to us if he does not wish to use his CAYE contributions to offset his outstanding MediSave payable from previous years.
2Sam may also choose not to use his CAYE contributions to offset his outstanding MediSave payable of $100 incurred in 2022. In this case, he will be refunded $300 instead.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Under Contribute As You Earn (CAYE), what should corporate service buyers do to set-off monies from an upcoming payment?
questions.text: To set-off monies (e.g. due to over-payment, or excess non-revenue payment made earlier) from an upcoming payment, corporate service buyers (CSBs) need to make the transaction via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) online submission mode. This means that CSBs need to key in the full service fee payable to derive the MediSave payable via CAYE, and thereafter set-off any monies from the net service fee payable to the self-employed person.
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why are Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps reduced for CPF Investment Scheme funds?
questions.text: The purpose of CPF Investment Scheme is to provide alternative investment to help CPF members build up their retirement savings. As expenses of investment have a significant impact on returns, a regular review of the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps is important as high expense ratio would erode investment returns for CPF members. Where feasible, TER caps should be kept low to increase the fund’s per-unit net asset value and enable CPF members to accumulate their retirement savings faster. This is in line with the efforts by regulatory authorities in other countries to reduce the cost of funds to investors.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What actions should Fund Management Companies/insurers take if their existing CPF Investment Scheme List A funds are unable to comply with the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps?
questions.text: Fund Management Companies (FMCs)/insurers have undertaken to comply with the Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps for funds included under CPF Investment Scheme. If their List A funds are not able to comply with the new TER caps from 2016, FMCs/insurers will be required to compensate the funds for the difference between the actual expense ratios and the new TER caps. The funds would then be downgraded to List B with effect from the implementation date (see relevant reporting period, (PDF, 0.1MB)). Under List B, funds are not allowed to take in new CPF monies.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Do Fund Management Companies/insurers need to submit a new undertaking in view of the new Total Expense Ratio caps?
questions.text: There is no need to submit a new undertaking. The previous undertaking continues to be valid for existing List A funds under CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can a fund downgraded to List B resume accepting CPF monies once the fund's Total Expense Ratio meets the cap subsequently?
questions.text: The fund would be upgraded to List A, and can take in CPF monies if its audited Total Expense Ratio meets the cap subsequently.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How frequent will CPF Board assess whether a fund can or cannot take in CPF monies?
questions.text: CPF Board will assess whenever a fund’s audited financial statements become available (i.e. yearly basis for most funds). A company that wishes to have its fund assessed more frequently may submit to CPF Board the fund’s semi-annual audited financial statements according to its accounting period. The company must ensure that all subsequent published Total Expense Ratios (TERs) of its funds are also in line with the TER cap.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will a fund be excluded from CPF Investment Scheme due to not meeting the Total Expense Ratio cap subsequent to the inclusion?
questions.text: The fund will remain under CPF Investment Scheme (as List B fund) but it will not be allowed to take in CPF new monies. However, the company will have to provide the fund’s investors with options to hold, redeem or make free switches within 3 months from informing the CPF Board of not meeting Total Expense Ratio caps.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can my company apply for the new fund to be included under the CPF Investment Scheme if its last audited Total Expense Ratio (TER) does not meet the TER cap?
questions.text:
Your company can apply to include the fund under List A if it undertakes to cap the TER of the fund with effect from the date it is launched for CPF subscription. The Letter of undertaking is attached below:
FMCsInsurers
UT Inclusion of new fund under List A (PDF, 0.2MB)​ILP Inclusion of new fund under List A (PDF, 0.2MB)
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What is the relevant reporting period (of audited expense ratio) that fund managers are required to submit?
questions.text:
For existing CPF Investment Scheme funds, the new Total Expense Ratio (TER) caps will take effect from 1 Jan 2016. As such, the compliance with the new TER caps for each fund will be based on the audited report for the financial year of the fund ended in a month in 2016. The implementation date for the new TER cap for a fund will be one day after the deadline of submission of the audited report for the fund.
The Board encourages Fund Management Companies (FMCs)/Insurers to assess early whether their funds can meet the new TER caps. If their funds cannot meet the new TER caps, FMCs/Insurers should inform the Board early.
However, FMCs/Insurers must factor in the period required for settling the purchase transactions and thus the last purchase date must be at least five working days before the implementation date. This means that after the last purchase date, if a CPF member buys a fund that does not meet the TER cap, FMCs/Insurers should not channel the subscriptions into that fund. If the funds cannot meet the TER cap, FMCs/Insurers should communicate the consequence clearly to their unitholders/policyholders, before the last purchase date. Please refer to the relevant reporting period (PDF, 0.1MB) for details.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the admission criteria that fund management companies (FMCs) and insurance companies need to meet, in order to be included under CPFIS?
questions.text: Please see the admission criteria for fund management companies (FMCs) and insurance companies.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What does the Board's investment consultant look for when evaluating fund management companies (FMCs), insurance companies or their products?
questions.text: Please see the evaluation criteria provided by the Board's investment consultant.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the CPFIS admission criteria for funds?
questions.text: You can refer to para 5 for the admission criteria for funds.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: What are the benefits of Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text:
The Internet Reimbursement (IR) service allows you to easily submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements for your employees, platform workers or insureds at your convenience. Benefits of using our IR service include:
Fast service turnaround time
Accurate reimbursements
Streamlined processes
Track reimbursement status online
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: How many reimbursements can I submit via E-File at one time?
questions.text:
You can submit up to 15,000 reimbursements at a time via E-File.
Please note that all 15,000 reimbursements should be submitted in a single Excel file.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: How do I know if my reimbursement submission via E-File is successful?
questions.text:
Once your E-file reimbursement submission is successful, you will receive an acknowledgement email at the address you provided under ‘contact details’ during submission. Please note the transaction number to check the status of your submission via 'Activities' page.
Report TitleYou will typically receive the report by

Unsuccessful after deduction
Unsuccessful before deductionNext working day after submission
Please note that submissions made on weekends or Public Holidays will be processed on the following working day.

questions.title: What sources of MediSave contributions are eligible for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution?
questions.text:
MediSave contributions1 made by the taxi principal hirer to offset MediSave payable will qualify him for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution. CPF contributions received as an employee (from both employer and self) for taxi principal hirers who are concurrently employed, as well as government top-ups are excluded.
1 You may make MediSave contributions as a self-employed person via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.

questions.title: My current registered bank account with CPF Board is also my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account. Do I still need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to receive my CPF withdrawals via PayNow?
questions.text: Yes, it is necessary to do a one-time update of your registered bank account to "PayNow NRIC-linked bank account" via Account settings if you wish to receive CPF payments via PayNow. If you do not update your registered bank account to PayNow, you will receive the payments within five working days of your withdrawal application via Interbank GIRO.

questions.title: Can I update my registered bank account when I have a pending withdrawal application?
questions.text: Please do not update your registered bank account until you have received your CPF savings in your bank account to avoid any delay or disruption in receiving your payment.

questions.title: I received a Final Reminder notification regarding my outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums, will the amount payable still be increased?
questions.text:
The Final Reminder notification shows the amount of your outstanding CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums as at the date sent.
Please pay your full outstanding premiums by the deadline indicated in the notification. Otherwise, the amount payable will increase as the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will impose compounded interest of 4% and penalties of up to 17% on your outstanding premiums. To do so, please click on the link below for the payment options.
How can I view and pay my/my dependant(s)s' CareShield Life/ElderShield and MediShield Life premiums?

questions.title: Who is a platform worker?
questions.text: You are a platform worker if you have an agreement with a platform operator to provide ride-hail or delivery services in Singapore to users for the platform operator and from this, derive any payment or benefit in kind. You are also subject to the control of platform operators, such as what tasks are assigned to you and how much you are paid. You will be given an earnings slip that specifies your status as a platform worker.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators
Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Who is a platform operator?
questions.text:
Platform operators are companies that:
a. have an agreement with users to provide ride-hail or delivery services to the users;
b. use data to automate decision making relating to platform workers, in areas such as task assignment and how much platform workers are paid per task; and
c. impose rules, requirements or prohibitions on platform workers.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / Overview of CPF contributions for platform operators
Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the benefits of CPF contributions for platform workers?
questions.text:
CPF contributions for platform workers and platform operators will gradually increase over five years from 2025 to 2029 to align to those for employees and employers. This enables you to achieve the same level of housing and retirement adequacy as employees who earn the same amount.
The increased CPF contributions will be mandatory for platform workers born in or after 1995 and the CPF contributions will be allocated to all three CPF accounts – Ordinary, Special or Retirement and MediSave account. Older cohorts can choose to opt in to the increased CPF contributions. If you choose not to opt in, you will be required to continue to make MediSave contributions, and will not receive the platform operator share of CPF contributions.
To ensure a seamless process, platform operators will submit CPF contributions for all platform workers every month, by deducting your share of CPF contributions from your income as and when you earn. If you do not opt in, platform operators will deduct just the MediSave contributions as and when you earn.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What if platform operators discriminate against workers who are mandated or opt in to increased CPF contributions, such as through job allocation or incentives?
questions.text:
Due to the cohort-based approach where it is mandatory for all platform workers born in 1995 or later to make CPF contributions aligned with that of employees, an increasing proportion of platform workers will be making the increased contributions. It would be advantageous for platform operators in the long term to treat all workers fairly, regardless of whether they opt in, are in the mandatory cohort, or do not opt in.
Platform workers also have the option of switching between platform operators. It is therefore in the interest of platform operators to treat all workers fairly from the perspective of worker retention.
Tripartite partners will be including additional guidelines in the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices to provide greater clarity that intermediaries such as platform operators should not discriminate based on characteristics that are not related to the job, including when allocating work to platform workers.
Finally, Platform Work Associations will have the legal mandate to represent the interests of platform workers. If there are instances of possible discriminatory practices by any platform operator, Platform Work Associations can take this up with the relevant platform operators and, where necessary, inform MOM.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: When would my platform operator submit my CPF contributions?
questions.text: Platform operators are required to submit CPF contributions on a monthly basis. The due date for CPF contribution is on the last day of the calendar month. Enforcement action would be taken against platform operators who fail to pay by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday). This includes imposing late payment interest charged at 1.5% per month commencing from the first day after the due date.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is it mandatory for platform workers born in 1995 or later to have increased CPF contributions aligned to employees, while those born before 1995 have the option to opt in?
questions.text:
Younger platform workers have a greater need for CPF contributions because of housing needs and can benefit more from the compounding interest given their longer runway for accumulation.
Older platform workers can choose to opt in to the increased CPF contributions if they wish to, as they may have existing plans to finance housing and retirement needs.
Older platform workers who do not opt in will continue to be required to make CPF MediSave contributions, and will not receive the platform operator’s share of CPF contributions.
Platform operators will deduct the CPF contributions from platform workers’ earnings as and when they earn and transmit them to CPF Board monthly for all platform workers, including the MediSave contributions for those who do not opt in.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the contribution rates for platform workers?
questions.text:
Your CPF contribution rate depends on your earnings (for the calendar month), age and opt-in status. You can verify your CPF contribution amount using the platform workers CPF Contribution Calculator.
The CPF contribution rates for platform workers and platform operators will be gradually increased over five years, by up to 2.5%-pt per year and up to 3.5%-pt per year respectively.
The actual schedule for platform workers aged 55 to 70 will depend on progress of the increases to CPF contributions for Senior Workers.
If you are born on or after 1 Jan 1995 or have opted in, you can refer to this file.
If you are born before 1 Jan 1995 and have not opted in, you can refer to this file.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: How will platform workers’ CPF contributions be allocated to the CPF accounts?
questions.text:
If you are born on or after 1 Jan 1995 or have opted in to increased CPF contribution rates, your CPF contributions will be allocated to your Ordinary Account, Special or Retirement Account and MediSave Account. You can view the allocation rates.
If you are born before 1 Jan 1995 and have not opted in, your CPF contributions will be allocated to your MediSave Account only.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: What are the benefits if I opt in to increased CPF contributions as a platform worker?
questions.text:
By opting in, you can enjoy CPF contributions from all your platform operators. The higher CPF contributions would help boost your CPF savings and strengthen your housing and retirement adequacy.
You can receive up to 17% in monthly CPF contributions from your platform operator by 2029.
Your Ordinary Account savings can be used for your housing loan, freeing up your cash for other needs.
If you are above 65, your share of CPF contributions will decrease, but you receive higher total CPF contributions, due to the platform operator share of contributions.
The table below provides a comparison for those who have opted in and those who did not opt in.
Non-opt-in
Opt-in
Share of CPF contributions
Consist only your share of CPF contributions. There is no platform operator share of CPF contributions.
View contribution rates >
Consist of both you and your platform operators’ share of CPF contributions.
The CPF contribution rates for both will gradually increase over five years to align with those of employees and employers, reaching up to 20% and 17% respectively by 2029.
View contribution rates >
