questions.title: How much extra interest can I earn on my CPF savings?
questions.text:
To help boost retirement savings, the Government pays extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances, which is capped at $20,000 for Ordinary Account (OA). Extra interest is structured so that all CPF members benefit, and members with lower balances benefit more. The amount of extra interest paid to you would depend on your combined CPF balances and age.
If you are below 55 years old, you will earn an extra interest of 1% per annum on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances (capped at $20,000 for OA). The extra interest earned on your Special Account (SA) and MediSave Account (MA) balances will go to the respective accounts, while the extra interest earned on your OA balances will go into your SA to enhance your retirement savings.
If you are 55 years old and above, you will earn an extra interest of 2% per annum on the first $30,000 and 1% per annum on the next $30,000 of your combined CPF balances (capped at $20,000 for OA). The extra interest earned on your Retirement Account (RA) and MA balances will go to the respective accounts, while the extra interest earned on your OA balances will go into your RA to enhance your retirement savings. If you have joined the CPF LIFE scheme, the extra interest earned will be paid into your RA or accumulated with the interest earned on the CPF LIFE premiums of all CPF LIFE members.
How is my combined CPF balance computed?
Your accounts are used to compute your combined CPF balances in the following order:
- 1st: Retirement Account (RA), including any CPF LIFE premium balance
- 2nd: OA, with a cap of $20,000*
- 3rd: Special Account (SA)
- 4th: MediSave Account (MA)
*A cap of $20,000 from OA is imposed because OA savings are short-term in nature and can be withdrawn on demand for a few purposes such as housing and education.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates

questions.title: How is my CPF interest computed and credited into my accounts?
questions.text:
CPF interest is computed monthly. It is credited to your respective accounts by the following year and compounded annually.
CPF balances used for interest computation are affected by the transactions in your account. For instance, contributions (including refunds) received this month start earning interest next month. Withdrawals/deductions in this month will not earn interest from this month onwards.
There are strict procedures in place to ensure the accuracy of members’ CPF accounts and transactions (including interest payments). To further ensure that our system is sound and robust, our statutory auditor performs regular reviews of formulas and computations in our systems for accuracy, and conducts independent verifications of the transactions and account balances.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF interest rates

questions.title: Does my doctor need to complete the required Medical Assessment Report for my Home Protection Scheme claim if I already have a medical report from a previous insurance claim?
questions.text: If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient to assess your Home Protection Scheme claim and inform you accordingly.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: When do I need to submit the supporting documents (Medical Assessment Report and employment information) for Home Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text:
The medical institution that you have approached and your employer are required to submit the completed Medical Assessment Report and your employment information respectively to CPF Board within 90 days of your Home Protection Scheme claim application. We will not accept Medical Assessment Reports submitted directly by CPF members.
If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. The application form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
Please note that your application will be cancelled if we do not receive the supporting documents by the given deadline.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: How much is the outpatient deductible? Will I need to pay more out-of-pocket for outpatient consultation?
questions.text:
The outpatient deductible is set at $500 to strike a balance between ensuring that it can sieve out smaller bills meaningfully and moderate the extent to which premiums need to increase by, whilst not overly affecting affordability for patients. It applies for all admissions on or after 1 June 2026 and is fully payable by MediSave. There should generally be no increase in out-of-pocket payable as you may use MediSave to pay for the outpatient deductible.
There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: Does my doctor need to complete the required Medical Assessment Report for my Dependants' Protection Scheme claim if I already have a medical report from a previous insurance claim?
questions.text:
If you already have a Medical Assessment Report on hand, you can submit it to CPF Board through the link which will be provided after you submit an online claim form. The application form will allow you to concurrently apply for both Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS) benefits, as well as withdrawal of CPF savings. We will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
If you are claiming for DPS benefits only, you may submit the report directly to Great Eastern Life (GEL). GEL will assess whether the report you have provided is sufficient and inform you accordingly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: When do I need to submit the documents (Medical Assessment Report and employment information) to support my application for Dependants' Protection Scheme claim?
questions.text:
If you had applied for Dependants’ Protection Scheme claim through the CPF website, the medical institution that you have approached and your employer are required to submit the completed Medical Assessment Report and your employment information respectively to CPF Board within 90 days of your application. The Medical Assessment Report and employment information will be used to process claims under Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS) and Home Protection Scheme (HPS), if you have applied for both. We will not accept Medical Assessment Reports submitted directly by CPF members.
Please note that your application will be cancelled if we do not receive the supporting documents by the given deadline.
To apply for withdrawal due to Reduced Life Expectancy (RLE) only, please write to us for assistance. If you are applying for DPS benefits only, you can submit the supporting document to Great Eastern Life directly.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: How do I get a document that shows I do not have a CPF account?
questions.text:
You can login to my cpf digital services via your Singpass. You will see a message "No information can be displayed here as you do not have a CPF account."
You can click on located above the graphic, to save or print a copy.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What is my CPF account number?
questions.text:
If you are currently/were previously a Singapore Citizen or a Permanent Resident, your CPF account number is the Unique Identification Number (UIN) stated on your NRIC, Citizenship Certificate, or entry permit (e.g. S1234567F or T1234567F).
Otherwise, your CPF account number could begin with the letter ‘S’ or ‘T’, followed by the letter ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’, ‘D’ or ‘F’ (e.g. SA123456D or TC987654B).
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When do I have a CPF account?
questions.text: Your CPF account is automatically created when a first top-up or CPF contribution is received.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How do I inform CPF Board of a change in my address?
questions.text:
By default, CPF letters are sent to your residential address on your Singapore Identity Card. If you are residing at a new address and have been receiving your CPF letters at your old residential address, please apply for the change of your residential address (local or overseas) via Immigration & Checkpoints Authority’s (ICA) e-Services using your Singpass.
Participating government agencies and statutory boards (including CPF Board) will be informed of the change in address through the One-Stop Change of Address Reporting Service (OSCARS) within one day. You will not be receiving an additional acknowledgement from CPF Board for updates via OSCARS.
Please visit ICA website for more information.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When and how should I inform CPF Board about changes to my particulars?
questions.text: For Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, you do not need to inform us separately as your latest particulars will automatically be updated in our records.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How can I inform CPF Board if I changed my name?
questions.text:
We use the principal name registered in your NRIC to transact with you. Principal name usually excludes variants such as hanyu pinyin, married name and other aliases.
If you have updated your principal name registered in your NRIC recently, you do not need to inform us separately. Your name will automatically be updated in our records.
If you have not updated the name registered in your NRIC or would like to transact with us using your hanyu pinyin, married or other aliases, you will need to update your principal name in your NRIC first.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What should I do if I receive mails from CPF Board that do not belong to me and my family member(s) at our address?
questions.text: If you received mails from CPF Board that do not belong to you and your family member(s) at your address, please state the reason for return, e.g. 'no such person' or 'change of owner', and drop the mail into SingPost's "Return Mail Here" mailbox. The undelivered mail will be returned to us.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What should I do if I receive a notification that is not meant for me?
questions.text:
This could happen because:
You are sharing contact detail(s) with your next-of-kin for handling of CPF matters; or
Your contact detail is a recycled mobile number/email address registered by another member with us previously; or
You are using a common business mobile number/email address shared within a company.
If you did not intentionally share your contact details with another member or wish to stop this arrangement, please write to us with a screenshot of the notification you have received.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Would other members receive my CPF notifications if they have registered the same contact detail(s) as me?
questions.text:
Members will receive CPF notifications at their email address and/or mobile number registered with us.
Other members can receive your CPF notifications only if they share the same email address or mobile number as you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: I have reviewed my contact detail(s) and am aware that it is also registered under another family member. Can we continue to share contact detail(s)?
questions.text:
We understand that some CPF members require help from family members on their CPF matters, and could have registered the same contact details with us.
No further action is needed if your contact details are still valid.
Otherwise, you can update your new contact details via the Account settings page with your Singpass.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Do I have to provide my bank account details to CPF Board if I do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board?
questions.text:
No action is required from you if you do not intend to make any withdrawals or do not have any upcoming payments from CPF Board.
However, if you expect upcoming payments from CPF Board, e.g. monthly payouts or refunds, please provide your bank account details to CPF Board so that you can receive your payments to your registered bank account. If you are nearing age 70 and have not already started your monthly payouts, you should expect to start receiving your monthly payouts when you turn 70 years old, and will need to provide your bank account details to receive your payouts to your registered bank account.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: When do I need to update my bank account?
questions.text:
You should review and update your bank account details when there are any changes to avoid any delay or disruption in receiving your payments. If you have a pending withdrawal, consider updating your bank account after the withdrawal is complete, to enable successful processing of your withdrawal application.
Your monthly payouts and CPF savings withdrawn (see list of payments) will be paid to the bank account you have provided under your Account settings.
You can update your bank account details via my cpf digital services – Account settings with your Singpass.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Which CPF payments will I receive in the bank account provided under my Account settings?
questions.text:
The bank account provided under your Account settings will be used for CPF payments such as:
Withdrawals of CPF savings from age 55
Monthly payouts
Cash bonus received under Silver Housing Bonus scheme
Cash bonus received under Lease Buyback Scheme
Sale proceeds from Singtel SDS
Withdrawals of deceased member’s CPF savings
This does not include long-term care payouts (e.g. CareShield Life, ElderShield and MediSave Care) where application is made through the Agency for Integrated Care, and Government payments (e.g. GST Vouchers, Workfare Income Supplement and Silver Support Scheme).
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What bank accounts can I use to update my bank account details?
questions.text:
You may update your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account as your registered bank account with CPF Board to receive payments via PayNow. Once updated, you do not need to update your registered bank account with CPF Board again if you switch to another bank account for PayNow. Your CPF payments will automatically be made to whichever bank account you have linked to your PayNow-NRIC.
Alternatively, you may use any POSB, DBS, OCBC and UOB bank accounts belonging to you. As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, we only accept accounts from these banks as they provide automated bank account verification to CPF Board. This ensures that payments are only made to accounts that belong to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How long does it take to activate my bank account details?
questions.text:
As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, your new bank account will be activated after a 12-hour cooling period or verification by banks:
Bank accountActivation time
PayNow NRIC-linked bank accountAfter 12-hour cooling period
Other bank account (POSB, DBS, OCBC, UOB)After your bank confirms that the account belongs to you which generally takes up to two working days
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How can I amend my bank account details or cancel the online application while it is pending activation?
questions.text:
You are unable to amend your bank account details by submitting a new application or cancel the online application while it is pending activation. You can update your bank account details after it has been activated, which will generally take 12 hours for PayNow NRIC-linked bank accounts, and up to two working days for other bank accounts.
If the changes made to your bank account details are unauthorised, please contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately and reset your Singpass. If you are age 55 and above, you can also activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to instantly disable online withdrawal.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Why do I need to update contact details to update my bank account?
questions.text: Notifications via SMS or email will be sent to you whenever there are updates to your bank account. As such, you will have to register or update your contact details under Account settings to receive these notifications and prevent any unauthorised updates from taking effect.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: How will I be notified about the status of my update bank account application?
questions.text:
You will receive an SMS and email notification to the local mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board as well as a push notification on your CPF Mobile app upon the following:
Submission of the application to update your registered bank account
Successful update of your registered bank account
Unsuccessful update of your registered bank account
You can also check the status of your online application under Activities.
If the changes made to your registered bank account are unauthorised, please contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately and reset your Singpass. If you are age 55 and above, you can also activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to instantly disable online withdrawal.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What are the benefits of using a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account?
questions.text: PayNow NRIC-linked bank account is easy to set up as it only requires a one-time registration with your bank using your NRIC number. It also provides convenience as you can receive CPF payments in any PayNow participating local and foreign banks, without having to provide your bank account number.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: What is a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account and how do I register for it?
questions.text:
PayNow is a secure funds transfer service that enables you to receive payment conveniently in your preferred bank account with only your NRIC number. It adopts the same high security standards as other trusted funds transfer services like FAST and GIRO.
You can register for a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account if you have a bank account with the PayNow participating banks in Singapore, which can be found on the Association of Banks in Singapore's website.
If your bank is a PayNow participating bank, you may refer to your bank's website for specific details on how to link your NRIC to PayNow.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Why do I need to link my bank account to PayNow using my NRIC number?
questions.text: Unlike mobile numbers, the NRIC number is an unchanged reference number issued by the Government and is the only accepted reference number for government payments via PayNow. Linking your bank account to PayNow using your NRIC number ensures that government payments will be made correctly to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Will taxi principal hirers who participate in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme have their Taxi Driver Vocational Licence (TDVL) be automatically renewed?
questions.text:
No, Taxi Driver Vocational Licences (TDVL) will not be automatically renewed upon participation in the Drive and Save (DAS) Scheme.
Taxi principal hirers must have fully paid their MediSave payable or are making monthly payments via GIRO to renew their TDVLs.
MediSave contributions1 and co-contributions from taxi operators will offset mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: What sources of MediSave contributions are eligible for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contributions?
questions.text:
MediSave contributions1 made by the taxi principal hirer to offset MediSave payable will qualify him for Drive and Save (DAS) co-contribution. CPF contributions received as an employee (from both employer and self) for taxi principal hirers who are concurrently employed, as well as government top-ups are excluded.
1 Taxi principal hirers may make MediSave contributions as self-employed persons via Manage your MediSave payable or GIRO.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / Drive and Save Scheme

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for admission into a nursing home? How do I apply for admission to a nursing home?
questions.text:
You can find out more information on nursing home admission and how to apply for admission to a nursing home at https://www.aic.sg/care-services/nursing-home/.
You can also speak to your healthcare provider and Medical Social Worker to find out more.

questions.title: What is the cost of staying in a nursing home?
questions.text:
You can find out more information about nursing home costs at https://www.aic.sg/care-services/nursing-home/.
Subsidies and financial assistance are available for eligible nursing home residents and more information can be found on the MOH website. You can also speak to your Medical Social Worker for assistance.

questions.title: Are nursing homes held to care standards? What measures are in place to ensure the safety of nursing home residents?
questions.text:
All nursing homes are licensed under the Healthcare Services Act. MOH conducts regular checks to ensure that nursing homes meet the licensing requirements. Licensing requirements include areas such as patient care, nursing home staff, and premises, equipment and sanitation.
MOH regularly reviews and enhances the care standards in our nursing homes.

questions.title: How are Long-Term Care (LTC) services made affordable for Singapore Citizens (SCs), Permanent Residents (PRs) and Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) Holders?
questions.text:
LTC services (such as those offered at Active Ageing Centres and Senior Care Centres) are either provided free or kept affordable through Government subsidies for Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PRs). Like many other countries, Singapore carefully considers the unique aspects of citizenship and differentiates the benefits that citizens, permanent residents, and foreigners receive. While LTVP holders are not eligible for subsidies, those in need may reach out to their service provider or the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for financial assistance.
For more information on accessing LTC services, you may reach out to AIC at enquiries@aic.sg or 1800-650-6060.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for Active Ageing Centres (AACs)?
questions.text:
1. Singapore Citizens (SC) and Permanent Residents (PR) aged 60 and above, regardless of housing types and socio-economic status,
2. SC/PR spouse aged below 60 of an SC/PR senior, and
3. Non-Resident (NR) spouse of SC senior.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How much does it cost to join an Active Ageing Centre (AAC)?
questions.text: Singapore Citizens (SCs) and Permanent Residents (PR) aged 60 and above do not have to pay any fee to join an AAC.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the range of active ageing programmes available at an Active Ageing Centre (AAC)?
questions.text:
As a drop-in social recreational space for Seniors, AACs conduct a range of programmes across physical, cognitive, social, learning and volunteerism domains.
For the physical domain, AACs offer fitness and strengthening exercises such as Yoga, Qigong, and Zumba.
For the cognitive domain, Seniors can participate in mind-stimulating activities such as puzzles and mindfulness-related activities.
For the social domain, Seniors can enjoy communal meals and games such as Bingo and Rummy-O to widen their social circles.
For the learning domain, AACs offer arts & crafts workshop and talks for Seniors to pick up new knowledge.
For the volunteerism domain, AACs offer opportunities for Seniors to volunteer in delivering meals or packing of goodie bags for the less privileged.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How does Active Ageing Centres (AACs) play a part in Healthier SG?
questions.text:
As part of the Healthier SG initiative, AACs deliver the 2S (Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, and Community Screening) which aims to empower Seniors towards healthy and active lifestyles.
As a Social Connector for Social and Lifestyle Interventions, AACs assist Seniors to join relevant active ageing programmes as recommended in their Healthier SG health plan.
AACs also serve as a community node for Community Screening, such as vitals screening and functional screening.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: How do I apply for my loved ones to receive the services at Senior Care Centres (SCCs)?
questions.text: You can approach the doctor at the hospital or polyclinic for assistance to submit an online application for the service or visit an AIC Link near you.

questions.title: What are the estimated costs for the services offered at Senior Care Centres (SCCs)?
questions.text:
For Day Care, the estimated cost ranges between $945 and $1,430 a month before subsidies, assuming daily attendance on weekdays, excluding transport.
For Dementia Day Care, the estimated cost ranges between $1,260 and $1,575 per month before subsidy, assuming daily attendance on weekdays and excluding transport services.
For active rehabilitation, the estimated cost ranges between $70 and $102 per rehabilitation session before subsidy, excluding transport services.
For maintenance rehabilitation, the estimated cost ranges between $52 and $65 per rehabilitation session before subsidy, excluding transport services.
Subsidies for both services and transport are available for application. The received amount varies depending on your family’s income.
You may visit an AIC Link near you for assistance on the application process.

questions.title: What are the volunteering roles available for seniors under the Silver Generation Office? What is the difference between volunteering at Active Ageing Centres (AACs) under the Silver Guardian Programme and the Silver Generation Ambassador programmes?
questions.text:
As a Silver Generation Ambassador, you will engage seniors through home visits, also known as Preventive Health Visits (PHVs). These visits allow us to understand how the seniors are in aspects of health, financial and social, and provide seniors with relevant information of government policies, schemes, community activities and health services which may be beneficial for the seniors.
As a Silver Guardian volunteering at Active Ageing Centres, you may be assigned as an Active Ageing Programme facilitator to help co-facilitate simple exercises or arts and craft activities, or become a befriender to vulnerable seniors, monitor their wellbeing and encourage/accompany them to attend community activities. You may also be assigned other roles within the AACs based on the needs within the centre.
If you would like to hear more about the volunteering opportunities at the AACs, you may sign up for an Information Sharing session with AIC via the link: https://for.sg/volunteer-with-us-today.
For more information about the Silver Generation Ambassador programme, visit https://www.aic.sg/about-us/be-sga-volunteer/.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: Will training be provided for Silver Guardians and Silver Generation Ambassadors prior to volunteering?
questions.text:
Yes, training will be provided to equip volunteers with the necessary skills for the volunteering roles, e.g., on effective communication with seniors.
The training structures and durations vary depending on the role.
For more information about the Silver Generation Ambassador programme, visit
https://www.aic.sg/about-us/be-sga-volunteer/
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What is the Silver Volunteer Fund under the Council for Third Age?
questions.text:
The Silver Volunteer Fund (SVF) was launched in 2016 as part of the National Senior Volunteerism Movement under the first Action Plan for Successful Ageing.
In 2023, the Council for Third Age (C3A) rolled out the Enhanced Silver Volunteer Fund (ESVF) to provide funding support for volunteer host organisations to offer a diverse range of volunteering opportunities for seniors.
Volunteer host organisations can tap on the ESVF to offer training and development opportunities and increase volunteer appreciation efforts for volunteers to better retain and grow their pool of senior volunteers. The ESVF also fosters exchanges to encourage sharing of knowledge and best practices amongst volunteer host organisations.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.text: You may wish to find out more here: (Link to AIC’s website on FAQs on ACP)

questions.title: Who can apply for the Seniors' Mobility And Enabling Fund (SMF) SMF - Devices Subsidy?
questions.text:
If you are a needy Singaporean aged 60 years and above, you can apply, subject to means-testing and needs assessment.
You must not be concurrently receiving (or apply for) any other public or private grants/subsidies that exceed the amount of co-payment should you get SMF subsidies for the device(s) you are applying for.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: How will seniors or Persons with Disabilities know if they are eligible for SMF or Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)?
questions.text:
Seniors and Persons with Disabilities will be served under one scheme throughout their lifetime. If the individual has tapped on ATF1 before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime. On the other hand, if the individual has not tapped on ATF1 subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime.
Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organizations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes. They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) or SG Enable (SGE) for assistance.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies
1 The ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living.

questions.title: What type of means testing will be done for SMF?
questions.text:
Means-testing will be conducted based on MOH’s SMF Device or Consumables Subsidy framework. To qualify for SMF subsidies, your household monthly income per person should be $2,000 and below OR Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC should be $21,000 and below for households with no income.

questions.title: What is the list of Assistive Devices covered under SMF - Devices Subsidy?
questions.text:

Walking aids
Basic wheelchair / pushchair
Motorised wheelchair / scooter
Pressure relief cushion
Pressure relief mattress
Commode / shower chair
Geriatric chair

Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Who can apply for the SMF - Consumables Subsidy?
questions.text:
If you are a needy Singaporean aged 60 years and above, you can apply, subject to means-testing and needs assessment.
You must be receiving one of the following services: Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, Day Hospice, Integrated Home & Day Care (IHDC) services.

Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: What consumables are covered under SMF?

Catheters and catheter set
Milk feeds

questions.title: What are the enhancements to Caregivers Training Grant (CTG) from 1 April 2024?
questions.text:
From 1 April 2024, eligible beneficiaries will start off with an initial grant of $400. Each year, there will be a top up to care recipients’ CTG by $200, and unused monies can be carried forward, with the CTG monies for each care recipient capped at $400 per year.
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Are Migrant Domestic Workers (MDW) eligible for the grant?
questions.text:

Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: How do eligible caregivers receive the grant?

questions.title: If there is more than one caregiver taking care of the same person, are they all eligible for the grant?
questions.text:
Yes, different caregivers of the same care recipient may utilise the grant to subsidise the caregiving training, up to the grant amount that each care recipient is eligible for per Financial Year.

Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Can more than one caregiver tap on the grant to attend the same training programme?
questions.text:
Yes. More than one caregiver of each care recipient can attend the same training and will be reimbursed only up to the grant amount care recipient receives per financial year, in the form of training subsidies.

questions.title: Can I attend any training programmes that I think are useful?
questions.text: No; however, to tap on CTG for training fee subsidy, caregivers may choose from a list of more than 150 training programmes that have been pre-approved. The list of pre-approved training programmes can be found here.

questions.title: I did not use my grant monies this year. Can I carry it forward next year?

questions.title: Can I apply for Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) if my loved one is unable to provide consent for the application due to e.g. lack of mental capacity or below 21 years old?
questions.text:
Yes.
For care recipient who lacks mental capacity
Care recipent’s donee/deputy# may provide consent on the care recipient’s behalf. If the care recipient does not have such a donee/deputy, the caregiver* may make the application on care recipient’s behalf.
# Donee/deputy must be appointed in accordance with the Mental Capacity Act (Cap 177) and is authorised to make decisions on behalf of the care recipient in relation to the care recipient’s property and affairs.
* For successful applications without a donee/deputy, the caregiver or another family member has 12 months to obtain a court order appointing him/her as a deputy, failing which the payouts will be suspended. For more information on how to apply for a deputyship, please visit SG Courts Website.
Doctor’s certification for mental incapacity is only valid for six months, unless stated permanent.
You will also need to submit the following additional supporting documents:
Doctor’s certification that the care recipient lacks mental capacity OR court order of deputy appointment OR recent medical report stating that the care recipient lacks mental capacity; and
Copy of bank book or statement IF you are nominating an account belonging to a deputy or trustee of the care recipient.
For care recipient below age of 21 years old
The care recipient’s parent or legal guardian^ may make this application on behalf of the care recipient.
^ Legal guardian refers to a person who has been lawfully appointed in accordance with the Guardianship of Infants Act (Cap. 122).
You may wish to find out more here:
Caregiver Grants & Subsidies

questions.title: Why are individuals who own multiple properties and PCHI ≤ $1,500 ineligible for the Home Caregiving Grant’s (HCG) $400 payout and eligible only for the $250 payout?

questions.title: What types of properties are considered for the multiple property ownership criterion for determining which Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) tier an individual is eligible for (i.e. $250 or $400 payout)?

questions.title: How do I apply home care services for my loved to support their care at home?
questions.text: Seniors who require the services can visit an AIC Link located in the restructured hospital near you or call the AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060 for assistance.

questions.title: How much out-of-pocket fees do I need to pay for the home care services?
questions.text: The out-of-pocket fees that you need to pay will depend on the type of home care service you require. Eligible seniors can receive subsidies of up to 80%, based on the non-residential Long-Term Care subsidy framework. You may approach an AIC Link or call the AIC hotline at 1800-650-6060 for more details.

questions.title: What is the eligibility criteria for the Community Care Apartments?
questions.text:
Conditions
Age
Applicant(s) and their spouse (if any) must be 65 years old and above.
Income Ceiling
The average gross monthly household income cannot exceed $14,000.
Family Nucleus and Citizenship
Available to:
Families with at least 1 Singapore citizen applicant and
Singles who are Singapore citizens.
Property Ownership
Applicant(s) or any person listed in the HFE letter application aged 65 and above who owns any private residential property or an HDB flat must dispose of the property within 6 months from collecting keys to the Community Care Apartment (CCA). If they own not more than one non-residential property, they do not need to dispose of the property.
Previous Purchase
Those who have enjoyed two or more housing subsidies before, one of which was a Studio Apartment or short-lease 2-room Flexi flat or CCA, are not eligible.
Lease Length
The lease chosen must be able to cover all applicants and their spouse (if any) till at least 95 years old. Options range from 15 to 35 years (in 5-year increments).
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: Which group of seniors are suitable for the CCA?
questions.text:
CCAs cater to healthier seniors, as well as those with some care needs. Healthier seniors can be supported to keep well and stay active for as long as they can. As care needs increase, residents will not need to struggle with navigating care options as the appointed CCA operator will take care of their needs where possible, and facilitate their access to other care services as needed.
However, seniors who have a high level of care or nursing needs, or who have been diagnosed with severe mental illness and/or loss of mental capacity that require intensive support, may not be suitably cared for within the CCA.
topics: Ageing Well / Ageing in the Community

questions.title: What are the payment modes for the Basic Service Package?

For the Basic Service Package, you can choose between 2 regular payment plans of either:
a. Payment due every month, plus a 1-year security deposit at the start of the lease; OR
b. Payment due every 3 years.
Payment for the Basic Service Package can be done by cashier’s order, GIRO, or bank transfer.

questions.title: How is the scope of benefits determined? What other treatments have been considered for coverage under MediShield Life?
questions.text: The MediShield Life Council has assessed the scope of benefits and new areas to be covered by MediShield Life, taking in proposals from various stakeholders. Treatments which are recommended for MediShield Life coverage have been prioritised based on suitability for risk-pooling, clinical- and cost-effectiveness, having significant affordability gaps, and/or potential to encourage patients to receive care in appropriate settings.
