questions.title: How do I claim from MediShield Life?
questions.text:
The medical institution will ask if you wish to make a claim and request for your authorisation to submit the claim to MediShield Life and your Integrated Shield Plan insurer (if any) on your behalf. If a payout is due, it will be made to the medical institution directly to offset your bill. The remaining balance can be paid by MediSave and/or cash.
To estimate the maximum amount that you can claim from MediSave or MediShield Life, click here
(https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/calculators/medisave-medishield-life-claims)
The list of medical institutions participating in MediShield Life is available here.
https://www.cpf.gov.sg/content/dam/web/member/healthcare/documents/MSH_MedicalInstitutions.pdf
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: With the availability of the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements, will I still receive hardcopy statements?
questions.text:
You will not receive a hardcopy statement when deductions are made from your MediSave Account to pay for your dependents or your own medical bills. Instead, you will be informed of any deductions via one of the following mobile notifications:
a. If you have the Singpass Mobile App, you will be notified via the Singpass Mobile App Inbox;
b. If you do not have the Singpass Mobile App, but have registered your mobile number with Singpass, you will be notified via SMS.
If you still prefer to receive a hardcopy of your MediSave transaction statement, please write to us. If you do not have a Singpass account and or a registered mobile number, you will continue to receive the hardcopy MediSave transaction statement. No further action is required.
If your claim was only for MediShield Life and there was no deduction made from your MediSave account for the claim, you will not receive a hardcopy statement. For these cases, you will be able to access the claim details from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements.
If you would like to have the claim statements but are unable to log in online, you may approach our customer service officers over the counter or contact us at 1800 222 3399 for assistance.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What is the pro-ration factor? How does it affect my claim?
questions.text: As private hospital bills and Ward A/B1 bills in public hospitals are generally higher than the Ward B2/C bills that MediShield Life is designed for, they are pro-rated to the equivalent level of a Ward B2/C bill before MediShield Life payouts are computed. This ensures comparable payouts for subsidised and private patients.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: How do I view details of my MediShield Life claims from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You can view the details of your MediSave withdrawals and MediShield Life claim details for past 15 months online at www.cpf.gov.sg under "Latest healthcare payments and claims".
Following are the steps to take:
(1) Login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
(2) Proceed to “Latest healthcare payments and claims”
(3) Click on “View past 15 months”
(4) Select the hospitalisation period
(5) Click on the amount at MediSave Payment or MediShield Life/Integrated Shield Plan Payment to view the claim details.
If you would like to view the details of claims prior to the past 15 months, please submit a request to the Central Provident Fund Board via www.cpf.gov.sg/eSvc/Web/FeedbackSubscription/Index .
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will I be able to view claim details of my dependant(s) from the online MediSave and/or MediShield Life Claim Statements?
questions.text:
You will be able to view claim details of your dependant(s) if
(i) You are the MediSave payer for your dependant’s hospitalisation; or
(ii) You are the MediShield Life premium payer for the dependant who is less than 16 years old.
If your dependants are 16 years old and above, they may apply for SingPass here and login to view their own healthcare payment details.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: Will my hospitalisation claims still be processed after renouncement or citizenship or permanent resident status?
questions.text:
If you are insured by MediShield Life only, you can claim for medical treatments consumed prior to the renouncement date of your citizenship.
Please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options, and on the processing of your claims under your Integrated Shield Plan.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: I am covered by Employer Medical Benefits. Can I claim from MediShield Life as well? Who pays first?
questions.text:
For members who are covered under multiple schemes, the Ministry of Health has set out the following claims protocol to avoid duplicative payouts:
1. Employer, private insurance, other third party pays first
2. Followed by MediShield Life (MSHL)/Integrated Shield Plan (IP)
3. Then MediSave
4. Then Cash
MSHL/IP will pay for the portion of the bill that is not covered by employer, private insurance and other third-party payers, subject to claim limits, deductible and co-insurance. If you have filed a claim under MSHL/IP first and subsequently with a third-party payer, you or the third party payer must reimburse the relevant amount to MSHL/IP, in line with the claims protocol. The public/private healthcare institutions and the insurance industry have been informed of this claims protocol.
topics: MediShield Life / Claims Under Medishield Life

questions.title: What are the different types of Government subsidies to help Singaporeans with their MediShield Life premiums? Who is eligible for them?
questions.text:
The Government provides the following premium subsidies and support to keep premiums affordable.
Premium Subsidies (up to 60%) for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents with household monthly income per person of $3,600 and below and living in residences with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below. Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible. Permanent Residents (PRs) will receive half the applicable Singapore Citizens (SCs) rate.
Additional Merdeka Generation (MG) Subsidies of up to 10% for all MGs, on top of above premium subsidies.
Special Pioneer Generation (PG) Subsidies of up to 60% for all PG seniors, regardless of income of Annual Value of property. PGs will also receive lifetime annual MediSave top-ups of $300 - $1,200 a year, which can be used to pay premiums. With this, PGs born in 1934 and earlier will have premiums fully covered by the government, while younger PGs will have about two-thirds of premiums covered. Older PGs (born in 1939 and earlier) who have serious pre-existing conditions will also receive an additional one-off annual MediSave top-up of $50-$200 for five years, from 2021 to 2025.
Additional Premium Support is available for needy Singaporeans who cannot afford their premiums even after the above subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.

questions.title: The majority of Singapore Residents are covered under Integrated Shield Plans. Are they eligible for subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes, Singapore Residents covered under Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) will also receive the applicable subsidies for MediShield Life premiums if they meet the eligibility criteria.
IPs are made up of 2 components: (i) the MediShield Life component and (ii) the additional private insurance component providing additional coverage intended to cover unsubsidised bills, such as those incurred from Ward A/B1 stays in public hospitals or private hospital stays.
Subsidies for those who are insured under IPs will be applied only on the MediShield Life component of the IP premiums.

questions.title: Will I receive premium subsidies even if I am not the one paying for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text: You will be able to receive subsidies if you meet the eligibility criteria, regardless of who is paying for your premiums.

questions.title: I am a Pioneer Generation member. How much subsidies do I receive for my MediShield Life premium?
questions.text:
All Pioneer Generation seniors receive special Pioneer Generation Subsidies of 40% to 60%, regardless of income or Annual Value of property. PGs also receive lifetime annual MediSave top-ups of $300 - $1,200 a year, which can be used to pay premiums. With this, PGs born in 1934 and earlier have premiums fully covered by the government, while younger PGs will have about two-thirds of premiums covered. Older PGs (born in 1939 and earlier) who have serious pre-existing conditions also receive an additional one-off annual MediSave top-up of $50-$200, from 2021 to 2025.
PGs who are unable to pay their remaining share of premiums even after the Pioneer Generation Subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support, which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years. No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: How does the Government help those who cannot afford their MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
All Singapore Residents will remain covered under MediShield Life and no one will lose coverage due to an inability to pay premiums. The Government provides Singaporeans with premium subsidies and support, such as Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income, special Pioneer Generation subsidies, additional Merdeka Generation subsidies, and MediSave top-ups.
Policyholders who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support , which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years.
From 1 April 2025, enhancements will be made to several of these premium support measures to cushion the impact of premium increases. Please refer to press release for more details.

questions.title: If I am eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, does this apply for the rest of my life?
questions.text: Your eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies is subject to your household monthly income per person, Annual Value (AV) of residence, multiple property ownership and citizenship. All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are generally means-tested once a year, and will continue to receive MediShield Life Premium Subsidies as long as one continues to meet the eligibility criteria. Premium Subsidies are provided to help the lower- to middle-income households with their MediShield Life premiums. Pioneer Generation subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies are applicable for life, regardless of income or place of residence.

questions.title: To receive Premium Subsidies, why is the household monthly income per person criteria set at $3,600 (Applicable for Renewals From 1 October 2024)? Does this mean if I earn above $3,600, I am considered high income and cannot receive any Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The $3,600 figure refers to the household monthly income per person, which is based on the total income earned by a family staying in the same residential address, divided by the number of members of that family.
So, if the total income earned by family members is $14,000, and there are four members in the family, then the household monthly income per person is $3,500, and the family would qualify for subsidies.
This is a fairer way of calculating the need for subsidies, because a family with more members may need more support, even if the total income they make is quite high.
Families in a lower household income category will get a higher subsidy rate. In this way, more help is given to those who have less resources, in line with being a compassionate and inclusive society.

questions.title: The use of Annual Value / Multiple Property Ownership as an assessment criterion for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies will overlook ‘asset-rich, cash-poor’ citizens. Is there any flexibility that can be extended to these citizens if they face difficulty with their premiums?
questions.text:
In general, Government subsidies are targeted at those in greater need. The assessment approach for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies uses the household monthly income per person and Annual Value (AV) of homes as a way to assess the household’s means and better target these subsidies. In addition, those who own multiple properties will not be eligible for Premium Subsidies.
The household assessment process strikes a balance between being more precise in assessing applicants’ means and keeping the process simpler for applicants and administratively practical. While the approach is not perfect, it provides us with a fair and objective basis to take a person's income and wealth into consideration.
Policyholders who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support, which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years. In the event of extenuating circumstances, appeals will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

questions.title: Do the Premium Subsidies differ for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents?
questions.text: Permanent Residents receive half of the subsidy rates applicable to Singapore Citizens.

questions.title: Where can I check my MediShield Life / Integrated Shield Plan premium and subsidies?
questions.text: Information on your MediShield Life premium and applicable subsidies will be sent in writing to the payer of your premium about 1-2 months before your policy renewal date, by the Central Provident Fund Board or your Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurer (if you are insured under an IP).

questions.title: How were the MediShield Life premium subsidies in my Premium Notice Letter (PNL) determined?
questions.text:
The different types of subsidies are as follows:
(a) Premium Subsidies for lower- to middle-income Singapore Residents. Eligibility for this subsidy will be subject to criteria such as household monthly income per person, Annual Value of residence and multiple property ownership.
(b) Special Pioneer Generation (PG) Subsidies for all PGs ranging from 40% - 60%.
(c) Additional Merdeka Generation (MG) Subsidies for all MGs, of 5% for those age 75 and below, increasing to 10% from 76 years old and above.
You may refer to the information booklet by using this link (medishieldlife.sg/infobooklet) for the computation of the various subsidies.

questions.title: If I have appealed for higher subsidies or against the Additional Premium imposed, how will I know if my appeal is successful? Will this be reflected in my Premium Notice Letter?
questions.text:
The premium and subsidies information reflected in your Premium Notice Letter is only accurate as of the date stated in the letter.
If you have appealed, you will receive a letter informing you of the outcome of your appeal.
If there are changes to the premium payable for MediShield Life premiums arising from the change in your subsidy status, you will receive a follow-up letter informing you about the change in premiums.
To check on the status of your appeal, you can write to us (medishieldlife.sg/writetous) or call the MediShield Life hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: Why did I not receive any premium rebates?
questions.text:
Under MediShield Life, Singapore Residents pay more premiums while they are working, and in return enjoy premium rebates during their older ages. The additional amounts paid during working age are set aside in the MediShield Life Fund, to provide for future premium rebates which will help to moderate premium increases experienced at older ages.
For policyholders born before 1950 and have been insured continuously under the scheme, they will receive premium rebates from age 71 to 90 (based on age next birthday). For policyholders born in or after 1950, they will receive premium rebates from age 66 to 90 (based on age next birthday).
Please click here (www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-premiums-and-subsidies/premium-rebates) for more information on premium rebates.
From 1 April 2025, changes will be made to the indicative premium rebates for policyholders born in or after 1950. Please refer to the MediShield Life 2024 Review press release for more details.

questions.title: Why is the private insurer writing to me about MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) are made up of 2 components – (i) the MediShield Life component administered by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and (ii) the additional private insurance component, which is managed by private insurers.
Your private insurer is writing to you about the MediShield Life component of your IP as they act as a single point-of-contact and take care of all communications with IP policyholders.

questions.title: How do I pay the MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums can be paid for by MediSave and are automatically deducted from the MediSave accounts of members. If there are insufficient monies in your MediSave account, other payment options for MediShield Life premiums include:
A family member performing a "Change of Payer for MediShield Life Cover" (cpf.gov.sg/changepayer) request to take over the premium payment using his/her MediSave.
Voluntary top-up to your or the premium payer’s MediSave Account (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/top-up-medisave-account) .
You can view the premium deduction in your Transaction history at the CPF website.
For further assistance, please contact us at 1800 222 3399 or email us by using this link (www.medishieldlife.sg/writetous).

questions.title: If there are insufficient funds in my MediSave account, can I use my Ordinary Account/Special Account monies to pay for my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The savings in a member's various CPF accounts are for specific uses. Savings in the Ordinary Account and Special Account are primarily for housing and retirement while the savings in the MediSave Account are for payment of MediShield Life premium and medical expenses.
Generally, funds in the accounts are not inter-transferable. Therefore, it is not possible for your Ordinary Account/Special Account to be used for payment of MediShield Life premiums.

questions.title: How do I make payment for my MediShield Life if I am overseas and who should I contact to verify that my payment has been received?
questions.text:
For more information on payment matters for overseas members, please click here.
If you require further assistance, you may contact us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65-6222-3399 from overseas), Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm or write to us.

questions.title: How often do I have to pay MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are the payer of your/your dependants’ MediShield Life premiums, the premiums will be collected annually from your MediSave Account.
You will be notified on the net premium payable and applicable subsidies via the Premium Notice Letter that will be sent about 1 to 2 months before the renewal of your MediShield Life cover.

questions.title: What if I am unable to pay for my MediShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
There are various Government subsidies available to help Singaporeans with their MediShield Life premiums. In addition, there is Additional Premium Support (APS) to help those who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and if they have limited family support.
The Government will send them application forms to apply for APS, and reach out to them to help them with the process if they are unable to make the applications by themselves.

questions.title: Can I opt out from MediShield Life and premium payment?
questions.text: MediShield Life is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life ensures that all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will have assurance against large healthcare bills. This is in line with our move towards a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility.

questions.title: I am a foreigner currently covered under MediShield Life. How can I pay for my MediShield Life Premiums if my CPF Account is closed?
questions.text:
When MediShield was replaced by MediShield Life, the Government had given concession to a small number of foreigners with MediShield cover to continue their coverage under MediShield Life.
With the closure of CPF accounts for all foreigners on 1 April 2024, foreigners covered under MediShield Life would need to pay by alternative means aside from their MediSave. For more information on how to change your payment mode, please write to us. If no alternative arrangements are made to continue paying premiums, the MediShield Life cover will be terminated without refund of past premiums paid.

questions.title: Can I help my family members pay for their MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
Spouses, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren who have sufficient MediSave balances may help their insured family members pay their MediShield Life premiums.
Other family members like uncles, aunts, and in-laws may only help pay the premiums for the insured, if the insured’s spouse, parents, children, siblings or grandchildren do not have sufficient MediSave funds to pay for the insured’s MediShield Life premiums.
You can help your family members pay their premiums using your MediSave by submitting a Change of Payer Request (cpf.gov.sg/changepayer).

questions.title: How was I identified to pay my family member’s MediShield Life premiums? On what authority does the Board automatically deduct my MediSave to pay for my family member’s MediShield Life premiums? Can I stop this payment arrangement?
questions.text:
You have been identified as the premium payer as you are the insured’s family member and have previously used your MediSave to pay the insured’s medical expenses or other health insurance premiums.
This option encourages family responsibility by notifying family members that they can use their MediSave to help a family member who has insufficient MediSave to pay MediShield Life premiums. This also makes it convenient for the majority of members who wish to help their family members pay their premiums.
This process to facilitate the payment of an insured family member’s MediShield Life premium is authorised under regulation 10(7)(b) of the MediShield Life Regulations 2015.
Family members identified as potential payers have about one month to consider whether to proceed with this payment arrangement, before premium deduction takes place. To date, the majority of family members approached have continued with this arrangement while allowing a small number of individuals who decline to stop premium payment.
You may stop this payment arrangement by completing the “Stop Premium Payment for Dependant(s)’ MediShield Life Cover” via cpf.gov.sg/changepayer or call us at 1800-222-3399. Once you have indicated your intent, future MediShield Life premiums for the insured family member will not be deducted from your MediSave Account.
Should you subsequently change your mind and wish to take over paying the insured’s premiums after all, you will need to submit a "Change of Payer for MediShield Life Cover" application via cpf.gov.sg/changepayer.

questions.title: Can I stop paying premiums for my child?
questions.text:
If your child is below 21 years old, you are legally responsible for your child’s premium payment. You may change payer to your child, if he or she has sufficient balance in his/her MediSave Account e.g. if your child is a Singaporean who has received MediSave Grant for Newborns or if your child has working contributions.
Otherwise, Section 4(1) of MediShield Life Act requires parents to pay their child’s premiums until their child is 21 years old. If you have valid reasons to stop paying premiums for your child, for example you have been discharged from liability to maintain the child after divorce, please write to us (www.medishieldlife.sg/writetous) and attach the relevant court documents to support your case.

questions.title: How do I appeal for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: You can submit your request through the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/) or call our MediShield Life hotline at 1800-222-3399. Do note that supporting documents will be requested for assessment.

questions.title: Will overseas Singaporeans receive Premium Subsidies?
What should I do if one of my household members has disallowed access to his means information for the purpose of means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
If one of your household members has decided not to allow access to his/her means information for means-testing for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life assistance measures, we will not be able to calculate the household's eligibility for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies. As such, we are unable to extend any MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies and any applicable assistance measures to all members of your household.
Please discuss with your household member if you have concerns regarding his or her disclosure status. If your household member now wishes to allow access to his means information, please call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 or visit the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/) and click “login to access the MediShield Life e-Service”.

questions.title: I am applying for subsidy from another healthcare scheme, but was directed to approach MediShield Life. What can I do to have my means-test result reassessed so that I can be eligible for higher subsidy?
questions.text: To reassess your household and/or means information for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies and/or other selected healthcare schemes, please submit your request via the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/). We will contact you if we require further clarification on your request. Alternatively, you may wish to call the hotline at 1800-222-3399.

questions.title: How long will it take for my appeal request to be completed?
questions.text: In general, the time taken to review your request would be 20 working days upon receiving the full set of supporting documents (if any). For complex cases, more time would be required. An update would be provided to you via the MediShield Life letter sent to your email or NRIC address.

questions.title: Why did I receive a MediShield Life letter when I have applied to review my means-test result for other healthcare schemes?
questions.text:
Other healthcare schemes may use MediShield Life means information to determine your eligibility for their schemes. Upon the completion of the review, a MediShield Life letter sent to your email or NRIC address would be provided as an update to your request.
You may also visit https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/ and log in with your SingPass to check on updates to your latest household and means information. MediShield Life means information includes Annual Value (AV) of the Property, Household Monthly Income Per Person and Multiple Property Ownership.
Based on the MediShield Life means information, you may visit https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies for more information regarding other healthcare schemes and their eligibility criteria/corresponding subsidy framework.

questions.title: The review of my eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies has been completed. Will the updated subsidies be automatically applied to my latest MediShield Life policy or at public healthcare institutions?
questions.text:
The updated Premium Subsidies (if any) will be applied at your next policy renewal date, after the completion of your latest MediShield Life Premium Subsidies’ review. To see your MediShield Life premiums and policy details, please refer to the CPFB’s Healthcare Dashboard.
For more information on other healthcare schemes’ subsidies, please contact your service provider for further advice on this matter, or visit this link.

questions.title: How can I tell if I am eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies upon the completion of the means test review / How much are my premiums after the premium subsidies?
questions.text:
You may visit https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/ and log in with your SingPass to check on updates to your latest household and means information. MediShield Life means information includes Annual Value (AV) of the Property, Household Monthly Income Per Person and Multiple Property Ownership.
To determine the subsidies granted to you and your family based on your respective age groups, please refer to the MOH website. Please note that the revised subsidy will apply upon the next policy renewal.
To see your MediShield Life premiums and policy details, please refer to the CPFB’s Healthcare Dashboard.

questions.title: I would like to check my latest subsidy eligibility for other healthcare schemes. How can I do so?
questions.text:
Please contact your service provider to find out more information on your current or latest subsidy eligibility.
For more information on other healthcare schemes, their eligibility criteria and corresponding subsidy framework, please visit https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies.

questions.title: I have completed the review of my means-test eligibility under MediShield Life and would like to appeal for higher subsidies for other heathcare schemes. How can I do so?
questions.text: Please contact your service provider for further advice.

questions.title: When should I review and update my household information?
questions.text:
You should review and update your household information whenever there are changes to your household (e.g. when you/your household member(s) move house and updated the NRIC address, or when there are new additions to your household).
Please submit the changes via the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg) and click “Login to access the MediShield Life e-Service”. Alternatively, you can call 1800-222-3399.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: Who should be considered as a member of my household? What is the definition of a household?
questions.text:
Only family members related by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption, (e.g. spouse, parents, children, grandparents, grandchildren, siblings, uncles, aunts, cousins and in-laws) and who live at the same residence are considered members of your household.
Domestic helpers, unrelated landlord/tenants, fiancé/fiancee, future in-laws, godparents and friends living at the same address are not considered members of your household. Family members not living at your address are not considered members of your household for the purposes of means-testing.
To view or update the household information used to compute your Premium Subsidies, log in to the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/).
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am or my household is overseas but have a local NRIC address, should I inform Ministry of Health?
questions.text:
The Ministry of Health (MOH) will assess you and your household members' subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life Premium Subsidies based on your residential address as reflected on your NRIC.
Please note that if you/your household member has confirmed with MOH as being overseas, MOH will not be able to automatically determine your/your household member’s eligibility for the Premium Subsidies under MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life, as they do not have the relevant information about the Annual Value (AV) of your overseas residence and income abroad. Overseas Singaporeans could submit sufficient documentation to MOH to assess their eligibility for the Premium Subsidies prior to the applicable policy year. Please submit your request through this online form or call our hotline at 1800-222-3399 if calling from Singapore / +65 6222 3399 if calling from overseas for more information.
If you / your family member is overseas for studies or will be returning soon, you may wish to retain him as part of your household. There is no need to inform MOH that you / your family member is overseas.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: What is the means information that the Government will be accessing for means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The means information that the Ministry of Health (MOH) will access for means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies refers to income and property ownership only. MOH does not have access to other types of means information such as bank balances.
If you do not wish to allow MOH to access your means information, you may register your preference through the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/). However, MOH will then not be able to assess your entire household’s subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies and all members in your household will not receive any MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. You will still qualify Pioneer Generation or Merdeka Generation Subsidies if you are a Pioneer or Merdeka Generation senior.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: How will the household monthly income per person be computed?
questions.text:
In general, annual income from work from all household members will be used.
For those who are salaried employees, their income will be based on either:
a) the average monthly income over the last available 12-month period, including bonuses, as derived by the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board ; or
b) the average monthly income from work (sum of net employment income and annual trade income before losses brought forward) assessed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for the latest available assessment year.
For those who are self-employed, their income will be based on either:
a) the average monthly income from work (sum of net employment income and annual trade income before losses brought forward) assessed by IRAS for the latest available assessment year; or
b) the income declared to the CPF Board or the income assumed under the CPF Legislation within the last year.
Should there be a change in your income or employment status, you may be required to submit supporting documents to reflect this change at a later date.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: Would changes to my income be taken into consideration immediately for means-testing?
questions.text:
Your income will only be assessed when your subsidy eligibility is due for an update. This will happen nearing the end of the 1 year validity period, and will take into account the latest available 12 months information based on Government records.
If there are changes to your household financial circumstances that you would want us to use before your subsidy eligibility is due for an update, please submit your request through the MediShield Life e-Service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg) for a re-assessment of your household’s subsidy eligibility.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: How do I find out what is the Annual Value of my Property?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) of HDB properties generally falls below $21,000, while some lower-value private properties have AV between $21,000 and $31,000.
You can find out about the AV of your residence from IRAS e-Valuation List at a nominal fee. You may also check your property tax bill or log in to myTax.iras.gov.sg.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am living at Property A (which I do not own), but I own Property B. Would I still be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: The Annual Value of the address on your NRIC will be used for the eligibility checks for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: What types of properties are considered for the multiple property ownership criterion for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: All types of properties, e.g., HDB flat, private residential property and non-residential property, are taken into account in determining the subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am living in Property A and have my registered address on my NRIC here. However, I own Property B too. Which Property address will be used for means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) of the address on your NRIC will be used. In this example, AV of Property A will be used for the eligibility checks for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.
Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who own two or more properties will not be eligible for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies. Other members of their households (who are not multiple property owners) will still be assessed for their eligibility for subsidies.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: What is the validity period for my subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text: In general, your subsidy eligibility will be valid for one year. Your subsidy eligibility may be updated when there are changes to your household information, such as a new-born in your household or when you apply for / renew your status under other healthcare subsidy schemes such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS).

questions.title: I have received a letter from CPF Board/private insurer stating that “The Government is unable to determine the Insured’s eligibility for Premium Subsidies due to incomplete information” and I am currently residing overseas. What information should I provide to review my eligibility for Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
To be eligible for Premium Subsidies, all of the following criteria must be fulfilled:
Household average monthly income per person of $3,600 and below
Living in residences with an Annual Value of $31,000 and below
Individuals who own multiple properties will not be eligible
Should you wish to proceed with the review, please ensure that your NRIC address is updated to your overseas residential address. As you are currently residing overseas, the Government will not be able to automatically determine your eligibility without the relevant supporting documents. In general, the following contains the list of documents required to facilitate the review based on your living and financial circumstances abroad:
Overseas identification documents
Declaration of household member staying at the overseas address
Latest pay slips (for the past 12 months)
Property tax document, property valuation document OR Sales and Purchase Agreement (dated not more than 5 years ago) if you own your place of residence OR a tenancy agreement (valid for the next 6 months) if you are renting your place of residence
Declaration of number of properties owned
If you would like to proceed with the review, please submit your request through this online form and we will advise if any further information/documents are required. Alternatively, you may contact us at 1800-222-3399 if calling from Singapore / +65 6222 3399 if calling from overseas.
topics: MediShield Life / Information used for means-testing

questions.title: I am uncomfortable with my personal information being accessed. Can I choose not to participate in means-testing for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies?
questions.text:
Yes, you may choose not to allow the Ministry of Health to access your means information, for example, income for means-testing.
If you chose not to allow access to your means information, you and your entire household will not receive any MediShield Life Premium Subsidies as there is insufficient information for us to calculate the subsidies to be given.
Your household will still be covered by MediShield Life.

questions.title: Will my information which was obtained to check for my eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies be shared with other Government public assistance schemes?
questions.text:
Yes, sharing the subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies will help Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents benefit from other Government assistance schemes easily. However, detailed means and medical information will not be shared beyond MediShield Life, in order to protect the confidentiality of the information.
If you prefer not to share your subsidy eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies with other Government public assistance schemes, you can exercise this option via the MediShield Life e-service (https://medishieldlife.moh.gov.sg/). Alternatively, please call 1800-222-3399 for further assistance.
Do note that if you exercise this option, you may need to re-submit separate applications and/or means information for such schemes in future. This will however, not affect your household’s eligibility for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies, unless you and/or your household members have also chosen not to allow MOH access to your means information for the eligibility check for MediShield Life Premium Subsidies.

questions.title: What is Additional Premium Support and what are the eligibility criteria for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. This may include low-income single elderly without family support and low-income families with multiple dependants. The Government will invite these individuals to apply for APS and help them with the process if they are unable to do so themselves.
Eligibility for APS is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his immediate family members’ financial means. Flexibility will be exercised for individuals who may not completely meet the criteria but need help because of their financial circumstances.
No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage due to the inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: How will those with no income (e.g. needy, not working) be able to afford the MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums? What if they do not have enough MediSave or do not have a MediSave account?
questions.text:
The Government provides Singaporeans with premium subsidies and support, such as Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle-income, special Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies. Those who are less well-off will qualify for higher Government subsidies to reduce their premium payment.
MediShield Life and CareShield Life premiums may be paid using your MediSave. Immediate family members such as parents and spouse, can help to use their MediSave to pay for their loved ones.
Those who are still unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave, and have limited family support, may be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS), which will cover all outstanding premiums and their premiums for the next two policy years
From 1 April 2025, enhancements will be made to several of these premium support measures to cushion the impact of premium increases. Please refer to press release for more details.
No one will lose their MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) coverage because of an inability to pay premiums.

questions.title: I am currently receiving Additional Premium Support (APS) for MediShield Life coverage, will I also receive APS for CareShield Life?
questions.text:
When approved, Additional Premium Support (APS) will cover MediShield Life and CareShield Life (if applicable) premiums for the next two years.
Please note that you will not be eligible for APS if you have an additional private medical insurance cover under an Integrated Shield Plan and/or Supplements under ElderShield/CareShield Life.

questions.title: How can Additional Premium Support help me with my MediShield Life and CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If approved, Additional Premium Support (APS) will cover your outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums as well as the premiums for the next two years.
For outstanding premiums, APS will pay the premiums and any interest incurred. Any penalty will also be waived.

questions.title: How can I apply for Additional Premium Support to pay for my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text: Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. You will be invited to apply for APS should you have insufficient MediSave, and details on the application process will be included in the invitation letter. There is no need for you to apply for APS ahead of time.

questions.title: What is the processing time for my Additional Premium Support (APS) Application?
questions.text:
Your application will be processed upon receipt of your completed application form and supporting documents where relevant.
The processing time is generally up to 20 working days for most cases as each APS application undergoes a thorough and careful assessment, including taking into consideration any extenuating circumstances that the applicant may be facing.
You will receive a letter to inform you on the outcome of your APS application.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I previously applied for Additional Premium Support but was rejected. Can I apply for assistance again to help pay my premiums for the next policy year?
questions.text:
As you were previously assessed to be ineligible to receive Additional Premium Support (APS), we encourage you to pay your outstanding premiums (if any) via any of the options enclosed in the Rejection for Additional Premium Support Application Letter (Ref: APCREJ).
You may re-apply for APS if there is a change in your financial circumstances or if you face any extenuating circumstances that were not highlighted during your previous application.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I am on a Government Financial Assistance Scheme. Can I conserve my MediSave and apply Additional Premium Support to pay my MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life Premiums?
questions.text:
If you are currently on a Government financial assistance scheme, there is no need for you to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). You will automatically be granted APS if you have insufficient MediSave to pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums.
APS is a financial assistance scheme designed to support members who cannot afford their premiums even after subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support. If you have sufficient MediSave to pay your MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums, you will not be eligible for APS.

questions.title: Will overseas Singaporeans in financial difficulties be eligible for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text:
Overseas Singaporeans who have insufficient MediSave and limited family support to pay their MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums will be invited to apply for Additional Premium Support (APS). Please note that all APS applications will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.
If you require further clarification, please call us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399 from overseas) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) or write in to us through this online form.

questions.title: Am I eligible for Additional Premium Support if I have an Integrated Shield Plan and/or active-paying ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement?
questions.text:
If you were approved for Additional Premium Support (APS) before CareShield Life (CSHL) implementation and have purchased an active-paying ElderShield (ESH) supplement, you will continue to receive APS for premiums for the two years after the approval. However, your APS will cease immediately if you purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP).
If you purchase an active-paying ESH / CSHL Supplement after CSHL implementation, you will not be eligible for APS. This is to ensure that APS is targeted at members who are needy and have financial difficulties.
Should you have difficulty paying the premiums for your IP or active-paying ESH/ CSHL Supplement, you may wish to approach your financial advisor to review your health insurance coverage based on your care preferences and long-term affordability of the plans.

questions.title: I am unsure of how to fill up the Additional Premium Support (APS) application form. Can I request an officer to help me with my APS application?
questions.text: If you require assistance to fill up or submit the Additional Premium Support (APS) application form, you may call us at 1800-222-3399 (or +65 6222 3399 from overseas) from Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 5.30pm (GMT+8) or write in through this online form. Our officers will guide you through the steps to fill up the APS application form.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I received the Additional Premium Support application form. Who are considered as my immediate family members to be included in the application form?
questions.text: Immediate family members refer to parents, spouse and children who is/are related to the Main Applicant by blood, marriage and/or legal adoption, but does not refer to other family members such as siblings, grandparents and grandchildren.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I received an application form each for myself and my child. I wish to apply for myself and my child. Can I submit only one application form?
questions.text:
You only need to submit one application form for yourself if your child is below 21 years old. Please indicate in the application form that you are applying for Additional Premium Support (APS) for yourself (Main Applicant). If you are assessed to be eligible for APS, we will automatically extend APS to your child.
However, if your child is above 21 years old, he/she will need to submit a separate application form with himself/herself as the Main Applicant.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: Why did I receive the Additional Premium Support invitation letter (Ref: APCINV)?
questions.text:
Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.
As you have outstanding MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums, the letter was sent to invite you to apply for APS if you wish to. Alternatively, you may top up your MediSave Account to pay your outstanding premiums. Family members can also help pay for your premiums using their MediSave.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: How can I submit the supporting documents to complete my overseas APS application?
questions.text: You may scan and email your completed Additional Premium Support (APS) application form and any relevant documents through this online form.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: I have received a letter from MOH stating that my Additional Premium Support (APS) application was rejected. Why was I rejected and how do I appeal for APS?
questions.text:
Eligibility for Additional Premium Support (APS) is based on, but not limited to the applicants’ and his/her immediate family members’ financial means. As individuals’ circumstances differ from one another, each application will be assessed on a case-by-case basis to ensure that assistance is targeted at members who are needy.
You may submit your enquiry and reason(s) for APS appeal, with any relevant supporting documents through this online form.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: Do I need to re-apply for Additional Premium Support (APS)?
questions.text: You will be invited to re-apply for APS if you still have insufficient MediSave to pay your premiums after your current APS ends.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: How do I know if Additional Premium Support has been granted to fully pay my outstanding MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You will receive a letter to inform you on the outcome of your APS application.
For MediShield Life premiums, you may log in to "Outstanding MediShield Life premium". If you do not have any outstanding premium, you will not be able to view this page.
For CareShield Life premiums, you may log in to ‘Check My Premium’ at careshieldlife.gov.sg via SingPass. If you are eligible for APS, the ‘Net Premium Payable after Additional Premium Support’ field will be reflected as $0.
topics: MediShield Life / Application For Additional Premium Support

questions.title: Why did I receive calls or visits from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) officers?
questions.text:
These officers from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) are part of the Additional Premium Support (APS) outreach team.
As you have outstanding MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life premiums and MOH has not received your APS application form after sending letter(s) to invite you to apply for APS, the MSF officer has called / visited you to explain about MediShield Life and / or CareShield Life and how to apply for APS to help you pay your premiums.

questions.title: Why did I receive a call from someone who claimed to be an officer from the Ministry Of Health (MOH) asking me to apply for Additional Premium Support?
questions.text: As the Ministry of Health (MOH) has not received your Additional Premium Support (APS) application form after sending letter(s) to invite you to apply for APS, the MOH officer had contacted you to find out if you need assistance with the APS application. This is to ensure that adequate assistance is extended to members who are unable to afford their premiums.

questions.title: What does distributing premiums more evenly over our lifetime refer to? Why is there a need to distribute premiums more evenly over our lifetime under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums increase with age. This reflects the higher incidence of claims among the older age groups, and the higher bills incurred.
Under MediShield Life, premiums are distributed more evenly throughout our life. Policyholders pay more premiums while they are of working age, which will then be returned as premium rebates at older ages when they typically would have stopped working. This ensures that premiums rise less steeply in old age. The additional amounts paid during working age are set aside and pooled within the MediShield Life Fund.
Distributing premiums more evenly over our lifetime helps policyholders to pay ahead for their premiums. Planning and saving for our future healthcare expenses will reduce concerns over adequacy of savings during retirement.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: An individual can also save for his future premiums through his own MediSave account. Why do we opt for this mechanism where monies that are paid ahead are pooled?
questions.text:
Paying ahead for insurance premiums is a more inclusive and collective approach to boost the support for each generation’s future old-age premiums. Under this approach, everyone pools some monies during working ages which are set aside to help support the old-age premiums of those of the same generation. Doing so gives policyholders a pool of pre-paid premiums to tap on in future, to cushion the impact of future increases during the retirement years.
In contrast, while MediSave is useful to help with healthcare costs, including insurance premiums, there are also many competing demands for it such as hospitalisation bills and outpatient treatment for chronic diseases, which all add to pressure on MediSave balances.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: How much more premium rebates will Singapore Residents get in old age, with premiums distributed more evenly over our lifetime?
questions.text:
Please click here (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/premium-rebates) for more information on the enhanced premium rebate table applicable to incoming cohorts.
The scheme is designed such that younger policyholders who pre-pay more during their working ages will receive greater premium rebates. This will help to offset more of old-age premiums for their generation.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: Why do premium rebates stop at age 90?
questions.text:
Under MediShield, the premium rebate schedule was designed to support premium rebates up to age 90, which was the maximum coverage age under MediShield. With MediShield Life, Pioneers above age 90 will not need to pay any premiums after the Pioneer Generation subsidies and MediSave top-ups. In view of this, there is no immediate need to extend the last coverage age of the premium rebates.
The Ministry of Health will review the premium rebates from time to time so that the distribution of rebates is able to meet the needs of the elderly.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: What will happen to the premiums that policyholders have pre-paid in their working years should they pass away early? Will the monies be returned to their family members?
questions.text: The premiums that are pre-paid are pooled together by age group to help cushion the future increases in premiums during older ages. While some members may pass on earlier, the remaining pool of funds will help those of the same age group who live longer and need to draw on more rebates.
topics: MediShield Life / Pre-funding under MediShield Life

questions.title: Who is covered under MediShield Life? Do I need to apply for MediShield Life?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are automatically covered under MediShield Life. No application is required.
If you are covered by MediShield Life only, when your plan is up for annual renewal, the current payer (who may be yourself or your family member) will receive a letter from the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board with details about your MediShield Life premiums and subsidies.
If you are covered by an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), when your IP is up for annual renewal, the current payer (who may be yourself or your family member) will receive a letter from your private insurer with details about your premiums and subsidies. You will receive subsidies for the MediShield Life portion of your IP if you are eligible.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: I have my own healthcare coverage, why do I need MediShield Life? How is MediShield Life different from other insurance schemes?
questions.text:
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are required to join MediShield Life. Under MediShield Life, Singapore Residents will receive lifelong protection for large medical bills. The Government provides support for premiums for the needy who are unable to pay. Even if you incur very large bills over your lifetime, the insurance cover will not be terminated when you get very sick.
Unlike MediShield Life, other healthcare coverage is not guaranteed for life. For example, employees with healthcare coverage from their employers may lose such coverage when they leave employment or retire. Those with other forms of private insurance (e.g., Integrated Shield Plans) may lose this coverage if they are unable to pay for premiums, and they may not be able to re-apply for coverage later or may incur exclusions if they have already developed some health conditions.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: I have been insured for many years but have not made a claim. Why should I remain insured under MediShield Life?
questions.text: Insurance provides protection against the risk of undesirable outcomes and financial costs. MediShield Life provides greater peace-of-mind if policyholders fall sick and incur a large bill. They can enjoy better protection, with payouts to reduce the amount that they need to pay using MediSave and/or cash.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: I am a pensioner retired from the civil service. Can I opt out of MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Universal lifelong coverage under MediShield Life ensures that all Singapore Residents will have assurance against large healthcare bills. It is in line with our move to a more inclusive society with stronger collective responsibility. MediShield Life coverage is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents, including those who receive benefits from their employer. This enables all Singapore Residents to share in our national risk pool and play our part in supporting our healthcare costs.
If you are a pensioner, you will also be covered under MediShield Life. To ensure that pensioners are not worse off with the introduction of MediShield Life, the Government has been helping pensioners with their MediShield Life premiums by paying for their premiums in full or by providing 2% MediSave contribution, depending on their respective medical benefit schemes.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: How can I find out if I am covered under MediShield Life or an Integrated Shield Plan?
questions.text:
You are covered under MediShield Life if you are a Singaporean or Permanent Resident.
If you are covered under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), your premium payer will be notified by your private insurer with details about your premiums and subsidies when your IP is up for annual renewal. You will receive applicable subsidies for the MediShield Life portion of your IP, if you meet the eligibility criteria.
You can log in to visit the Healthcare dashboard (cpf.gov.sg/healthcare) 'Coverage and premium details' to check the coverage and premium information for yourself and the dependant(s) you are paying premiums for.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: Will new Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents be required to join MediShield Life?
questions.text:
New Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents will be required to join MediShield Life, in line with the principle of universal coverage. New Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with serious pre-existing conditions may have to pay Additional Premiums upon joining MediShield Life. They will be eligible for Government subsidies for their MediShield Life premiums if they meet the eligibility criteria and will receive premium rebates in line with their age of entry.
They will be notified of their MediShield Life cover by Central Provident Fund Board when their covers have been issued, generally within 1 month of attaining permanent residence.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: When will the MediShield Life cover of my newborn baby start? Will I be notified?
questions.text: Newborns who are registered as Singapore Citizens at birth are insured under MediShield Life from birth. The Central Provident Fund Board will notify his/her parent (usually the father) of the new-born’s MediShield Life coverage details generally within 1 month of the start of the MediShield Life cover.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What are the areas of duplication between MediShield Life and health insurance plans that are not Integrated Shield Plans?
questions.text: MediShield Life is a basic health insurance plan that helps to pay for large hospital bills and selected expensive outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy for cancer. It is basic which means it is sized for subsidised treatments in the public hospitals. You may wish to compare the benefits of your health insurance plan with those of MediShield Life at this link (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-benefits/), to identify the areas of duplication. You may also wish to approach your financial advisor who will be able to share more with you.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What should I do if I want to avoid/remove such duplication between MediShield Life and health insurance plans that are not Integrated Shield Plans?
questions.text:
You may wish to consider avoiding/removing such duplication by taking up an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), which comprises a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance coverage component.
Unlike MediShield Life which provides coverage for policyholders with pre-existing conditions, you may be subject to exclusions by private insurers. You may wish to speak to your financial advisor who will be able to share more about your options.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What will happen to my MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan cover when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status?
questions.text:
Today, all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents are covered by MediShield Life.
Should you renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status and are only insured under MediShield Life, you will lose MediShield Life cover.
If you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), you will either no longer have a MediShield Life component (which may include coverage of any pre-existing conditions) in your IP or have your IP terminated. Please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options. If you wish to terminate your IP, you will also need to notify your private insurer in a manner as required by your insurer.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What will happen to the MediShield Life or Integrated Shield Plan premiums I paid when I renounce my Singapore Citizenship or Permanent Resident status?
questions.text:
Should you renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status and are only insured under MediShield Life, your MediShield Life cover will cease. The annual premium that you have paid will be pro-rated and the amount for the period after your renouncement date will be refunded to the MediSave Account of the premium payer.
If you are insured under an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), please inform your private insurer if you have plans to renounce your citizenship or permanent resident status so that your insurer can advise you on the available coverage options and explain what will happen to the premiums you have paid. If you wish to terminate your IP, you will also need to notify your private insurer in a manner as required by your insurer.
topics: MediShield Life / Universal Coverage For All

questions.title: What are pre-existing conditions? What are considered serious pre-existing conditions?
questions.text:
A pre-existing condition is a medical condition or illness that an individual already has before he is covered under an insurance plan.
A serious pre-existing condition is one that may require intensive medical intervention to treat or manage; or have high risk of future complications or recurrence, and therefore may require prolonged treatment.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: For those with serious pre-existing conditions, why do they have to pay Additional Premiums? What is the reason for setting it at 30% over 10 years? Would this be too onerous for some?
questions.text:
The Additional Premiums apply to the first 10 years of premiums paid by Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents who newly join the scheme and who have pre-existing conditions.
The Additional Premiums reflect the higher risks of covering these individuals with serious pre-existing conditions while ensuring that premiums remain affordable and are not overly onerous.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: What are the serious pre-existing conditions that will be subject to Additional Premiums?
questions.text:
A fair and compassionate approach has been adopted in identifying the Singapore Residents who will be subject to the Additional Premiums due to their serious pre-existing conditions.
The focus is on serious conditions that require intensive medical intervention to treat or manage; or have high risk of future complications or recurrence and therefore may require prolonged treatment. Within these broad categories, whether individuals with serious pre-existing conditions will be subject to Additional Premiums depends on factors such as specific nature and severity of the individual’s medical condition.
For more details on the broad categories of serious pre-existing conditions that would require Additional Premiums, click here (https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/medishield-life/coverage-for-pre-existing-conditions).
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: What if my medical condition has improved? Must I still pay the 30% Additional Premiums? Can I appeal against the imposition of the Additional Premiums?
questions.text:
You may apply to the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board to reassess your medical condition with updated medical information.
For more information, you can write to us (medishield.sg/writetous) or call 1800-222-3399.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Will individuals with developmental disorders have to pay the Additional Premiums?
questions.text: Developmental conditions such as Down Syndrome and Autism alone do not have Additional Premiums imposed on them. However, if an individual with these conditions also presents with serious pre-existing medical complications, such as heart or kidney disease, which elevate the risk of claims, MediShield Life will apply Additional Premiums based on these medical conditions.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Are checks conducted for new Singapore Residents who are automatically covered under MediShield Life?
questions.text:
For new Singapore Residents who are automatically covered under MediShield Life, we implement a range of checks, including reviewing medical records after they are covered. They are also required to declare their health status upon receipt of the In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter from the Immigrated & Checkpoint Authority of Singapore (ICA). A copy of the form can be found by using this link (https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/tools-and-services/forms-e-applications/health-declaration-pr-applicants)
If they are identified to have serious pre-existing conditions, they will be subject to the 30% Additional Premiums for 10 years. Those who make false health declarations will be guilty of an offence under the MediShield Life Scheme Act and will be liable to pay penalties.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: What if I have an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), does the 30% Additional Premiums apply to my entire IP premiums?
questions.text:
Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) consist of 2 components – the MediShield Life component, sized for Ward B2/C bills, administered by the Central Provident Fund Board and the additional private insurance component for Ward A/B1 bills at public hospitals and private hospital stays, administered by private insurers.
The 30% Additional Premiums only applies to the MediShield Life component of your IP premiums.
For the additional private insurance component, IP insurers will separately assess whether to introduce exclusions or risk-loading (i.e., higher than the standard premiums) for those with pre-existing conditions.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Are subsidies applicable to the 30% Additional Premiums for those with serious pre-existing conditions?
questions.text: Yes, all subsidies are applicable to the 30% Additional Premiums for those with serious pre-existing conditions. This includes the Premium Subsidies for the lower- to middle income, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation subsidies for Singapore Citizens. For Singaporeans who are not able to afford their premiums even after subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, which will also be applicable to the Additional Premiums.
topics: MediShield Life / Coverage for pre-existing conditions

questions.title: Why is there a need for strong premium recovery measures?
questions.text:
With universal MediShield Life coverage, as part of collective responsibility, all Singapore Residents should play their part in paying their premiums in a timely manner. This ensures that MediShield Life is able to meet its commitments to all its members and pay out on claims.
The Government will provide strong support through various subsidies to help Singaporeans with their premiums. Active measures will also be taken to facilitate the payment of premiums, including deduction of premiums fully from MediSave balances, regular reminders, switch of payment arrangement to family members and Additional Premium Support for the genuinely needy.
However, there may be a small group of defaulters who have means but choose not to pay premiums. The premium recovery measures are targeted at this group to discourage freeloading and ensure that they also pay their fair share of premiums. Otherwise, premium defaults will translate to bad debts to the MediShield Life Fund and higher premiums for all.

questions.title: What are the premium recovery measures? Who will enforce premium payment?
Will those who are less well-off and unable to pay their premiums face these premium recovery measures?
questions.text:
In addition to premium support measures from the Government to help the lower-income ensure that premiums are affordable (e.g. Additional Premium Support), these are some other measures that have been implemented:
a. Helping to keep MediSave contributions current. As MediShield Life premiums are deducted from a policyholder’s MediSave account, the first step is to ensure that MediSave contributions are kept current. The Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board has in place arrangements with multiple government agencies to ensure employers, employees and especially self-employed persons meet contribution requirements.
b. Supporting switch of payment to other family members’ MediSave accounts. If an insured person has insufficient MediSave balance, immediate family members such as parents and spouses can use their MediSave to help pay for their family member’s premiums.
c. Regular reminder letters to top up the insured’s MediSave account and to pay MediShield Life premiums.
These measures ensure that premium recovery measures are targeted at those who have the means to pay but choose not to do so. There is Additional Premium Support (APS) to help those who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums even after Government subsidies and MediSave use, and if they have limited family support. No one will be denied MediShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: Why is there a need to impose interest?
questions.text:
Interest may be imposed on outstanding premiums where appropriate, e.g. defaulters with premium arrears outstanding for prolonged periods. The interest may be compounded and recovered together with the outstanding premiums.
This fairly reflects the opportunity cost to the MediShield Life Fund, which would otherwise be invested in order to support future payments (e.g. MediShield Life claims) from the MediShield Life Fund. This loss translates to higher premiums for the rest of the insured if they are not recovered in a timely manner.
