questions.title: Do I still have to contribute to MediSave as a self-employed person even though my MediSave balance has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person, you are required to make mandatory MediSave contributions even if you have met the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS). Your MediSave contributions are computed based on your assessable net trade income.
This is no different from employees and platform workers, who continue to make CPF contributions, based on their employee wages or platform worker net earnings, even after reaching BHS and/or the Full Retirement Sum (FRS).
MediSave Account (MA) savings above the BHS will first be channelled to your CPF Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA), depending on your age, to build up your retirement savings. Once you have met the FRS in your SA or RA, the MA savings in excess of the BHS will be channelled to your Ordinary Account, which you can tap on for your housing needs. This overflow arrangement prevents excessive accumulation in your MA and helps to enhance your retirement and housing adequacy.

questions.title: What other moves are the Government making to ensure Assistive Technology (AT) remains affordable?
questions.text:
The Assistive Technology Fund (ATF) provides subsidies of up to 90% for PwDs who require AT devices. Subsidy rates are regularly reviewed to ensure that AT remains affordable.
Open Door Programme (ODP)-registered employers can also apply for grants and employment support services such as the Job Redesign Grant to support redesigning of jobs such as purchases of equipment (including AT devices) and workplace modification.
PwDs who require more financial support in purchasing AT devices may approach SG Enable for further assistance.

questions.title: Why is the Government expanding the coverage of the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) to Singaporeans with disabilities below age 55?
questions.text:
From 1 January 2026, MRSS will be expanded to include younger Singaporeans with disabilities to give them a greater boost for retirement by helping them to start building up their retirement savings earlier via cash top-ups to the CPF Special Account (SA).
Eligible persons with disabilities can receive a dollar-for-dollar matching grant of up to $2,000/year, with a lifetime limit of $20,000 from the Government on cash top-ups received in their CPF SA. Persons with disabilities will need to register as a person with disability and will still be subject to other MRSS eligibility criteria such as CPF balances, monthly income and Annual Value of their residential property. More details on how to register as a person with disability will be released in the second half of 2025.

questions.title: How was I identified to pay my family member's CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
You had previously used your MediSave to help pay the insured’s medical expenses or health insurance premiums. To encourage family responsibility, we will notify family members that they can use their MediSave to help their family member with insufficient MediSave. This makes it convenient for the majority of members who wish to help their family members pay their CareShield Life/MediShield Life premiums. To date, more than 90% of family members approached have accepted the arrangement.
Family members who are identified as potential payers will be notified one month before premium deduction takes place. You may reject this payment arrangement by submitting Stop Payment for CareShield Life/MediShield Life or call us at 1800-222-3399.
You can later decide to pay for your family member's MediShield Life premiums by submitting a Change Payer for CareShield Life/MediShield Life.

questions.title: Will I get into trouble if my actual income declared to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) in the following year is different from the estimated income which I provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services?
questions.text: No, as the revenue and expenses information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only an estimate of your business outlook for the year. You are still required to separately declare to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) your actual net trade income (NTI), which may differ from the estimated revenue and expenses provided for the purposes of CAYE.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Why do I still need to declare my income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) when I have already provided my estimated income via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services?
questions.text: The revenue and expenses information you provided via the Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) digital services is only an estimate of your business outlook for the year and is only used to compute your CAYE contribution rate. You are still required to separately declare your actual net trade income (NTI) in the following year to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: Can I receive my net service fee payments through methods other than PayNow?
questions.text:
You will only be able to use the bank account registered to your PayNow to receive service fee payments.
Please ensure that you have registered for PayNow (excluding PayNow Mobile Number and Virtual Payments Address) so that you receive your service fee payments promptly.
You may approach your bank if you need more information on how to sign up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: How can I change the amount or delete my recurring CPF transfer arrangement?
questions.text:
You can change the amount of your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement by following the steps below:
Delete your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement in the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form.
Create a new recurring CPF transfer arrangement via the same form with the revised amount. The transfer will take effect from the following month on the 18th upon successful application.
You can delete your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement via the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form.
Your deletion application will generally be processed instantly. For example, if you delete your recurring CPF transfer arrangement on 17 May, no transfer will take place on 18 May.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: What happens to my recurring CPF transfer arrangement if I have reached my top-up limit or have insufficient Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: If you have insufficient top-up limit or Ordinary Account (OA) savings, we will transfer up to your remaining top-up limit or available OA savings. Please note that your recurring arrangement will be stopped after two consecutive unsuccessful transfers (where no amount is transferred).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: I am below 55 years old. Can I set up recurring CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Special Account?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above. If you are below 55 years old, you may wish to make a one-time CPF transfer from your Ordinary Account to Special Account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I check my existing recurring CPF transfers arrangements?
questions.text: You can check your existing recurring CPF transfer arrangement by accessing the Manage recurring cash top-ups and CPF transfers for retirement form, under “Who you are making recurring top-ups to”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I make monthly transfers of my CPF employment contributions from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
If you are aged 55 and above and would like to transfer your monthly CPF employment contributions regularly from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA), you can do so by setting up recurring CPF transfers . With this recurring transfer service, you can conveniently earn higher interest on your CPF employment contributions credited to your OA and build up your retirement savings in your RA.
Upon successful application, your recurring transfer will take effect from the following month on the 18th.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible. The savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I make recurring CPF transfers to my loved ones?
questions.text: The recurring CPF transfer e-Service is currently only available for members aged 55 and above to make CPF transfers to their own Retirement Account. If you wish to make CPF transfer to your loved ones, you may make a one-time CPF transfer instead.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Can I set up yearly CPF transfers from my Ordinary Account to Retirement Account?
questions.text:
The recurring CPF transfer e-Service currently allows monthly CPF transfers only. By setting up recurring CPF transfers, you can easily transfer your monthly CPF working contributions received in your Ordinary Account to your Retirement Account.
If you intend to make a CPF transfer once a year, you may wish to do so via the one-time CPF transfer form.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: When does my recurring CPF transfer take place?
questions.text:
The transfer from your Ordinary Account (OA) to Retirement Account (RA) takes place on the 18th of each month.
If you set up a new recurring CPF transfer, the transfer will take effect from the following month upon successful application.
Note: Please ensure that you maintain sufficient funds in your OA for the transfer. The recurring CPF transfer arrangement will be stopped if there are two consecutive unsuccessful transfers. There is no penalty for unsuccessful transfers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: How can I receive my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment if I don't have a bank account with DBS/POSB, OCBC or UOB?
questions.text:
If you do not have a bank account with the three local banks (DBS/POSB, OCBC and UOB) but have a bank account with a PayNow-GIRO participating foreign bank, you can link the bank account to PayNow using your NRIC to receive your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment. Payment via PayNow-NRIC will be faster as compared to other payment modes. Please contact your bank to check how you can link your bank account to PayNow-NRIC.
If you do not have any PayNow-NRIC linked bank account or bank account with the local banks (DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB), you will receive your PCTS via GovCash.
As payment by GovCash takes three weeks longer than through a bank account, we encourage you to register for PayNow-NRIC with your preferred bank or ensure that you have a valid bank account registered via the govbenefits website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can someone else withdraw my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) which has been credited via GovCash, if they know my Payment Reference Number (PRN)?
questions.text:
It is not possible to withdraw your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) benefits credited into GovCash using just the Payment Reference Number as GovCash uses the Singpass facial verification technology to authenticate users during the withdrawal of Government cash benefits from OCBC ATMs. The facial verification technology incorporates a liveness-detection capability that blocks the use of photographs, videos or masks during the verification process.
This security feature prevents any fraudulent withdrawal of Government benefits by third parties using photographs or videos belonging to the beneficiary. This ensures that only the eligible Singaporean can perform the withdrawal of his or her government benefits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I obtain my Payment Reference Number (PRN) for my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) which was paid to me via GovCash?
questions.text: If you are eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), and received payment via GovCash, you will receive an 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN) via an email or SMS after the PCTS payment has been credited.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can you re-send my Payment Reference Number (PRN) to me?
questions.text: You can retrieve your Payment Reference Number (PRN) via logging on to the govbenefits website using your Singpass. You can find your PRN by selecting “GovCash PRN” that is found at the menu on the left. You will be directed to the page where your PRN will be displayed.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Will notifications be sent to all platform workers on their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments?
questions.text:
Only eligible platform workers will receive notifications on their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) benefits if they have an email address or mobile number registered with CPF Board, and after the payment has been credited.
Platform workers who are not eligible for PCTS will not receive notifications on PCTS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next-of-kin. How do I request for the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) on behalf of my next-of-kin?
questions.text:
If you are the appointed donee or deputy, you can consider setting up the Singpass Multi-User SMS 2FA via the links below:
- Application for Donees with LPA
- Application for Deputies with Court Order
This allows you to conveniently access and view your next-of-kin’s Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) without having to repeatedly provide supporting documents.
You will have to provide the necessary supporting documents for the one-time set-up via the links above. Please refer to Singpass FAQs for more information on Multi-User SMS 2FA.
If you are unable to set up the Singpass Multi-User SMS 2FA, you can Write to us to request for your next-of-kin’s statement on their behalf, by providing the following documents:
- For Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Submit the LPA document and a medical report certifying your next-of-kin’s loss of mental capacity
- For Deputy appointed by the Singapore Court: Submit the Deputyship court order
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Why is the option to withdraw GovCash only available in $10 denominations and what can I do with my balance GovCash?
questions.text:
The minimum withdrawal amount at the ATMs is $10, so GovCash withdrawals are made in $10 denominations. If your GovCash balance is less than $10, you can accumulate funds for your next withdrawal.
Alternatively, you can transfer the balance to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account, use it to make payments at merchants with PayNow/NETS QR codes, or transfer it to your family/friends by scanning the PayNow QR code using the LifeSG mobile app.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I seek help regarding my GovCash withdrawal?
questions.text: If you are unable to verify your identity via Singpass Face Verification at an OCBC ATM after several attempts or if you require assistance with your GovCash withdrawals, you can visit a NEW ATM located at selected OCBC branches (refer to OCBC website for latest list of New ATMs) during the branch operating hours. OCBC Digital Ambassadors will be available to assist you.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: How do I check my GovCash balance?
questions.text: To check your GovCash balance, visit any OCBC ATMs with your 8-digit Payment Reference Number (PRN). Upon successful authentication, you will be able to view your GovCash balance. Alternatively, you can log in to the LifeSG mobile app using your Singpass to view your balance and transaction history.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: What is the bank account that is linked to PayNow with my NRIC number?
questions.text:
The information about your bank account that is linked to PayNow with your NRIC number is maintained with the bank and not known to CPF Board. Check with your bank directly on the specific bank account that is linked to PayNow with your NRIC number.
CPF Board only needs your NRIC number to make CPF payments to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars

questions.title: Will I still get my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) if I do not use PayNow-NRIC?
questions.text: Platform workers who do not register for PayNow-NRIC will still receive Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment based on existing modes of payment, i.e. through your bank account registered to receive Government benefits or through GovCash. You may check and update your bank account information via the govbenefits website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Can the Government credit my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) to me via PayNow-Mobile? Why do I need to register my NRIC with PayNow to receive government payments?
questions.text: We can only credit your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) to you via PayNow-NRIC as NRIC is an unchanged proxy issued by the Government that serves as a unique identifier for each individual. Unlike the NRIC, mobile numbers are not unique to the individual and may be subject to change. To ensure that the money is credited to the correct recipient, we are using NRIC as the proxy for government payments via PayNow.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I view details of my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment?
questions.text: Eligible platform workers will receive notifications for their Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment via email or SMS, after the PCTS is disbursed every month. Please refer to your bank statement of your PayNow-NRIC linked bank account or the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why have I not received any notification about my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment even though I am eligible, and the payment has been credited?
questions.text: You will not receive any notifications on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payment if you have not registered your email address or mobile number with CPF Board. To receive notifications, you may update your mobile number or email address via my cpf digital services - Account Settings with your Singpass.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Where can I view details of my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) eligibility?
questions.text: Eligible platform workers will receive notifications sent via email/SMS, after Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) payments are made in each month. You can also refer to your bank statement of the PayNow-NRIC linked bank account or the bank account that you have registered to receive Government benefits. The crediting to your bank account will be reflected as “OTHR GOV GOV”. You can use the PCTS calculator to estimate the amount of PCTS you may be eligible to receive.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: If I work for multiple platforms, how will my eligibility for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) be assessed?
questions.text:
To qualify for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS), your total income for the month must not exceed $3,000. This includes your net earnings (gross earnings minus the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount) from each platform operator you work for, along with any income from other employment sources, which will all be summed up to determine whether your income exceeds $3,000.
If your total income does not exceed $3,000:
Your PCTS amount will be computed based on net earnings from each platform operator separately (i.e. per-platform basis), and then summed up. This is in view that all your platform operators will calculate and contribute CPF for you separately (i.e. per-platform basis), and PCTS is intended to offset part of the increase in CPF contributions made.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings when I turn 55?
questions.text:
When you turn 55, the following will happen to your CPF savings:
Retirement Account (RA): Savings from your Special Account (SA) and Ordinary Account (OA) will be transferred to your newly created RA, up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Your SA savings will be transferred first, followed by your OA savings if your SA savings is insufficient to set aside your FRS.
SA closure: After the transfer, your SA will be closed, and any remaining SA savings will be transferred to your OA.
Find out more about what happens when you reach age 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is the Retirement Account for?
questions.text:
The savings in your Retirement Account (RA) is meant to provide you with payouts in retirement. You can start your payouts anytime from your payout eligibility age of 65.
Find out how your RA is created when you turn 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is the closure of Special Account for members aged 55 and above about?
questions.text:
The closure of Special Account (SA) for members aged 55 and above was announced during Budget 2024, and took effect from 19 January 2025. This change is to better align CPF interest rates to the nature of CPF savings in each CPF account, i.e. savings that cannot be withdrawn on demand should earn the long-term interest rate, and savings that can be withdrawn on demand should earn the short-term interest rate.
With the closure of the SA, your SA savings will be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), where they will continue to earn the long-term interest rate. If you have set aside your FRS, whether fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash, any remaining SA savings will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA) and can be withdrawn on demand.
- If you were 55 and above on 19 January 2025: Your SA was closed on that date, with your SA savings transferred to your RA, up to your FRS, and any remaining savings transferred to your OA. For more information on how the amounts transferred from your SA to your RA and OA were determined, you may view this infographic.
- If you turn 55 after 19 January 2025: On your 55th birthday, RA will be created for you, and your SA will be closed. Find out more about what happens when you reach age 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: In setting aside the Full Retirement Sum in my Retirement Account, why are my Special Account savings transferred before my Ordinary Account savings?
questions.text: The savings in your Special Account (SA) are meant for your retirement needs, while your Ordinary Account (OA) savings can be used to meet shorter-term expenditure needs such as housing. Hence, when you turn 55, SA savings are first transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to help you set aside the retirement sum, which will eventually be streamed out as monthly payouts when you reach your payout eligibility age.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Do I need to top up my Retirement Account and will I receive monthly payouts if I am unable to set aside my Full Retirement Sum?
questions.text:
It is not mandatory for you to top up your Retirement Account (RA) if you are unable to set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). You can still receive monthly payouts anytime from your payout eligibility age, and the payout amount will be based on your RA savings.
However, you may wish to top up your RA for higher monthly payouts. You can also enjoy tax relief for cash top-ups up to the FRS.
Did you know? You can use the Monthly payout estimator to estimate how much you need to top up to reach your desired monthly payouts.
If you receive contributions, government grants or other refunds in your CPF accounts after 55, they will be transferred to your RA up to your FRS (or Basic Retirement Sum if you own a property) on your next withdrawal.
If you are born in 1958 or after and wish to start your monthly payouts, there will be another transfer of your Ordinary Account (OA) savings, up to your FRS, to your RA, if you have not met your FRS. This transfer allows you to receive higher monthly payouts.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Can I choose to transfer more savings from the Special Account to the Ordinary Account since I am still servicing my housing loan/education loan etc.?
questions.text:
When your Special Account (SA) is closed after your Retirement Account (RA) is created, any remaining savings in your SA that are withdrawable on demand will be transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA).
You may use the portion transferred to your OA for your housing loan/education loan (subject to applicable limits) or choose to withdraw them anytime for your immediate needs. You cannot choose to allocate more SA savings or your future RA contributions to your OA to service your housing/education loan, etc.
If you are using your OA savings to service your housing loan, you may apply to reserve your OA savings prior to turning 55 years old for housing payments beyond age 55. The amount reserved in your OA will not be transferred to your RA.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: I belong to the generation born before 1958 and can withdraw a portion of my Special Account (SA) savings even though I have not set aside my Full Retirement Sum. Will I continue to be able to withdraw after my SA is closed?
questions.text:
When your Special Account (SA) is closed, the amount you could have withdrawn from your SA will be transferred to your Ordinary Account, and you can continue to withdraw this amount anytime.
If you continue to work after your SA is closed, any new contributions that used to be allocated to your SA will instead be allocated to your Retirement Account (RA), up to your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). This will go towards meeting your long-term retirement needs, by allowing you to receive higher monthly payouts from your Payout Eligibility Age. If you have immediate needs, you can choose to set aside up to half the FRS using your property and withdraw your savings above the Basic Retirement Sum in your RA.
If you require further assistance, you may write to us.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How much interest will I earn on the Special Account (SA) savings that are transferred to my Retirement Account and Ordinary Account upon the closure of my SA when I turn 55?
questions.text:
As CPF interest is computed monthly, your Special Account (SA) savings (excluding contributions and refunds received in the month) that are transferred to your Retirement Account (RA), up to the Full Retirement Sum, will earn RA interest for that month. The RA interest rate is the same as the SA interest rate.
Remaining SA savings that are transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA) will earn OA interest for that month. If you wish to earn the RA interest rate on these savings and receive higher retirement payouts, you may transfer your SA savings that were channelled to your OA, to the RA up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum, after your SA has been closed. The amount transferred to your RA (excluding any new contributions and refunds received in the month) will earn the RA interest rate in the month of transfer1 . For example, if you transfer your OA savings to your RA in June 2025, the amount transferred will earn the RA interest from June 2025.
If you are receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after age 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible. The savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes.
1 Find out more about the normal processing time for CPF transfers.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: My Special Account (SA) savings were transferred to the Ordinary Account (OA) after SA closure, as I have set aside the Full Retirement Sum. With the OA having lower interest, what can I do to earn the interest that the SA pays?
questions.text:
If you wish to earn higher interest and receive higher retirement payouts, you may transfer your Special Account (SA) savings that were channelled to the Ordinary Account (OA) due to the closure of SA, to the Retirement Account (RA), up to the prevailing Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS). The RA interest rate is the same as the SA.
If you are still receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after age 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
Find out more about how you can make the transfer at cpf.gov.sg/rstu.
Please note that CPF transfers are irreversible and the savings are set aside to boost your monthly payouts in retirement. Thus, the amount transferred cannot be withdrawn for any other purpose such as housing, investment, or immediate needs after age 55. Read more on how the top-ups will be used.
You can also invest the OA savings in low-risk investments, such as T-bills and fixed deposits, under the CPF Investment Scheme.
Did you know? From 1 January 2025, the ERS will be raised to four times of the Basic Retirement Sum to allow members to save more in the RA and receive higher payouts, if they want.
With the change, the ERS in 2025 would be $426,0001, up from $308,700 in 2024. Hence, if you are aged 55 and above in 2025, you can save up to $426,000 in the RA.
1 This is the limit for the savings set aside in the RA (excluding amounts such as interest earned, government grants received, plus retirement withdrawals).
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: If I turn age 55 in the middle of the month, why do the Special Account savings transferred to my Ordinary Account not earn 4% interest from the start of the month to the day I turn age 55?
questions.text:
CPF interest is computed monthly, and is credited to your respective accounts by the following year. As the Special Account (SA) amounts transferred to your Ordinary Account (OA) are withdrawable, the funds earn 2.5% interest for the month you turn age 55, in line with the principle that short term funds earn the lower short-term interest rates.
If you wish to earn the higher long-term interest rate, you can transfer your OA savings, which originated from your SA, to your Retirement Account (RA). If you are still receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
The transfer is irreversible, and will be paid to you as monthly payouts and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: My Special Account (SA) will be closed when I turn age 55 in the middle of the year. If I have the Full Retirement Sum, where does interest earned on my SA (before SA closure) go? Do I lose any interest for the remaining months till the end of the year?
questions.text:
The process for crediting CPF interest remains unchanged even after your Special Account (SA) closes at age 55. CPF interest is computed on a monthly basis and credited annually to all our CPF members.
If you have already set aside the Full Retirement Sum, the interest earned on your SA prior to its closure will be allocated to your Ordinary Account (OA) after your SA is closed, which is in line with the principle that short term funds earn the lower short-term interest rates. After your SA is closed on your 55th birthday, your CPF savings will continue earning interest in their respective accounts till the end of the year. All the interest you have earned for the whole year will then be credited by the following year.
To earn the higher long-term interest rate, you can transfer your OA savings to your Retirement Account (RA) up to the current year’s Enhanced Retirement Sum. The transfer is irreversible and will be paid to you as monthly payouts and cannot be withdrawn for other purposes. The transfer can be made anytime from age 55.
If you are receiving monthly employment contributions in your OA after 55, consider setting up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA to earn higher interest on your CPF contributions.
Find out more at cpf.gov.sg/RSTU.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Does the interest earned on my retirement savings form part of the retirement sum that I am required to set aside at age 55?
questions.text: No, the interest earned on your retirement savings does not form part of the retirement sum that you are required to set aside at 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Which accounts will my CPF contributions be allocated to after I turn age 55 and my Special Account is closed?
questions.text:
After you turn 55, CPF contributions allocated to your Special Account will be fully allocated to your Retirement Account (RA) instead, up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS), to boost retirement payouts.
If you have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to your Ordinary Account (OA).
To build up your retirement savings, you can now conveniently set up monthly recurring CPF transfers from your OA to your RA, allowing you to continue earning higher interest rates on your contributions.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Which CPF accounts will my voluntary top-ups be allocated to after I turn 55 and my Special Account is closed?
questions.text: If you are aged 55 and above, the portion of voluntary top-ups that goes to your Special Account (SA) currently will be allocated to your Retirement Account (RA) up to the Full Retirement Sum. Once you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum in your RA, it will be allocated to your Ordinary Account.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Why am I not eligible for Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) if I do not opt in to the increased CPF contributions?
questions.text: Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is intended to offset part of the year-on-year increase in contribution rates to platform workers’ Ordinary Account (OA) and Special Account (SA) or Retirement Account (RA) for lower-income platform workers (i.e. earning $3,000 or less per month). Platform workers who do not opt in to the increased CPF contributions will not experience increases in OA, SA, RA contributions, and are thus not eligible for PCTS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support

questions.title: Why is the MediShield Life claim limit for a particular combination treatment not the sum of all the claim limits for individual cancer drugs in that combination?
questions.text:
If a particular combination treatment is cost-effective, the MediShield Life (MSHL) claim limit is sized to be sufficient to cover the post-subsidy cost of the entire combination in Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs). In some cases, the claim limit for the entire combination is the same as the highest-cost drug in that combination because the cost of the other drugs in the PHIs are low and can therefore be adequately covered by the same claim limit.
If a particular combination treatment is not cost-effective, the MSHL claim limit is pegged to the highest individual claim limit of the drugs in the combination. Doctors and patients are encouraged to use treatments that have been assessed to be cost-effective, for which MSHL claim limits have been sized for.

questions.title: Why is there an increase in my MediShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
MediShield Life premiums increase with age as they are set in line with the risks for each age group. This is to avoid intergenerational cross-subsidy, where the young have to pay for the old. If premiums were not priced by age, they would keep escalating as a growing number of elderly would need to be supported by a decreasing number of younger members, imposing an increasing burden on future generations. Instead, the Government provides subsidies and premium assistance to those who are unable to afford their premiums.
Premiums may also be adjusted periodically to support enhancements to the scheme, such as expanded coverage and increased claim limits. From April 2025, premiums will increase upon policy renewal to support MediShield Life enhancements. You can refer to the MediShield Life premium rate table for policy periods commencing or renewing on or after 1 April 2025.
For more information, visit the MSHL 2024 Review page.

questions.title: How is the Government helping me to cope with the MediShield Life premium increase?
questions.text:
To help Singaporeans manage the premium increases, the Government will provide an additional $4.1 billion in premium support measures, comprising $3.4 billion in MediSave top-ups and $0.7 billion in premium subsidies over the next three years.
In addition, the total premium increase is capped at 35% and the increases will be phased evenly from April 2025 to March 2028. You can refer to the MediShield Life Information Booklet for more information on MediShield Life premiums, Government subsidies and support.
Additional Premium Support is available for Singaporeans who are unable to afford their MediShield Life premiums after premium subsidies and have limited family support. The Government will expand the eligibility criteria to cover more lower-income Singaporeans. No one will be denied coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.
Please refer to press release for more details of the MediShield Life 2024 Review premium support measures.

questions.title: What should I do with the mismatched name entries in the Record of Payment?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution will be credited to the CPF account based on the NRIC in the CPF submission.
Only for employees with ‘New’ or ‘New & Leaving’ employment status - if their submitted name is different from the name in their NRIC, a mismatched entry will be flagged out in the Record of Payment. When this happens, employers are required to check their CPF submission record:
If you have paid CPF contributions to the intended employee (i.e. NRIC submitted was correct but the name submitted does not match the NRIC name).
You should update your employee's name as shown in his/her NRIC in your next CPF submission. Kindly note that name matching is only done on the principal name, so you should not key in variants such as hanyu pinyin and aliases.
If you have paid CPF contributions to the wrong employee (i.e. the NRIC submitted was wrong).
You should submit request for adjustment or refund of CPF contributions immediately.
Any errors in CPF contributions should be rectified early while the documentary evidence is fresh. Request for refund or adjustment of CPF contributions online must be made within one year from the date of payment of the CPF. You can refer to the 'Payment Received on' field in the Record of Payment to determine the date of payment.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: I have substantial balances in my Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts. Can I use the available funds to offset my MediSave payable?
questions.text: The Ordinary, Special, or Retirement Accounts, serve different purposes from the MediSave Account. While the Ordinary and Special or Retirement Account savings are meant for retirement or housing needs, your MediSave Account savings are for your healthcare needs. Thus, the balances in your Ordinary and Special or Retirement Accounts cannot be used to settle your MediSave payable, so as not to affect your retirement adequacy.

questions.title: How do I close my CPF Investment Account under CPF Investment Scheme-Ordinary Account?
questions.text:
This FAQ applies to you if you are below age 55 and no longer hold any investments in your CPF Investment Account.
If you wish to close your CPF Investment Account, please take the following steps:
Ensure that you have no remaining investments in your CPF Investment Account. If you still hold investments and wish to sell them, please approach the relevant product providers to do so.
Contact your agent bank to close your account. Visit any branch of your agent bank and request to close your CPF Investment Account. Any late proceeds would be credited to your CPF Ordinary Account.
You can check your investment holdings in the bank statement issued by your agent bank. To find out which bank is your agent bank, please refer to the Investment Dashboard.
Please note that there is no custodian fees charged if you have no investments in your CPF Investment Account. Hence, you can choose to leave it open even when you do not have any investment holdings in the account.
If you are aged 55 and above and have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), please refer to FAQ for your options under the CPF Investment Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I provide for alternate nominee(s) who will receive my CPF monies only if my sole nominee passed away before me?
questions.text:
Under the current CPF laws, making such a nomination is not possible.
If your sole nominee had passed on before you, you can make a new nomination and nominate alternate nominee(s). We encourage CPF members to review their nominations regularly and make a new nomination whenever required.
Alternatively, to give effect to your intent, instead of nominating an individual to receive your CPF, you may wish to nominate a trust company or a trustee and set up a trust agreement to control how your CPF savings should be distributed. For more information, you can read about nominating a trust company or a trustee via this link.

questions.title: Can I nominate a trustee or a trust company to receive my CPF savings for the benefit of my nominee?
questions.text:
You can nominate a trustee (i.e. a natural person) or a trust company to receive your CPF savings as your nominee.
A trust company is a legal entity which is capable of receiving monies (including CPF savings) in its own right. As such, you can nominate a trust company to receive your CPF savings. One example of such a trust company is the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC), which can receive CPF savings as a nominee, who will then transfer these CPF savings to the trust funds set up by their clients.
Members should note that when appointing a trustee/trust company as a nominee, the trustee/trust company will receive the CPF monies in their own right.
Members would need to have a separate arrangement (such as a letter of intent or a trust deed) with the trustee/trust company on how to channel their CPF savings to benefit the intended beneficiary.
CPF Board is not in the position to enforce or ensure that the trustee/trust company will use the CPF savings for the benefit of the intended beneficiary. This is strictly a private arrangement between you and the trustee/trust company.
If you require further clarification, you can write to us for assistance.

questions.title: How do I select the correct employment status when submitting CPF contributions for my employees?
questions.text:
Select the employment status based on your employee's situation when submitting CPF contributions:
New (N)
For submitting the first CPF contribution when an employee joins your company
Existing (E)
For submitting monthly CPF contributions for current employees who have completed at least one month of employment
Left (L)
For submitting the final CPF contribution when employment ends
New & Leaving (O)
For submitting CPF contributions when employment begins and ends in the same month
Example: Employee starts on 1 March and resigns on 15 March
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.text: For details on upcoming CPE events, please refer to the Event Calendar.

questions.title: How do I find a registered Allied Health Professional?
questions.text:
You can search and view the register online via “Search for Allied Health Professionals and Providers” at AHPC’s website. Allied health professionals who are registered with the AHPC are listed online as long as they have a valid practising certificate.
A search may be done by either (i) entering the full or partial name of the allied health professional or (ii) entering his/her registration number under ‘More Search Options’.

questions.title: My PC application has been approved. How do I view and download the e-Certs?
questions.text:
You will be able to view and download the e-PC that is current and valid. Once the e-PC is no longer valid, e.g. validity of e-PC has expired, you will no longer be able to view/download it.
To view and download your valid e-PC, please follow the steps below:
Log in to the Professional Registration System (PRS)
At the left menu, click "Administration" followed by "View Certificates"
Click on the hyperlink under "PC Period"
The e-PC would then display in a pop-up window:
For most mobile device users, the e-PC should download and display automatically;
For laptop/computer uses, please follow instructions on your internet browser to view and download a copy of the e-PC.

questions.title: How long will it take for my appeal to be processed?
questions.text: Your appeal will be processed within 15 working days.

questions.title: Will the Act provide any protection for SRH staff, such as care staff and social workers who are abused by clients?
questions.text:
MSF takes the safety and well-being of our social service professionals very seriously, and we do not tolerate any forms of abuse. When our professionals face threats or harassment from clients, they should promptly report the matter to the police, MSF, as well as their employers. MSF will provide guidance and support to the affected social worker while police investigations are ongoing. If a police investigation is not initiated, MSF will provide guidance to the affected social worker on lodging a magistrate’s complaint.
Individuals who harm or hurt SRH staff can be charged under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA)’s enhanced penalties for persons who harass or abuse public service workers, as well as the Penal Code.
MSF will continue to work with SRHs to implement: (i) a supportive culture of reporting, (ii) training to manage challenging situations and deter abuse, and (iii) effective post-incident support.
topics: Social Residential Homes Act / Regulatory Scope of the Social Residential Homes Act (SRHA)

questions.title: How will I receive my payouts?
questions.text:
You will receive your payouts through your PayNow-NRIC linked account, GIRO or GovCash. You are encouraged to link your NRIC to PayNow to receive your payouts earlier.
For step-by-step guidance on setting up your PayNow-NRIC account, please visit: CPFB | What is PayNow and how do I link my NRIC to PayNow?

questions.title: Why was Medical Ethics Core points for CME implemented by SMC to renew doctors’ practising certificates?
questions.text:
In the Report on Recommendations by the MOH Workgroup to review the taking of Informed Consent and SMC Disciplinary Process published in November 2019, one of the Recommendations was to establish compulsory continuing medical education (CME) on Medical Ethics for all doctors.
The Workgroup identified the need to increase doctors’ awareness of ethical issues and developments, such as informed consent, as these developments could have a significant impact on the practice of medicine. Doctors need to be updated on ethical issues to ensure that they have the knowledge that would enable them to practise ethically and safely.
You may read the MOH Workgroup report at MOH’s website.
topics: Continuing Professional/Medical Education / Mandatory Medical Ethics CME

questions.title: I am not a registered doctor with SMC, but I graduated with a MBBS/MD qualification overseas. Can I use the ‘Dr’ title?
questions.text: You may wish to note that the title “Dr” is not restricted for use by a medical practitioner (medical doctor) only. An individual who is academically accredited, for example, a person who has obtained a PhD qualification, may also use the title of “Dr”. However, any person who misrepresents himself or herself as a medical practitioner or who attempts to practise as a medical practitioner without being registered with SMC will be in breach of the law and may face legal action.

questions.title: How do I find out the Annual Value of the property I am staying at?
questions.text: You may find out the annual value of your place of residence through the IRAS portal or through MyInfo. If you live in a HDB flat, you will likely qualify.

questions.title: What happens to my CPF savings if my nominee passes away?
questions.text:
There are two different outcomes when your nominee passes away.
#1 - If your nominee passes on BEFORE you
Your nominee’ share will be redistributed to surviving nominee(s) in the same proportion you have specified for them.
If there are no surviving nominee(s), your nomination is considered revoked, and your savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee for distribution under the intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.
We encourage CPF members to review their nominations whenever there are changes to their circumstances, such as death of nominee, and make a new CPF nomination if necessary. CPF members can consider reallocating the shares to surviving nominee(s) based on their wishes, or even include new nominees.
#2 - If your nominee passes on AFTER you
The share of CPF savings still belong to your nominee since your nominee survived you. The nominee’s share of monies would form part of his/her estate. You can also refer to the FAQ for more information.

questions.title: Why can’t I book a vaccination appointment at a polyclinic through the Health Appointment System (HAS)?
questions.text:
Polyclinics are currently not available on HAS for vaccination or consultation appointments as they use their own appointment booking systems managed by their respective healthcare clusters.
You can book appointments with polyclinics through:
NHG Cares (for NHG polyclinics)
Health Buddy (for SingHealth polyclinics)
NUHS App (for NUHS polyclinics)
HealthHub (for all clusters)
HAS is designed to help members of the public find and book subsidised vaccinations at participating CHAS GP clinics. Participation is voluntary, so not all CHAS clinics may appear on HAS.
If your preferred clinic isn’t listed, you can call them directly to check availability or to arrange for a vaccination appointment.
Do note that some clinics may require time to order in the vaccine stock if you are planning to walk in.

questions.title: How long does it take to process my application for higher CPF contribution rates for a Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR)?
questions.text:

Once the application has been processed, both the authorised representative and the SPR employee will receive a notification email at the addresses provided in the application form.

questions.title: Are the PWM wage requirements inclusive of CPF contributions?
questions.text:
The PWM wage requirements include employees’ CPF contributions, but not employers’ CPF contributions.
If the PWM monthly wage requirement is $2,500, employers may offer $2,500 in wages (inclusive of employee’s CPF contributions).
Employers cannot offer $2,000 in wages and $500 in employer CPF contributions.

questions.title: Can I help my employee save some part of their salary each month?
questions.text:
You should inform your employee to use secure methods to keep their savings, such as banks.
We also strongly suggest not to open a joint bank account with your employee. This is to protect yourself against any salary payment disputes, e.g. claims that you withdrew your employee’s money without their knowledge.

questions.title: My employer has been late in paying my salary. What can I do?
questions.text: If your employer has been late in paying your salary, you can lodge a claim or seek advice.

questions.title: What is PayNow QR payment?
questions.text:
PayNow QR payment allows you to make payments by scanning a PayNow QR code using a participating bank’s mobile banking application.
It is a quick, secure, and contactless payment method.

questions.title: Which mobile banking applications can I use for PayNow QR payment?
questions.text:
You may use mobile banking, mobile wallet, or payment application in Singapore that supports PayNow QR payments.
The availability of PayNow QR payment depends on the features and services supported by your bank or payment service provider.
For more information on PayNow QR payment support, please refer to your bank’s or payment service provider’s application.

questions.title: Will I be charged additional fees for using PayNow QR payment?
questions.text: No. There are no additional charges for using PayNow QR payment.

questions.title: What are the payment methods?
questions.text:
The following payment modes are available:
1. e-payment online (NETS or Debit/Credit Card)
2. GIRO

questions.title: How do I know if it's a cardiac arrest? What if I cause more harm than help?
questions.text: You may call 995 either using normal dialup or through the myResponder app to get in touch with our experienced operators. Our 995 operators will guide you through what to look out for and what to do. It is unlikely that you would cause more harm than good in such situations, and our 995 operators will be guiding you through the process.

questions.title: Where can I find MediShield Life claim examples?
questions.text:
For examples of MediShield Life claims, please refer to pages 29 to 31 of the MediShield Life Information Booklet.
For more information about MediShield Life, visit MOH website.

questions.title: I received a notification/ letter bearing the CPF letterhead requesting me to participate in a Member Services Survey. Is CPF Board conducting this survey?
questions.text: Yes, CPF Board is conducting the Member Services Survey from 29 April 2026 to 19 June 2026.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: What is the purpose of the Member Services Survey?
questions.text: The Member Services Survey aims to gather members' feedback on CPF Board's services to identify areas for improvement and enhance our service delivery.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Is the Member Services Survey available in languages other than English?
questions.text: Yes, the online version of the Member Services Survey is available in English and Mandarin. If you require this survey in other languages, please provide your unique login code and contact details. We will try our best to provide the survey in your preferred language.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: How will my personal data be protected in this Member Services Survey?
questions.text: All responses will be kept strictly confidential and used only for research purposes. The Member Services Survey data will be anonymised and analysed at an aggregate level. Our vendor, Blackbox Research Pte Ltd, is bound by strict data protection agreements.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Why are platform workers' CPF contribution rates being aligned with employees' rates gradually instead of immediately?
questions.text:
For platform workers born in 1995 or later, or who have opted in, the CPF contribution rate will gradually increase based on calendar year to align with employees by 2029.
For example, if you are a platform worker who opts in in 2026, you will receive the 2026 contribution rate in 2026, and it will increase gradually until 2029. You will not need to start from the 2025 rate if you opt in in 2026.
The gradual increase allows you to adjust to the new CPF contributions without a sudden reduction in take-home earnings. The transition period will also give you time to progressively adapt your monthly budgeting and financial planning, and your platform operators time for a smoother transition in their business operations as they adapt to the changes.
Find out more about the CPF contribution rates for platform workers.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why am I unable to make an appointment at the Service Centre more than 2 weeks in advance?
questions.text:
Based on our experience, the 2-week advance booking window meets the needs of most CPF members. Booking appointments too far in advance may lead to missed appointments when there are changes in members’ circumstances or needs.
With a 2-week booking window, we are better able to ensure that our customer service officers are accessible to members who need assistance.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: Can witnesses view my nomination details when I submit an online nomination?
questions.text:
No. When you submit an online nomination, your witnesses will not be able to view any of your nomination details, such as who are your nominee(s).
Witnesses will only be asked to declare that they are aware of your intention to make a nomination and specify how the request was communicated to them by you.
Your nomination details remain private and confidential to you.

questions.title: Which is religiously better? Joint Tenancy contract or the Tenancy-in-Common contract?
questions.text:
While Joint Tenancy is often recommended as a means to safeguard the interests of a family in the event of a spouse's death, there may be instances where Tenancy-in-Common could be a more just and appropriate choice.
It is important for property owners to carefully consider their personal circumstances and make an informed decision about the most suitable ownership structure.

questions.title: What is the Workfare Income Supplement scheme?
questions.text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme was introduced in 2007 as a permanent feature of Singapore's social security system. It supports lower-wage Singaporean workers, primarily those in the bottom 20% of the working population, with some assistance for those slightly above. The scheme is regularly reviewed to ensure it continues to meet the needs of Singaporeans.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What should I do if I do not have any CPF contributions payable (e.g. ceased operations or no workers temporarily)?
questions.text:
If you do not have CPF contributions payable*, you need to:
i) notify CPF Board immediately by submitting your request to us, and
ii) indicate the effective period or month(s) that you do not have CPF contributions payable.
By doing so, you can avoid any potential enforcement actions.
If you are on Electronic Standing Instruction (ESI), please also ensure that you de-activate it via CPF EZPay.
*Note: Terminating Electronic Standing Instruction (ESI) or Direct Debit Arrangement (DDA), stopping payment of CPF contributions or deleting employee records from CPF EZPay do not constitute as informing CPF Board that you do not have any CPF contributions payable.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / Updating employer's particulars

questions.title: What is the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme enhancement that applies to platform workers?
questions.text:
Eligible platform workers who are mandated or opt in to the increased CPF contributions will receive higher Workfare Income Supplement Scheme (WIS) payments matching those of employees starting from 2029, once their CPF contribution rates align fully with those of employees. They will also receive a higher proportion of WIS payments in cash from the current 10% to 40%.
All eligible platform workers will also receive WIS monthly (instead of annually) from March 2025 (for Work Year 2025 onwards). This is because platform operators will deduct CPF contributions from platform workers as they earn and submit them to CPF Board monthly starting from 2025 onwards. This includes MediSave contributions for those who do not opt in to increased CPF contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why must self-employed persons contribute to MediSave to receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
A key principle of the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme is personal responsibility in saving for future needs, with the government providing supplementary support.
Self-employed persons (SEPs) are required to contribute to their MediSave Accounts because they do not receive employer contributions. Regular Medisave contributions help ensure they have enough savings for healthcare needs, especially in old age.
To qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), SEPs must contribute to MediSave as WIS is intended to supplement both income and CPF savings for long-term financial security.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How are employees, self-employed persons and platform workers defined?
questions.text:
You may refer to the definitions of employees, self-employed persons and platform workers below.
Employee definition:
You are an employee if you are employed in Singapore under a Contract of Service (COS).
If you are employed on a contract or part-time basis, or on study, medical, or maternity leave, you are considered an employee so long as you receive a salary and CPF contributions from your employer.
Self-employed person definition:
A self-employed person (SEP) is someone who performs work for others under a Contract for Service.
You are an SEP if you own a business, work for yourself and are in the position to realise a business profit or loss. Examples of SEPs include hawkers, taxi drivers, freelancers, home business owners (such as those baking or sewing), sole proprietors or a partners in a partnership.
Visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website to read more on the definition of a SEP.
Platform worker definition:
You are a platform worker if you provide ride-hail or delivery services under a platform work agreement with a Platform Operator (PO) and receive a payment or benefit; and are under the PO’s management control while providing these services.
Platform workers who are concurrently working as employees and/or self-employed persons will also be eligible for Workfare Income Supplement if they meet the WIS eligibility criteria.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How do I cancel my Home Protection Scheme application?
questions.text:
If you have recently applied for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) cover and your application status is “Pending Processing”, write to us using your Singpass to inform us that you wish to cancel your application.
You can check your application status via “Activities”.
Find out more:

questions.title: What are the eligibility criteria of the Workfare Income Supplement scheme?
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How do eligible caregivers qualify for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
Individuals must fulfil all four criteria below to be eligible for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) as a working caregiver:
(i) their care recipients qualify for selected Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) schemes1;
(ii) they are related household members of the care recipient (i.e. related by blood or legal relations to the care recipient, and staying together at the same address);
(iii) their care recipients are not residing in nursing homes; and
(iv) they meet all other eligibility criteria for WIS, except the $500 minimum income threshold.
You are required to update your residential address in your NRIC with Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) if you are a caregiver and have recently moved in with your care recipient. If you have already done so but have yet to receive concessionary WIS payments, please contact CPF Board.
For more information on concessionary WIS, you can refer to the following FAQ.
1 The schemes from Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) are: Home Caregiving Grant, Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme, Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly, ElderFund, MediSave Care, CareShield Life, and ElderShield. These AIC schemes are for individuals who have permanent moderate to severe disabilities.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What do I need to do to receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
If you are an employee or platform worker, no action is required for you.
For employees
We will automatically assess your Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility based on the monthly gross income your employer(s) declares along with CPF contributions made.
For platform workers
We will automatically assess your WIS eligibility based on the net earnings your platform operator(s) declares in their monthly CPF submissions.
Action needed
For self-employed persons
1. Declare your Net Trade Income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS)
If you receive a notification from IRAS (via letter/form/SMS) to file your tax, or you meet the requirement to file tax (i.e. NTI above $6,000 and/or Total Income above $22,000),
File your tax return between 1 March and 18 April each year.
If you did not receive a notification from IRAS or do not meet the requirement to file tax
File your tax return to IRAS via myTax Portal between 1 March and 31 October of the following Work Year (WY).
Once IRAS finalises your income, CPF Board will receive your NTI.
2. Contribute the full required MediSave amount within the specified deadlines below to be eligible for WIS.
Your NTI for the WY determines the MediSave contribution needed to qualify for WIS. This NTI excludes any losses from previous years and net earnings from platform work, if applicable. If you have declared your income to IRAS and have not receive your MediSave contribution statement (i.e 'Notice of CPF Contributions for Self-employed Persons') from CPF Board by 31 January two years after the WY (for example, by 31 January 2026 for Work Year 2024), you may write to us to request an assessment of your WIS eligibility.
The MediSave amount required for WIS may differ from your Self-Employed Scheme (SES) contributions as SES contributions can be adjusted based on losses from the previous years or excess MediSave contributions. Any excess MediSave you contributed in previous years cannot be used to meet the current year's WIS requirement.

Alternatively, 31 December two years after the Work Year (If you are making your MediSave contributions via GIRO instalments)

Please declare your self-employed NTI to IRAS via myTax Portal to e-File your tax returns.31 December two years after the Work Year
(This deadline also applies to MediSave contributions via GIRO instalments.)
Use these tools to determine how much MediSave to contribute to qualify for WIS:
WIS e-Services: Log in to the WIS e-services with your Singpass to check your eligibility and MediSave payable.
WIS Calculator for SEPs: Estimate the amount of WIS and MediSave payable based on your income and age.
NTI is $6,000 or less
You may qualify for concessionary WIS if your NTI is less than $6,000 and you meet the relevant eligibility criteria.
While you do not need to contribute to MediSave under the SES, you must still contribute to MediSave to qualify for WIS. These contributions must be made within two years after the year you worked. For example, if you worked in 2024, you should make the required contribution by 31 December 2026.
Your MediSave contributions will be reflected in the WIS e-Services by the 9th working day of the following month.
The required contribution amount depends on your age in the year you worked. See the table below for details.

questions.title: Can I qualify for Workfare Income Supplement if I earn less than $500 per month?
questions.text:
You may qualify for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if you earn less than $500 per month or your Net Trade Income is less than $6,000, belong to one of the following groups and meet other WIS eligibility criteria:
Person with Disabilities
Comcare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance recipient
Caregiver of a care recipient. This generally includes caregivers residing with care recipients who are medically certified to have permanent moderate to severe disabilities. For more information on who are considered eligible caregivers, you can refer to this FAQ.
Self-employed persons (SEPs) must make full MediSave contributions to qualify for concessionary WIS, even if you are not required to contribute under the Self-Employed Scheme.
Your contribution amount depends on your age during the work year (see table below). You have two years to make these contributions after the work year ends. For example, if you worked in 2024, you should contribute by 31 December 2026. If you require assistance, you can write to us to assess your eligibility.

Self-employed persons (SEPs) and platform workers will receive two-thirds of the WIS payments received by employees.
If you earn $500 or more per month (in total), but work for multiple employers/platform operators and are not required to make CPF or MediSave contributions for one or more income source each, you may be eligible for WIS. You can refer to this FAQ for more information on how to receive WIS, if eligible.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: If my employer(s)/ platform operator(s) and I are not required to make CPF or MediSave contributions for my income with each employer(s)/ platform operator(s), can I still receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
If you earn less than $500 per month (in total), you must meet the eligibility criteria for concessionary Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) in order to qualify for concessionary WIS payments.
If you earn $500 or more per month (in total) but work for multiple employers/platform operators and are not required to make CPF or MediSave contributions for your income with each employer/platform operator, you may be eligible for WIS.
If you are an employee and meet all the eligibility criteria:
(i) you will be automatically assessed for WIS if your employer is making CPF contributions for you. This is when you are earning more than $50 per month with the employer.
(ii) you may write to us to assess your eligibility if you are earning $50 or less per month with an employer.
If you are a self-employed person (SEP) and meet all the eligibility criteria:
You will receive WIS payments after you have made the required MediSave contributions.
If you are a platform worker and meet all the eligibility criteria:
(i) You will be automatically assessed for WIS if your platform operator is making CPF contributions for you. This is when:
you are mandated or opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning more than $50 per month with the platform operator.
you are not opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning more than $500 per month with the platform operator.
(ii) You may write to us to assess your eligibility if:
you are mandated or opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning $50 or less per month with a platform operator.
you are not opted-in to increased CPF contributions and are earning $500 or less per month with a platform operator.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: I am an existing ElderShield insured. If I am eligible for ElderShield claims, should I claim from ElderShield or join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
If you have severe disability (i.e. unable to perform three or more Activities of Daily Living) and are an ElderShield insured, you should apply to claim under ElderShield so that you can receive your monthly claim payouts in a timely manner.
You will not be eligible for CareShield Life if you have severe disability.

questions.title: Can I use my nominee's passport number as their identification number?
questions.text:
We strongly recommend that you indicate the NRIC equivalent of your nominee’s home country. Passports can expire, and your nominees may not retain possession of their expired passports for which they will need to produce when they apply to withdraw a deceased member’s CPF savings.
Nominees may face delays in receiving the deceased member’s CPF savings if they cannot produce the relevant passport documents.

questions.title: How can I make a new nomination if I do not have Singpass?
questions.text:
We strongly encourage you to sign up for Singpass, as it allows you to transact easily with CPFB and other government agencies. You can also view and monitor your CPF nomination application online with your Singpass. To apply for Singpass, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk.
If you do not have Singpass, you can make your CPF nomination at any CPF Service Centre. Please make an appointment at least one working day in advance, as our counter services are available by appointment only. Our Customer Service Executives will act as your witnesses for your nomination.
However, if you are unable to visit our CPF Service Centres, you can contact us at 1800-227-1188 or may write to us instead.

questions.title: How can I submit a new nomination if I failed the enhanced authentication?
questions.text:
If you failed the enhanced authentication when trying to submit a new nomination, we recommend that you wait for 10 minutes before trying again.
If you are still not successful despite multiple attempts, you may visit any of the CPF Service Centres to make a nomination in person. Please make an appointment at least one working day in advance, as our counter services are available by appointment only. Our Customer Service Executives will act as your witnesses for your nomination.
However, if you are unable to visit our CPF Service Centres, you can contact us at 1800-227-1188 or write to us.

questions.title: Can I request to access a deceased member's CPF account information if he/she did not make a CPF nomination?
questions.text:
Yes. You can request to access deceased member’s CPF information even if the deceased member did not make a CPF nomination. Please note that requests should only be submitted four weeks after the death of the member.
For deceased members who did not make a CPF nomination, their CPF savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee's Office for distribution to their family member(s) in accordance with the relevant intestacy laws or inheritance certificate (for Muslims).
If deceased member is a non-Muslim
You can submit a request to access a deceased member’s CPF account information. Please note that you will need to provide the Statement of Account issued by the Public Trustee, in your request. You can approach the Public Trustee to obtain the Statement of Account.
If deceased member is a Muslim
You can submit a request to access a deceased member’s CPF account information. Please note that you will need to provide the Inheritance Certificate issued by the Syariah Court, in your request. You can approach the Syariah Court to obtain the Inheritance Certificate.

questions.title: I am a homemaker/babysitter. Can I qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement scheme?
questions.text:
Allowances received for family support roles such as babysitting or caregiving for dependants are considered transfers within the family rather than income from employment. As they are not external sources of income, they do not qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme.
The Government recognises the importance of family support roles. To support these roles, it provides assistance through schemes like the Marriage and Parenthood package which helps couples raise and care for their children.
Employees or self-employed persons who are also caregivers may qualify for concessionary WIS, even if they earn less than $500. This generally include those living with care recipients who have permanent moderate to severe disabilities. For more information, please refer to our FAQ.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How do residents in welfare homes qualify for Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text: Residents in welfare homes registered with the National Council of Social Service, Ministry of Health, or Ministry of Social and Family Development will qualify for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) if they meet all of the other WIS eligibility criteria.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Can Singapore Permanent Residents qualify for the Workfare Income Supplement scheme?
questions.text:
Only Singapore citizens are eligible for the Workfare Income Supplement scheme.
If you require financial assistance, please contact the ComCare hotline at 1800-222-0000, or email Ask_SSO@msf.gov.sg.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why are overtime pay and bonuses included in Workfare Income Supplement assessment?
