questions.title: How do I declare my annual net trade income as a self-employed person?
questions.text:
From Work Year 2023 onwards
All net trade income (NTI)1 declarations can be made with the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) by filing a tax return. There is no need to file separate declarations with CPF Board.
1NTI is your gross trade income minus all allowable business expenses, capital allowances and trade losses as determined by IRAS.
If you have earned income from more than one trade, you should declare each source of income separately when filing your tax return with IRAS. Each trade should be reported under its own appropriate nature of business category. Refer to IRAS’ step-by-step guide to declare your income(s).
When IRAS has completed the income assessment for the year, you will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons from CPF Board informing you of your MediSave payable. You will be able to view this notice on the self-employment dashboard after logging in with your Singpass.
For Work Year 2022 or earlier
If you were not issued with a Notice of Assessment by IRAS and wish to declare your NTI for work year 2022 and earlier, you can write to us using your Singpass.
If you have declared your NTI with IRAS, you do not need to declare your income again to CPF Board.

questions.title: Can I still request information regarding my CPF balances, CPF interest earned or, my CPF transaction statement after renunciation of my Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you have recently renounced your Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency, please log in to my cpf digital services while you still have access to your Singpass account. You may wish to download any CPF information you need, including your Yearly Statement of Account for the past 10 years (if applicable), and settle any outstanding matters related to your CPF account.
Please note that we do not provide CPF statements beyond the past 10 years.
Due to difficulties in authenticating a caller’s identity over the phone and email, we seek your understanding that the Board is unable to disclose any information relating to a specific CPF account over phone or email. This is for your own protection.
The Board would like to assure that your full CPF balances will be transferred to your bank account upon your request, after the closure of your CPF account.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: I am not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, how do I receive my CPF savings?
questions.text:
You will need to submit an application to receive your CPF savings if you are no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident. For details on the various application modes, please refer to this FAQ. When submitting your application, you may choose to receive your CPF monies via one of the following two options:
1. Bank transfers via Interbank GIRO (IBG) to your Singapore bank account
2. Telegraphic transfer to your bank account overseas
Please ensure that the bank accepts payment in Singapore dollars. Otherwise, we will convert the payment to US dollars. You will need to bear all bank charges, including any foreign exchange rate differences and conversion charges:
i. for telegraphic transfer to an overseas bank account
ii. if you provide insufficient bank account details resulting in an unsuccessful telegraphic transfer.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: Are CPF contributions for platform workers rounded to the nearest dollar?
questions.text:
For mandatory/opted-in platform workers
The total contributions for the calendar month should be rounded off to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents. Amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar.
The cents should always be dropped for the platform worker’s share of CPF contributions.
For not-opted-in platform workers
As there is no platform operator share of CPF contributions, the total contributions payable by platform workers for the calendar month should be rounded off to the nearest dollar. Cents should be dropped for amounts less than 50 cents. Amounts of 50 cents and above should be treated as an additional dollar.
You can use our PW CPF Contribution Calculator to calculate the CPF contributions applicable to your platform workers.

questions.title: Why are the retirement sums increasing yearly?
questions.text:
The increase in retirement sums is due to the following:
Increase in cost of living
As prices of goods and services rise over time, we will need to save more for retirement to ensure that our savings will still be sufficient to cover higher expenses in the future.
Increase in life expectancy
As people are living longer, we will need more savings to last throughout our retirement.
Increase in standard of living
As incomes increase over time, our basic retirement expectations and expenses will also naturally increase. Setting aside more savings allows us to receive higher monthly payouts to afford higher retirement expenses in future.
However, if you are already 55, the yearly increase won't affect you. The retirement sum you need to set aside depends on when you turn 55 and is fixed for the rest of your life.
It's important to keep in mind that the amount needed for retirement has increased over the years. For example, if the Full Retirement Sum had remained unchanged from $30,000 when it was first introduced in 1987 (previously known as the Minimum Sum), it would only provide a monthly payout of about $300 today. This amount would not be enough to cover daily living expenses and rent.
Overall, the goal of increasing retirement savings is to help individuals build a financial foundation that will enable them to support themselves through retirement.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What are the retirement sums - Basic Retirement Sum (BRS), Full Retirement Sum (FRS) and Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS)?
questions.text:
The CPF Retirement Sum is the principal amount1 of savings in your CPF Retirement Account (RA). The more savings you have in your RA, the higher your monthly payouts will be in retirement.
There are three Retirement Sum reference points to guide you on the Retirement Sum to set aside based on your retirement needs.
Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) provides you monthly payouts for basic living needs, excluding rental expenses2.
Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is double your BRS and is the default amount to set aside in your RA when you turn 55.
Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) is double the current year’s FRS and is the maximum amount you can top up to your RA if you are aged 55 and above. The ERS increases yearly, and topping up to the current year’s ERS allows you to get the highest CPF monthly payouts.
If you are age 55 and above, visit the Retirement Dashboard to find out whether you have set aside your FRS and the amount you can top up to your RA for higher monthly payouts.
1This includes CPF contributions, top-ups and transfers from other CPF accounts to the RA, but generally excludes government grants. Interest earned on RA savings is excluded.
2If you own a property in Singapore with remaining lease that lasts you until you are 95 or older, you may apply to withdraw RA savings down to your BRS.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What happens if I have used my CPF savings to pay for my home and do not have enough CPF savings left to set aside Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
You can set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS) with a mixture of CPF savings in your Retirement Account (RA) and CPF savings used for your property. At age 55, if your RA savings is less than your FRS, the CPF savings used for your property (including accrued interest) will automatically be counted towards meeting up to half of your FRS.
For example: John turns 55 in 2025 and has $113,000 in his RA. He had used $200,000 of his CPF for his property (including accrued interest). His FRS of $213,000 would be set aside with the $113,000 in his RA and $100,000 of the CPF used for his property.
When you sell your property, you will need to refund the CPF savings (including accrued interest) used for your property to your CPF accounts. This will be used to set aside your FRS in cash.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: Will my CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme be used to make up my Full Retirement Sum when I turn 55?
questions.text:
No, your CPF savings withdrawn under the CPF Investment Scheme will not be used to make up your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). Your FRS is made up using your Special Account (SA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings.
Find out how your FRS is set aside when you turn 55.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: How are the Basic Retirement Sum and Full Retirement Sum determined for each cohort?
questions.text:
The Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) takes reference from a person's expenditure from a lower-middle retiree household, according to the latest Household Expenditure Survey (HES). It assumes that the member owns a property that lasts him up to 95 and he does not need to pay rent in retirement.
The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) is set at two times of the BRS.
The BRS or FRS you need to set aside depends on when you turn 55 and is fixed for the rest of your life.
Find out why the retirement sums are adjusted yearly for successive cohorts.
topics: Retirement Income / Creation of Retirement Account and closure of Special Account at age 55

questions.title: What is the current Enhanced Retirement Sum?
questions.text:
The current Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) for 2026 is $440,800.
The ERS is increased yearly. For members 55 and above who wish to have higher monthly payouts in retirement, they can top up their Retirement Account up to the current ERS. To find out how much you can top up, log in to your Retirement dashboard.
From 1 January 2025, the ERS was raised to double the current year’s Full Retirement Sum to enable members to voluntarily commit more savings for even higher payouts. This allows members to get higher CPF LIFE monthly payouts of up to $3,440 for life from age 65 through CPF top-ups. Learn more about the payouts you can receive.

questions.title: How are the CPF LIFE payouts calculated?
questions.text:
CPF LIFE payouts are computed based on the following factors:
FactorHow it affects your monthly payout
Your Retirement Account (RA) balance when you join CPF LIFEYour RA savings are used to pay for the CPF LIFE premium. The higher your RA balance when you join CPF LIFE, the higher your payout will be.
When you start payouts For each year that you defer starting payouts, your payouts will increase by up to 7%.
CPF interest ratesCPF LIFE payouts factor in the CPF interest rate, with a floor of 4%, and up to 2% extra interest on the first $60,000 of your combined CPF balances.
Life expectancy / Mortality rates
Since CPF LIFE pays monthly payouts for life, longer life expectancies would result in lower monthly payouts as the payout duration is longer on average.
Hence, males receive higher payouts compared to females as they have a shorter average life expectancy.

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 65?
questions.text:
The amount of CPF savings you can withdraw from age 65 depends on your birth year and whether you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS). The withdrawal criteria differ across cohorts and generally:
You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA) savings if you have set aside your FRS, or up to $5,000 if you have not.
If you are born from 1957 onwards, you may also withdraw an additional amount from your Retirement Account (RA) savings, depending on your RA savings at age 65.
Refer to the infographic on the withdrawal criteria and an example on the additional withdrawal from RA.
You can log in to the withdrawal application form to check how much you can withdraw.

questions.title: Can I choose to receive my CPF savings partially when my CPF account is closed after my renunciation of Singapore citizenship/ permanent residency?

questions.title: Can I attend and vote at meetings for shareholders, bondholders, or unit holders under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)?
questions.text:
You can attend and vote at meetings for shareholders, bondholders, or unit holders if you hold these investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS):
Shares of Companies incorporated in Singapore (click this link to check if a company is incorporated in Singapore)
REITs
Corporate bonds
Unit trusts
If you hold shares, REITs, or corporate bonds under CPFIS, you generally do not need to inform your agent bank of your attendance. Your agent bank will automatically appoint you as a proxy to attend and vote at the meetings. You will be appointed to exercise the rights attached to the shares, REITs, or corporate bonds held by you.
However, for specific events such as schemes of arrangement, where only one proxy is allowed, you will need to pre-register your attendance with your agent bank. This ensures that you can be appointed as the proxy for these special circumstances.
If you are unable to attend the meeting, you cannot appoint a proxy to attend on your behalf. Instead, you may indicate your voting preference to your agent bank, who will vote on your behalf.
If you hold other investments like shares of foreign-incorporated companies or business trusts and wish to attend the meeting, you need to pre-register your attendance with your agent bank. Thereafter, you may attend the meeting as an observer only. However, you may indicate your voting preference to your agent bank, who will vote on your behalf.
If you hold unit trusts, you will be notified by the registrars, and you can attend the meeting directly.
Identification requirements
CPFIS investors must bring their NRIC/passport for identity verification at the registration counter(s) outside the meeting venues. Companies reserve the right to refuse admittance to their meetings if attendees' identities cannot be verified.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I withdraw from age 55 to 64?
questions.text:
You can check the CPF savings you can withdraw from age 55 by logging into your Retirement dashboard.
The amount that you can withdraw is determined as follows:
If you have set aside your Full Retirement Sum (FRS), fully in cash or with a mixture of property and cash:
You can withdraw any amount from your Ordinary Account (OA)
If you have not set aside your FRS:
You can withdraw $5,000 from your OA
Upon your withdrawal, non-withdrawable amounts in your OA may be transferred to your Retirement Account (RA) to make up your FRS. This transfer occurs with each withdrawal until you have set aside your FRS.
For example: John turned 55 in 2026 with $100,000 in his RA and $5,000 in his OA. His OA savings later grew by $2,000 from contributions and interest earned, bringing the total to $7,000. As he has not set aside his FRS of $220,400, he can only withdraw up to $5,000 from his OA. The remaining $2,000 in his OA cannot be withdrawn and will be transferred to his RA subsequently to help him set aside his FRS.
You can withdraw an additional amount of your retirement savings from 65. The amount you can withdraw depends on your birth year and generally excludes any cash top-ups, CPF transfers and government grants.

questions.title: When should I receive my CPF contributions?
questions.text:
Your employer must pay your CPF contributions for each month's wages by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Public Holiday).
Enforcement action will be taken against employers who fail to pay CPF contributions by the 14th of the following month (or the next working day if the 14th falls on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday).
Once CPFB has received the payment, the contributions will be credited to your CPF accounts within three working days, and you will be able to view the amounts through the CPF transaction history using your Singpass.
If you notice that your CPF contributions are not paid accurately or timely, you should check with your employer immediately.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions

questions.title: Why is a conveyancing lawyer required when using CPF savings to purchase a private property?
questions.text: A conveyancing lawyer is required when you would like to use your CPF savings for purchase of a private property for the first time. The lawyers would typically manage all legal aspects of your transaction, including preparing and submitting required documents needed by the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), creating and lodging a CPF charge. This legal representation protects both your CPF savings and your interests in the property, which is critical in high-value transactions such as buying a property.

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next-of-kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I apply to withdraw his CPF savings?
questions.text:
Make an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centre and bring along the following original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order;
Trust bank account statement or passbook; and
Your NRIC.
*If the original medical report has been submitted to the Court, you can retrieve a copy via IFAMS and note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on “Mental Capacity Act Application”
Click on the tab “Other Matters”
Click on “File Other Applications or Requests”
Log in via SingPass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select “File request for copy of documents” and fill up the required information.
Please ensure that you have all the necessary documents so that you can receive your loved one’s CPF savings smoothly.

questions.title: I am the appointed donee/deputy for my next-of-kin under the Mental Capacity Act. How can I apply to withdraw his CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme?
questions.text:
You may apply to withdraw your next-of-kin’s CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme by following the steps below:
Step 1: Submit online application
Complete and submit the online withdrawal application form. You can also use the same form to concurrently apply for Home Protection Scheme (HPS) and Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) benefits.
Step 2: Submit supporting documents
After submitting your online application, provide these original documents:
Medical report* from an accredited doctor stating that the member lacks mental capacity permanently;
Lasting Power of Attorney or Court Order; and
Trust bank account statement or passbook.
You can submit the documents by making an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centres or mail them to us at:
Central Provident Fund Board
Retirement Withdrawals Department
Privy Box No. 920651
Singapore 929292
*If the Court Order was applied through iFAMS, you can retrieve a copy of the medical report via iFAMS. Please note that fees may apply for the request:
Click on “Mental Capacity Act Application”
Click on the tab “Other Matters”
Click on “File Other Applications or Requests”
Log in via SingPass (when prompted) as Individuals
Select “File request for copy of documents” and fill up the required information.

questions.title: What is the voluntary top-up limit to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up is the difference between the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740 and the mandatory CPF contributions made for the calendar year.
Do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups. If the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest in the following year to your registered bank account in our records. For top-ups made on behalf of others, the excess top-up amount will be refunded directly to the recipient's registered bank account in our records.
Please keep your bank account in Account settings up to date. If your bank account details are not updated, the refund will be made to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account by default.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Is my voluntary top-up to the 3 CPF accounts reversible?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups made are irreversible.
However, if the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, any excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest. Therefore, do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones' 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
You can make a top up via Top up your 3 CPF accounts using PayNow QR1.
You will be prompted to key in your Recipient's NRIC/CPF Account Number if you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf.
All applications and payments should reach CPF Board by the last day of the calendar year for it to be counted as the year’s CPF Annual Limit. Backdating of top-ups to previous years is not allowed.
Tax relief is only applicable if you are a self employed-person with assessable net trade income for the year of assessment, when you make a self top-up or receive a top-up from another person.
You can find out more on the different voluntary top-ups.
For self-employed persons, amounts allocated to your MediSave Account from these top-ups will be used to offset your MediSave payable and meet the MediSave requirement for Workfare Income Supplement (if eligible).
1Subsequent or duplicate payments made using the same PayNow QR code will be refunded. To ensure that your cash top-ups are processed successfully, please only scan the PayNow QR code and make payment once. You will need to submit a new application each time you wish to make another top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why is there a limit set for top-up to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text: There is a limit set as the CPF system is generally meant to cater to the needs of up to 80th percentile of workers in Singapore. Higher income earners would have other means to supplement their retirement income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How long does it take to process voluntary top-ups applications to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
The application relating to voluntary top-ups to your 3 CPF accounts will be processed as stated in the table below.
Service
Processing Time
Top up your 3 CPF accounts
Almost immediately
If the top-up amount is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Can I voluntarily top-up to my Ordinary Account only?
questions.text:
Voluntary top-ups cannot be made solely to the Ordinary Account.
You can make voluntary top-ups to your:
Special / Retirement Account only under the Retirement Sum Topping Up Scheme (RSTU) (tax relief available).
MediSave Account only (tax relief available)1
3 CPF accounts2
Voluntary top-up is applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents only.
You can find out more on the different voluntary top-ups.
1For self-employed persons who wish to make a voluntary top up to MediSave Account, you must have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for your MediSave payable as a self-employed person.
2Tax relief is only applicable to self-employed persons, based on their assessable net trade income for the year of assessment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups only refunded in the following year?
questions.text:
The CPF Annual Limit (AL) consists of both the Mandatory Contribution (MC) from your employer and Voluntary Contributions (VC) paid by you, if any. You are allowed to top up VC up to the CPF Annual Limit (AL) of the year.
As the MC for December can be paid by January of the following year, any excess VC top-ups made for the preceding year can only be finalized and refunded in the following year.
If your mandatory and voluntary CPF contributions have exceeded the CPF Annual Limit during the year, you can write to us to request for refund of the excess voluntary top-ups.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: Why are the excess voluntary top-ups refunded with no interest?
questions.text: The excess voluntary top-ups can only be determined after all your mandatory contributions have been received for the year. This is usually after the month of January in the following year. The interest on the excess voluntary top-ups which should not be earned by the member will be returned to the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How can I check the status of my top-up application?
questions.text:
You may login to your CPF account and check the status of your online application under “Activities”. If your top-up application is successful, it will be reflected in your CPF accounts.
If you have made multiple top-up applications, do check the status of all your applications to see which transactions have been successfully processed and make a new application if necessary.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: My top-up via PayNow QR is not reflected in my CPF account. Why is my CPF account balance(s) not updated immediately?
questions.text:
Your top-up via PayNow QR will generally be processed immediately upon successful deduction from your bank account.
If your top-up is not reflected in your CPF accounts, please check your CPF account balance after five working days as more time may be needed to process the transaction. Such cases may arise due to intermittent network connectivity issues beyond CPF Board's control.
Please alert us immediately if your payment is still not updated in your CPF account balance after five working days.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: With the closure of my Special Account, how will the top-up to my 3 CPF accounts be allocated?
questions.text:
For CPF members aged 55 and above, the voluntary top-up to your 3 CPF accounts after the closure of the Special Account will be made to your Ordinary Account (OA), Retirement Account (RA) and MediSave Account.
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
You may refer to the CPF allocation rate table (PDF, 0.1MB) for more details.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your 3 CPF accounts to build your savings

questions.title: How do I find my downloaded CPF documents on my mobile phone or tablet?
questions.text:
When you download your CPF documents (e.g. statements) your device saves it automatically. Here's how to find it:
For iPhone or iPad:
Look for the blue "Files" app on your screen
Tap on "Files"
Tap on "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For Android phones or tablets:
Look for "My Files" or "File Manager" app
Tap to open it
Look for "Downloads"
Your CPF documents will be there
For more information, please see:
Where to find downloads on your iPhone or iPad
Where to find downloads on Android devices

questions.text:
Make an appointment to visit any of our CPF Service Centres and bring along the following original documents:

questions.title: How do I check the voluntary top-up limit to my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
When you make a cash top-up online, you will be shown the amount of top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
You can follow these steps to check how much you can top up to your 3 CPF accounts:
Go to the Top up your 3 CPF accounts form
Log in with your Singpass
Select “I wish to make a top-up to Myself” under “Recipient details”
Your top-up limit will then be displayed.
If the total mandatory CPF contributions and voluntary top-ups exceed the CPF Annual Limit in the calendar year, the excess voluntary top-ups will be refunded without interest the following year. Therefore, do remember to consider your mandatory CPF contributions which you will be receiving for the calendar year, before making voluntary top-ups.
If you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.

questions.title: What is the CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender?
questions.text:
The CPF EZPay Submission Mode Recommender is a tool designed to assist employers to easily identify a CPF EZPay submission mode that is assessed to be suitable for them.
The Recommender would recommend one of the available submission mode (i.e. CPF EZPay (Employee Database), CPF EZPay (FTP), CPF EZPay (ESI), and CPF EZPay Mobile) based on information the employer provides. Employer may find out more on the submission mode recommended to see if it meets their needs.
Regardless of the recommendation by the Recommender, employers may continue to use any of the CPF EZPay submission mode they prefer.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay

questions.title: Can my employer update my employment details with the Board on my behalf?
questions.text: No. You must submit an Update Particulars application through the Professional Registration System using your Singpass credentials to update your employment details.

questions.title: Can I pay my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium by instalments?
questions.text:
Home Protection Scheme premiums cannot be paid by instalments. The premium is structured to be paid in full at the beginning of each policy year so that the scheme remains viable and the premiums kept affordable for all insured members.
You can find out more on the available payment options.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: Can I request an extension for my Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium payment if I am facing financial difficulties?
questions.text: If you are unable to pay the outstanding Home Protection Scheme (HPS) premium within the given two months grace period due to financial difficulties and need more time for payment, you may request to extend the HPS premium payment deadline online. Your request is subject to approval.
topics: Home Ownership / Protecting against losing your home

questions.title: What are the differences between topping up my retirement savings, making a Voluntary Housing Refund, topping up my MediSave Account and topping up my 3 CPF accounts?
questions.text:
Find out the differences between the various types of top-ups in the table below:
Topping up your retirement savings
Voluntary Housing Refund
Topping up your MediSave Account
Topping up your 3 CPF accounts
Top up/refund to
Special Account (SA) for members below 55; or
Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above.
Ordinary Account (OA); and/or
RA for members 55 or above and have not met their Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in their RA.
MediSave Account (MA)
Ordinary Account (OA)
Special Account (SA) for members below 55 or Retirement Account (RA) for members 55 or above
MediSave Account (MA)
The CPF contributions allocated to the RA will be up to the Full Retirement Sum (FRS). For members who have set aside the FRS in the RA, these contributions will be channelled to the OA.
Eligibility for tax relief
You can enjoy tax relief if you made cash top-ups to yourself or your loved ones up to the current year's FRS.
However, please note that tax relief would not apply if you made a CPF transfer.
You will not be eligible for tax relief.
For non self-employed persons:
You get to enjoy tax relief for voluntary top-ups to MA.
If you are self-employed, you will enjoy tax relief on your MediSave contributions based on your annual net trade income (NTI). There will be no tax relief for your MediSave contributions if your assessed NTI for the year of assessment is zero or negative.
For non self-employed persons:
You are not eligible for tax relief
For self-employed persons who made self top-up or received a top-up:
You can enjoy tax relief based on your assessable net trade income for the year.
Top-up limit
What is the maximum amount of top-ups I can receive?
If you are below 55, you may top up your SA up to the current year's FRS.
If you are 55 or above, you may top up your RA up to the current year's Enhanced Retirement Sum.
You can check your top-up limit in your Retirement Dashboard.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
You can make a refund of any amount, capped at the full principal amount you have withdrawn for the property, along with the accrued interest.
You may check the amount that you can refund through the Home Ownership Dashboard.
Do note that after making a full voluntary housing refund of the CPF savings withdrawn and accrued interest, all CPF withdrawals including monthly housing loan instalments (if any) for the property will stop.
What is the voluntary top-up limit to my MediSave Account?
The maximum amount you can voluntarily top up to your MA is the difference between your Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) and your current MA balance. Once your BHS has been reached, no further voluntary top-ups can be made to your MA. If you exceed your BHS from the top-up, the full amount of your top-up will be refunded to you.
You can check your top-up limit with these steps.
Top-ups cannot exceed the CPF Annual Limit of $37,740, which includes your mandatory CPF contributions for the calendar year.
When you make a cash top-up online, you will be shown the amount of top-up you can receive before you reach the top-up limit.
If you are making a top-up on another person’s behalf, please check with your recipient directly on the amount he can receive.
Top-ups in excess of the recipient’s Annual Limit will be refunded.
Withdrawal
Top-ups are meant to boost your retirement income. They will be streamed out to you as monthly payouts and cannot be used for other purposes.
You can continue to use your OA savings for the current or next property after making a voluntary housing refund.
However, if you would like to use your OA for the same property, after making a voluntary refund of the full principal amount used and the accrued interest, you will need to re-apply to use your CPF savings.
After turning 55 and setting aside the FRS, you can withdraw the remaining balance in your OA in full or in part at any time.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn as cash.
From 55, you can make retirement withdrawals from your OA in full or in part, at any time for your immediate needs, provided you have set aside your FRS.
Top-ups to your SA and RA are meant to boost your retirement income while MA savings are meant for your healthcare needs and cannot be withdrawn in cash.
Application
Top-ups can be made using cash and/or CPF transfers.
How do I apply to make a top-up?
Refund can only be made via cash.
Can I voluntarily refund a portion of the CPF savings I used for my property?
Top-ups can only be made via cash.
How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones’ MediSave Account?
Top-ups can only be made via cash.
How can I top up to myself, my children or my loved ones' 3 CPF accounts?
Click this link to find out what the CPF interest rates are.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Top up your MediSave account
Growing Your Savings / Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme

questions.title: Why are platform workers not counted towards my Work Permit and S Pass quota?
questions.text:
Only Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents who are employed under a contract of service and are paid at least the Local Qualifying Salary will count towards your foreign worker quota.
Platform workers are not employees under a contract of service and are therefore not counted towards your foreign worker quota.
topics: Work passes and permits / Work passes

questions.title: How do I know if I am engaged under a contract of service or contract for service?
questions.text:
Whether you are an employee hired under a contract of service or a self-employed person (SEP) under a contract for service depends on the actual relationship between you and the company.
Employers hire employees under a contract of service, entitling them to benefits such as sick and annual leave as well as CPF contributions.
If you work as an SEP, there is no employer-employee relationship under such an arrangement. You would not be covered under the Employment Act and the Work Injury Compensation Act, and the company does not need to make CPF contributions to you.
Examples of SEPs include:
Healthcare providers on platforms like Homage
Freelancers and Independent contractors
Sole proprietors
You can also use our self-assessment tool to assess your employment status.

questions.title: Can I download or print the results from the KETs verification tool?
questions.text: You can save the results by selecting the “Save as PDF” option under Print.

questions.title: What should I do if I do not trust the doctors appointed by my employer?
questions.text: If you have a valid concern, you should lodge a case with MOM or raise this issue to the case officer who is assisting with your claims.

questions.title: I purchased an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for my employee. Can they downgrade to MediShield Life again?
questions.text: Yes, employees can choose to downgrade from their IP to MediShield Life at any time. Their MediShield cover will not be subject to further underwriting.

questions.title: My employee is currently covered under MediShield Life. What will happen to their MediShield Life cover if I buy an Integrated Shield Plan (IP) for them?
questions.text: All Integrated Shield Plans (IP) have a MediShield Life component and an additional private insurance component. Hence, your employee’s MediShield Life cover will continue when you buy them an IP. In addition, they will not have exclusions for their MediShield Life cover, even if there are exclusions for the additional private insurance component of their IP.

questions.title: What happens to the additional MediSave contribution if my employee has reached the Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS)?
questions.text:
The Basic Healthcare Sum (BHS) is adjusted yearly to ensure Singaporeans have sufficient savings to meet their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age.
Any MediSave contributions in excess of the BHS will be transferred from the MediSave Account to the other CPF accounts to help with retirement expenses.

questions.title: Is salary during an employee's notice period subject to CPF deductions?
questions.text:
Yes, Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions must be made by both employer and employee if:
The employee is working during the notice period.
The employee hasn't yet joined their new company.

questions.title: My employer hasn't paid my salary, or has made an unauthorised deduction. What can I do?
questions.text:
You should make a claim as early as possible as this will give you a higher chance of recovering the salary owed to you.
To be eligible to file a claim, you need to:
Be covered by the Employment Act.
File the claim within 1 year of the non-payment.

questions.title: If my employee has acute respiratory infection (ARI) symptoms but hasn't seen a doctor, how should I handle their absence?
questions.text:
Employees should see a doctor if they:
Are medically vulnerable (such as seniors and those with chronic medical conditions) and have ARI symptoms
Have severe, prolonged or worsening ARI symptoms
Under the Employment Act, eligible employees will be entitled to paid sick leave when they are certified unfit for work by a doctor.
As part of your talent attraction and retention strategies, you may grant paid sick leave for employees with mild acute respiratory infection (ARI) symptoms without requiring a medical certificate (MC).
In such instances, employees should maintain open communication with you and use such concessions mindfully, while ensuring that the company’s business needs are fulfilled.
If there are disputes over the period of absence, you may require your employees to produce an MC so that they can be granted paid sick leave according to the Employment Act.

questions.title: What information do I need to prepare before making an incident report to MOM?
questions.text:
The following information are required when reporting an incident to MOM:
Informant's personal particulars and organisation details, where applicable.
Accident details, e.g. when, where and how did the incident happen.
Occupational disease details.
Injured person's details, e.g. personal particulars, employment, nature of injury, insurance policy details and other pre-existing accident condition information.
topics: Workplace safety and health / WSH incident reporting

questions.title: I have outstanding MediSave payable but I am unable to contribute the full amount. Can I make a partial contribution using the Manage your MediSave Payable form (MMSP)?
questions.text: You can make contributions of any amount using the Manage your MediSave Payable (MMSP) form, if you are contributing to your MediSave monthly via an instalment plan. This enables you to shorten your instalment duration and fulfil your MediSave payable sooner by making additional contributions as and when you wish to.

questions.title: How will the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) and GRIT@Gov Programmes help fresh graduates? What are the expected outcomes of GRIT?
questions.text:
GRIT and GRIT@Gov are initiatives by Workforce Singapore (WSG) and Public Service Division (PSD) respectively that offers fresh graduates with traineeship opportunities for a period of 6 months across various sectors.
The programme supports structured traineeships for trainees to gain hands-on industry-relevant experience and skills, preparing them for successful transition into full-time employment.

questions.title: How will I receive my monthly payouts if my combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are less than the minimum sum of $350?
questions.text: You will receive monthly payouts as long as you have at least $350 in your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings. If your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: What happens if my Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted and I receive new inflows in my RA and OA?
questions.text: If you are not on CPF LIFE, your monthly payouts will stop when your combined Retirement Account (RA) and Ordinary Account (OA) savings are depleted. When you receive any new inflows in your RA or OA, your monthly payouts will automatically resume from the following month. However, if your combined RA and OA savings are less than $350, the balance will be paid to you next January (e.g., if your account balance falls below $350 in August, you will receive your payout next January).

questions.title: How do I make payment after MRI Scan?
questions.text:
You may check if your bill is ready for payment by logging into Health Buddy, Health Hub or the SGH Online Payment portal www.sgh.com.sg with your SingPass.
You will receive an SMS notifying you of your final bill 1 to 7 days after your appointment.
Visit the following URL to find out more about the different payment modes offered: https://for.sg/sgh-payment

questions.title: What are the signs of infection?
questions.text: Redness, Swelling, pain, warm to touch, pus

questions.title: How do I check the eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme for myself or my loved ones?
questions.text:
For self:
You can check your eligibility for the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) via these ways:
1. By checking your personalised Retirement Dashboard, under the “Matching grant for cash top-ups” section.
Please refer to the following illustration.
2. When you are making your cash top-up, the online application form will display information on your eligibility.
For loved ones:
When you are making a cash top-up for your loved one aged 55 and above, the online application form will display information on their MRSS eligibility and the estimated matching grant that your loved ones may receive on your intended cash top-up. If you are making a cash top-up to a loved one aged below 55, you may refer to this FAQ on how to check their eligibility.
To view details on the grant amount that you will receive at the beginning of the next year, you may log in to your Retirement Dashboard. The cash top-up online application form will also display the estimated grant on your cash top-up.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched Retirement Savings Scheme

questions.title: Why is there a need to double CareShield Life payout growth rate?
questions.text: CareShield Life works alongside other Government subsidies and grants to support long-term care costs. With rising long-term care costs, the enhancements in the payout growth rate are necessary to ensure that CareShield Life continues to meaningfully support the varied care needs of those with severe disability.

questions.title: What happens to my CareShield Life payout if I have been receiving payouts prior to 1 January 2026?
questions.text: Existing CareShield Life claimants will not be affected by the enhanced CareShield Life benefits and increased premiums, and will continue to receive their existing CareShield Life payouts for the duration of severe disability.

questions.title: Why does the CareShield Life claim threshold remain at severe disability?
questions.text:
Expanding CareShield Life coverage to those with milder forms of disability would require premiums to at least double, due to the longer claim duration and higher claim incidences for these individuals. As this would have come at the expense of premium affordability for more policyholders, the CareShield Life Council has recommended not to vary the scheme’s scope of coverage.
Importantly, the CareShield Life Council notes that those with mild or moderate disability can continue to access Government subsidies and grants that have been designed with them in mind. These include long-term care subsidies and grants such as Home Caregiving Grant that the Government will enhance progressively from 2026.
Those who wish for additional insurance coverage can also consider Supplements offered by private insurers.

questions.title: How much will my CareShield Life premiums be after the premium changes take place, and how much would it increase by?
questions.text:
With the CareShield Life premium support measures, annual CareShield Life premium increases from 2026 to 2030 will be moderated to about $38 on average, and no more than $75.
CareShield Life premiums will continue to be fully payable via MediSave, which will minimise out-of-pocket payments for policyholders.
Lower- and middle-income policyholders will have smaller CareShield Life premium increases, as they will receive means-tested premium subsidies.
Individuals may check their personalised premiums through the CareShield Life premium checker from November 2025 onwards.

questions.title: How is the Government Transitional support different from the CareShield Life premium subsidy?
questions.text: Unlike CareShield Life premium subsidies, which are means-tested and targeted at the lower- and middle-income policyholders, all policyholders who see an increase in their gross premiums will benefit from the transitional support to help manage the premium increases from the CareShield Life 2025 Review.

questions.title: Where can I get help if I cannot afford my CareShield Life premiums?
questions.text:
The Government provides means-tested premium subsidies targeted at the lower- and middle-income individuals.
Policyholders’ loved ones may also help with premium payment for policyholders through their MediSave or by topping up to the MediSave accounts of their loved ones.
For those who are unable to pay for their CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies and family support, the Government will provide Additional Premium Support, so that no one loses CareShield Life coverage due to an inability to pay their premiums.

questions.title: How will my CareShield Life Supplement premiums be affected by the CareShield Life changes?
questions.text:
CareShield Life Supplements are offered by private insurers, and CareShield Life Supplement premiums are independent of CareShield Life.
Most Supplement benefits also stack independently on top of CareShield Life benefits, and would not be affected.
Supplement policyholders may wish to contact their insurers to enquire about any potential changes or impact to their Supplement policies.

questions.title: Can I opt out of the upcoming CareShield Life enhancement?
questions.text:
Maintaining the enhancement as a standard feature for all policyholders helps keep the scheme fair and sustainable, and premiums affordable. This helps to:
Reduce adverse selection risk, where those who are more likely to claim are more likely to opt into the scheme.
Keep administrative processes simple and efficient.
Hence, the CareShield Life Council has recommended to apply the enhancements to all policyholders, striking a fair balance between stronger protection and premium affordability for all.

questions.title: Why is the enrolment criterion being reinstated for CareShield Life application?
questions.text:
When CareShield Life was launched, older Singaporeans with less severe disability were allowed to join as a time-limited concession, so that more seniors could enrol in and benefit from CareShield Life.
However, this also meant that premiums for all older Singaporeans had to be priced higher, to account for the possibility that those with milder forms of disability were more likely to join the scheme.
This concession period lasted 4 years, over twice as long as what MOH had announced when the concession was rolled out. In this time, application rates have also decreased over time.
Thus, the CareShield Life Council views that this is an appropriate juncture to reinstate the underwriting criteria, which will moderate the extent of premium increases for all older policyholders, keeping the scheme fair and sustainable.

questions.title: Who can still enroll in CareShield Life after 1 January 2026?
questions.text:
After 1 January 2026, individuals born in 1979 or earlier can still enrol into CareShield Life if they do not have any pre-existing disabilities.
All Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born in 1980 or later will continue to be automatically enrolled when they turn age 30.

questions.title: What is the CareShield Life 2025 Review about?
questions.text: On 27 August 2025, Ministry of Health announced the changes related to the CareShield Life 2025 Review. You can read more about the changes by clicking on this link.

questions.title: When will the enhancements to CareShield Life take effect?
questions.text:
The revised payouts and premiums under the CareShield Life 2025 Review will take effect from 1 January 2026.
Changes to other aspects of the scheme such as improvements in scheme administration will take place progressively.

questions.title: How do I stop monthly deductions from my CPF for my housing loan?
questions.text:
You can stop your housing monthly deduction through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Apply or Change CPF Payment for Housing Loan or Upgrading Cost
Processing Time: three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB.
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB.
If you have a bank loan
Online Application
Visit CPFB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: Select your property > Select Cease Monthly Instalment
Processing Time: generally within three working days.
In-person at CPF Service Centre
Make an appointment at any CPF Service Centre to submit your request.
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches and CPF Service Centres require prior appointments.
If you have fully redeemed your housing loan
Once HDB or your financier informs us that your housing loan has been fully redeemed, we will automatically stop your monthly deductions. There is no need to submit a request to stop the deductions.
You can confirm that the deduction has stopped by checking your Home Ownership Dashboard under “Monthly CPF deduction” section. If your housing loan has been fully redeemed this month, your monthly CPF deduction status on the dashboard will be updated next month.

questions.title: I am paying the premium for my family member's CareShield Life policy. How can I find out more information about their policy?

questions.title: Won't natural immunity be better than getting vaccinated?
questions.text:
Our immune system produces immunity following vaccination, similar to how it would after a "natural" infection.
The difference is that you do not get sick first when you get the vaccination. Vaccines help strengthen your immune system and protect you from potentially life-threatening complications.
Hence, it is highly recommended that you and your loved ones get vaccinated according to the national immunisation schedules.

questions.title: What are the recommendations for pneumococcal vaccines for adults?
questions.text:
Under the National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS), persons who are recommended to be vaccinated can either receive (i) PCV20, or (ii) PCV13 and/or PPSV23.
Persons aged 65 or above who have not received any pneumococcal vaccine can either receive:
One dose of PCV20 (regardless of age or conditions); or
One dose each of PCV13 (regardless of age) and PPSV23; PCV13 should be given first, followed by PPSV23 a year later (or at least after a minimum interval of 8 weeks) for better protection.
Persons aged 65 or above who have received PCV13 and/or PPSV23 but have not completed the recommended vaccination series can either receive:
One dose of PCV20 to complete the vaccination series; or
Complete the vaccination series using PCV13 and/or PPSV23.
If you have previously received PPSV23 before age 65 years, you are recommended to get another dose of PPSV23, at least one year after the most recent PCV13 and at least 5 years from the previous dose of PPSV23.
If you have already received PCV13 as an adult (regardless of age) and one dose of PPSV23 on or after 65 years of age, there is no further need for either of the pneumococcal vaccination.
For persons aged 18 to 64 years who are recommended for vaccination, please consult your doctor for more details on the type of pneumococcal vaccine and number of doses recommended.
Individuals should consult their doctor for vaccination advice specific to their age and medical conditions.

questions.title: What does the Varicella vaccine do?
questions.text:
The Varicella vaccine helps prevent chickenpox, a highly infectious disease caused by the Varicella-Zoster Virus (VZV).
Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral disease that spreads through direct contact, respiratory droplets, or contaminated items. It causes an itchy rash across the body (except palms and soles), fever, fatigue, loss of appetite and headache. While typically lasting a week, it can also lead to serious complications including skin, lung, blood, bone and joint infections, as well as inflammation of blood vessels and neurological tissues such as brain and spinal cord coverings.

questions.title: How many varicella vaccine doses are required, and what are the intervals?
questions.text: Two doses are recommended, given 4 to 8 weeks apart.

questions.title: How do I reschedule my appointment?
questions.text:
To cancel or reschedule your appointment, please use the unique booking link in your confirmation SMS.
There are no penalties for missing an appointment, but please inform the clinic in advance if you need to cancel or reschedule.
If you have deleted the previous appointment's confirmation SMS, you can reach out here - https://go.gov.sg/has-support to share your details so we can provide better help.

questions.title: Can I apply for loans or credit facilities after being discharged from bankruptcy?
questions.text: Yes, you can apply for loans or credit facilities after you are discharged from bankruptcy. However, you may wish to note that this is subject to the financial institution's approval.

questions.title: Where can I find a list of all law practices and lawyers in Singapore?

Please refer to the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's ("LSRA") integrated online search function, which lists all Singapore solicitors with a current practising certificate from the Supreme Court of Singapore, as well as all foreign lawyers, individuals and law practice entities registered with the LSRA.
Please note that search results are based on the data available at the time of the search.

questions.title: I have a query on CPF matters.
questions.text: Please refer to https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member for information on CPF-related matters.

questions.title: CPF Board has notified me that the deceased's un-nominated CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee but a check with the Public Trustee reveals that there are no CPF monies in the case account.
questions.text:
Upon receiving notification of the death of the CPF member, the CPF Board typically requires 17 working days to transfer the moneys to the Public Trustee.
You will only be able to submit an online application for the administration of the Deceased’s un-nominated CPF moneys after we have received the CPF moneys from the CPF Board.
Once we have received the moneys from the CPF Board, we will write to the person who had notified the CPF Board of the death of the CPF member or his next of kin, to make an online application to us to distribute the un-nominated CPF moneys.

questions.title: When will the estate monies be paid out?
questions.text: As a general rule, the monies will be distributed within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the full set of documentation or the date of receipt of the deceased's monies, whichever is later.

questions.title: What is the meaning of tenants in common?
questions.text: When a property is owned under tenants in common, the deceased's share does not automatically pass on to the surviving owner(s). The deceased's share is distributed according to the terms of the will. Where there is no will, the deceased's share will be distributed according to intestacy laws.

questions.title: Who are the beneficiaries to claim the estate or unnominated CPF monies of a deceased (non-Muslim)?
questions.text: You may refer to the rules of distribution under the Intestate Succession Act 1967 (for non-Muslims). Please see information in https://pto.mlaw.gov.sg/files/Information_Page/AnnexB_NonMuslims_Oct20.pdf.

questions.title: Does the Public Trustee assist in the administration of a deceased's share in a HDB flat?
questions.text: On a case-by-case basis, the Public Trustee does administer a deceased's share in a HDB flat if it is of small value (≤ $50,000). You will first have to submit an online application at https://go.gov.sg/pto (Deceased's Assets other than Un-nominated CPF Monies / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA) for the Public Trustee to administer the deceased's estate so that we may consider your request.

questions.title: Minor's CPF monies held in trust.
questions.text:
The Public Trustee will hold in trust, monies of minors who have yet to attain the age of majority.
The monies that is held in trust will be invested in safe financial instruments such as fixed deposits and bonds. The monies with interest earned (after deduction of the Public Trustee's administration fees) will be distributed to the minor when he / she reaches the age of majority (either 18 or 21).
Statement of Accounts for the monies held in trust by the Public trustee can be viewed online through https://go.gov.sg/pto.

questions.title: Are Podiatrists doctors?
questions.text: Podiatrists are trained foot and ankle specialists. In Singapore, we are allied health professionals, not medical doctors.

questions.title: If I do not opt in to increase my CPF contributions as a platform worker, will I be subject to the same CPF contribution rate as before 1 January 2025?
questions.text:
The maximum CPF contribution rate for platform workers who do not opt in will remain at 8% to 10.5%, depending on their age and income. They will also only need to make MediSave contribution if they earn above $500 in a month from a platform.
Some platform workers may see a difference in CPF contribution rate due to changes in the way CPF contribution is computed and collected. Before 1 January 2025, platform workers’ earnings are aggregated across platforms and assessed annually when computing the applicable MediSave contribution. From 1 January 2025, platform operators will be making CPF contribution on a monthly basis and based on earnings on each platform.
CPF contribution rates are tiered based on income – a platform worker earning below $750 will have a lower CPF contribution rate. Overall, whether platform workers’ CPF contribution rate is lower or higher as compared to today depends on their individual circumstances. For example, if platform workers have multiple income streams from different platforms, and if their income for each platform is low, platform workers will be subject to the lower CPF contribution that is now applied on a per platform basis.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Are CPF contributions payable on traineeship allowance given to your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme if you are the host company?
questions.text:
CPF contributions are not payable on traineeship allowance for your trainee under the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme so long as the trainee is not employed under a contract of service.
You and your trainee may enter into an employer-employee relationship at any time, including upon completion of the GRIT programme, in which case, CPF contributions would be payable on wages given to your employee.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / What payments attract CPF contributions

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary who is illiterate, digitally unable or has medical condition(s) and does not have Singpass to check their eligibility for Workfare Income Supplement benefits?
questions.text:
To safeguard citizens’ confidentiality, beneficiaries must check what benefits they are eligible for on the govbenefits website using their Singpass. Citizens who are illiterate or unable to use the website may seek assistance at any ServiceSG centres or community centres. However, if the beneficiary has a medical condition and is unable to do so, you can help them check their eligibility for Government benefits if you are:
aged 21 and above; and
a next-of-kin or appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), or court-appointed Deputy of the beneficiary.
To assist the beneficiary in checking their eligibility for Government Benefits, you will need to provide the following supporting documents:
If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are a parent/guardian who is helping your child, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
birth certificate of your child; or legal document to verify the guardianship between the legal guardian and child;
documentary evidence stating your child’s medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
your child’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary with medical condition(s) to provide/update their bank account details registered with the Government to receive Workfare Income Supplement?
questions.text:
The cash portion of Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) will be credited to the beneficiary’s PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account by default. If they do not have a PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account with a PayNow-GIRO-participating bank in Singapore but have provided their bank account number to the Government previously, they will receive their cash portion of WIS via bank transfer. If they do not have a bank account, the amount will be credited to them via GovCash.
If a beneficiary is unable to perform these transactions due to a medical condition, you may assist them in providing or updating their bank account details registered with the Board, if you are:
aged 21 and above; and
a next-of-kin or appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA), or court-appointed Deputy of the beneficiary.
Option 1: To update to a bank account held in trust for the beneficiary
You can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
bank book/statement reflecting that the account is held in trust for the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
Option 2: To update to a personal or joint bank account in the beneficiary’s name
If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are a parent/guardian who is helping your child, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
birth certificate of your child or legal document to verify the guardianship between the legal guardian and child;
documentary evidence stating your child’s medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
your child’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
Please note the bank account must include the beneficiary's name. This is to help the Board safeguard the beneficiary's interests. If you are unable to fulfil any of the above options, you can write to us for further advice.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary with medical condition(s) to appeal to receive Silver Support?

your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and

If you are a next-of-kin or caregiver of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, you can write to us with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
court order authorising you to perform financial transactions on behalf of the beneficiary;
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
Please note the bank account must include the beneficiary's name. This is to help the Board safeguard the beneficiary's interests. If you are unable to fulfil any of the above options, you can write to us for further advice.

questions.title: What happens to the Silver Support paid via GovCash if the beneficiary passes away?
questions.text: If the beneficiary passes away before fully using their GovCash, the remaining balance will be credited to their CPF Ordinary Account. This amount will form part of their CPF monies and will be distributed according to their CPF Nomination. If there is no CPF nomination, the CPF monies will be forwarded to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution in accordance to the intestacy or Muslim inheritance laws.

questions.title: How can I help a beneficiary who is illiterate, digitally unable or has medical condition(s) and does not have Singpass to check their eligibility for Silver Support benefits?
questions.text:
To safeguard citizens’ confidentiality, beneficiaries must check what benefits they are eligible for on the govbenefits website using their Singpass. Citizens who are illiterate or unable to use the website may seek assistance at any ServiceSG centres or community centres. However, if the beneficiary has a medical condition and is unable to do so, you can help them check their eligibility for Government benefits if you are:

documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). your NRIC; and
the beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the appointed donee under the Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
Lasting Power of Attorney of the beneficiary;
documentary evidence stating the beneficiary's medical condition (e.g. doctor's memorandum, medical report, or court order). The document(s) should be dated within the last year, unless it specifically states that the condition is permanent or if the condition is known to be permanent (e.g. physically incapacitated, autism, Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.);
your NRIC; and
beneficiary’s NRIC.
If you are the court-appointed Deputy, please contact us on govbenefits with the scanned copies of the following document(s):
