Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: What is Singpass Face Verification?
questions.text:
Singpass Face Verification is a method of verifying your identity using a face scan compared against the government's records.
Please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for more information on Singpass Face Verification.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why am I prompted for Singpass Face Verification when performing transactions using my cpf digital services?
questions.text:
This is an additional safeguard against unauthorised usage of your Singpass account on transactions that require Singpass.
Please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly for more information on Singpass Face Verification.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: Why is Singpass Face Verification failing for me?
questions.text:
There may be several possible reasons for this. For ways to improve the success of Singpass Face Verification, you should ensure that:
Your face is not covered
You keep still while scanning is in progress
Your environment is not too dark
There is no strong lighting in the background
You use a minimum resolution of two megapixels for the camera. If you are using a laptop, you may wish to try again using a mobile phone which has a better camera
If you require assistance with Singpass Face Verification, please contact the Singpass Helpdesk directly.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Protecting your CPF account

questions.title: How can I tell if the Workfare SMS I received is real?
questions.text:
Given the recent rise in scams and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received is genuinely from an official source.
As of 1 July 2024, all government SMS communications are sent under the sender ID “gov.sg”. The SMS will begin with the full name of the sending agency (e.g. “Central Provident Fund Board”) and end with “This is an automated message sent by the Singapore Government”, meaning you should not reply to the message.
This is only an example of a Workfare SMS. The actual SMS you receive may be different.
Here are some tips to help protect yourself against phishing SMSes that appear to be sent from CPF Board:
check that the SMS is sent from “gov.sg”to the mobile number registered with CPF Board. If you are unsure of whether you had registered your mobile number, log in to the CPF website with your Singpass and check your account settings.
verify that the last four characters of the masked NRIC number match your NRIC number.
We will never ask you to reply to a Workfare SMS or direct you to a non-Government website. If you receive suspicious SMS please report it at the CPF official hotline or write to us.
Be Cautious, Pay attention to scams and don't be the next victim of Fraud.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I know whether the emails I receive are genuinely sent by CPF Board?
questions.text: To ensure that an email is genuinely sent by the CPF Board, remember to always check that the sender’s email address ends with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: How do I verify that the CPF Contribution Alert email I received is legitimate?
questions.text:
The CPF Contribution Alert is a notification service to inform CPF members who are Singapore Citizens and 3rd year onwards Singapore Permanent Residents when their monthly CPF contributions are credited.
Members will receive the email notification at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address which you have earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
If you have the CPF Mobile app installed, you will be directed to view your details via the app.
To verify if the CPF Contribution Alert email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on has a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as an employee with CPF contributions
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a call claiming to be from MediShield Life. What should I do if this is a scam and my contact details are shared with external agencies?
questions.text:
The MediShield Life Team does not contact members to request sensitive personal information or engage any external agencies to call members on MediShield Life matters. The MediShield Life Team will not disclose members’ contact details to external agencies without members’ consent.
If you receive an unexpected phone call from someone who claims to be from the MediShield Life Team, please be vigilant and do not provide your sensitive personal information (E.g. Singpass ID/password, bank account or credit card details). When in doubt, you may end the conversation with the individual and check with the organisation which the caller claims to represent directly. To verify the authenticity of such calls, you can call us directly at 1800 222 3399 or write to us.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I have received a notification on topping up MediSave savings. How do I know that this notification is indeed sent by CPF Board?
questions.text:
Members will receive email notifications at the email address registered with the Board. You may check or update your email address earlier registered with us using your Singpass.
To verify if the email you received is legitimate and avoid falling prey to phishing scams,
Ensure that the sender's email address is correctly spelt and ends with "@e.cpf.gov.sg".
Ensure that the hyperlinks or links you click on have a domain ending with “.gov.sg”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Matched MediSave Scheme
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/letter claiming they are from the Household Means Eligibility System (HOMES). Are they legitimate?
questions.text:
HOMES is a Government system supporting the Silver Support (SS) Scheme in conducting household means-tests, which are used to assess a senior’s eligibility for the SS Scheme. If you or your family member had asked for a reassessment of SS eligibility, and there is a need for further clarification regarding your household information, the HOMES team may contact you via phone, email or letter to find out more on your household circumstances.
If you are unsure of the authenticity of the mobile number that you have received, please call their hotline 6818 1422 for confirmation.
If you have any query on HOMES, you may visit the HOMES website to provide your contact details and a brief description of your query.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/SMS from the CPF Board regarding my Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS). How do I know if it is legitimate?
questions.text:
We understand your concern on phishing. Given the recent rise in scam and phishing attempts, it is important to verify that the message you received on your Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) is genuine.
Remain vigilant and cautious when receiving calls/emails/messages. Government officials, including CPF Board officers, will never:
Ask you to withdraw CPF or transfer money to them (or to other persons);
Ask you to provide personal or banking IDs/passwords
Ask you to download and install non-Government mobile apps from sources other than official app stores; or
Transfer your call to SPF, except when necessary in life-threatening emergencies
If you receive such requests from anyone claiming to be a CPF Board officer, do not act on them. End the conversation, call the 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799, and inform CPF Board.
To receive notification on your PCTS, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated under Account Settings.
You can further protect yourself against scams by doing the following additional checks:
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
SMSes will only be sent from “gov.sg” to the mobile number registered with CPF Board.
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
Messages from CPF Board may contain links to the CPF website or other Government websites (NEVER to non-Government). Please check that the domain of such links end with ".gov.sg" before clicking on them. To determine if a link will lead you to a malicious website or is reliable, you can hover your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Platform Workers CPF Transition Support
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received a call/email/SMS/WhatsApp message from the CPF Board. How do I know if it is legitimate?
questions.text:
Check the source of the message
CPF Board will only contact you through these official channels:
Calls from CPF Board will only be made from 6227 1188.
SMSes will only be sent from "gov.sg" sender ID.
Sender's email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg. Check that the email address is spelt correctly.
WhatsApp sender is "CPF Board Text Us" with the blue badge. This is our official business account with the phone number 6031 5753.
CPF Board Text Us
Messages from CPF Board may contain links to the CPF website or other Government websites. Please check that the domain of such links end with ".gov.sg" before clicking on them. To determine if a link will lead you to a malicious website or is reliable, you can hover your mouse over the link to view the full address. For mobile devices, you can hold your finger down on the link so that a window pops out and shows you the full address.
Scammers may impersonate Government Officials
Be aware that scammers may impersonate CPF Board staff or Government officials and:
Cite your personal information like name or NRIC number to appear legitimate
Insist that you are involved in crimes like money laundering
Pressure you to hand over valuables like cash or gold bars for “investigation”
Instruct you not to tell anyone about the “investigation"
Government officials, including CPF Board officers, will NEVER:
Ask you to withdraw CPF or transfer money;
Ask you to disclose bank log-in details;
Ask you to install mobile apps from unofficial app stores; or
Transfer your call to Police
If you receive such requests from anyone claiming to be a CPF Board officer, do not act on them. STOP and CHECK with 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799, and inform CPF Board.
Update your Contact Details
We will send notifications to you whenever you make a transaction and may contact you to perform further verification checks on your transactions for added security. Hence, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated under Account Settings (Singpass login required).
For more information
To learn more about protecting yourself against scams, please visit the ScamShield website and find out more about the anti-scam security measures available to CPF members.
topics: Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received an anonymous call claiming that I can sign up for a new CPF Scheme that allows me to withdraw my CPF savings, and the caller offered to meet me to sign an application form. Is it a scam?
questions.text:
Yes, it is a scam. CPF Board officers will not solicit sign-ups for CPF Schemes which involve the withdrawal of CPF savings. Members who wish to perform transactions with the Board should use my cpf digital services instead.
In the unfortunate event that you fall prey to a scam, we recommend taking the following actions immediately:
Alert your bank to freeze the affected bank account.
Reset your Singpass password if you think your Singpass has been compromised. For further assistance, please contact the official Singpass helpdesk at 6335 3533.
If you are 55 and above, activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock under Account settings to disable online CPF withdrawals instantly.
File a police report and provide all details.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: I received an SMS/email informing me that I will receive CPF notifications via my Singpass registered email address and/or mobile number. Is this legitimate?
questions.text:
Your Singpass contact information was shared with us so that we can update you on your CPF matters in a timely and efficient manner. This is part of the whole of government effort to provide you with a seamless digital experience.
If you prefer us to contact you via a different email address or mobile number, you can update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account settings page with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile number or email address for verification before the changes can take effect.

The ‘gov.sg’ SMS Sender ID will be used by all Government agencies from 1 July 2024.

questions.title: Do CPF volunteers conduct house visits or door-to-door services?
questions.text: No, CPF volunteers do not make house visits or conduct door-to-door activities. All CPF Volunteering activities take place at designated venues such as community centres or official events. CPF volunteers will never approach you at your home.

questions.title: How can I verify if someone claiming to be a CPF volunteer is genuine?
questions.text:
All CPF volunteers at events carry official identification displaying CPF Board and CPF Volunteering (CPFV) logos. If someone claims to be a CPF volunteer, always ask to see their identification or contact CPF Board to verify their identity. If you have any doubts about their authenticity, do not engage with them.
CPFV lanyard and identification card:

questions.title: Should I disclose my personal details to a CPF volunteer?
questions.text:
No. Our volunteers will never ask for your personal details such as NRIC, phone number and email address. If you have account-specific queries, they are best addressed by our trained staff via our various customer service channels.
If you encounter such a situation, it is important that you report so that appropriate action can be taken.
