questions.title: What services do CPF volunteers NOT provide?
questions.text:
CPF volunteers do not:
call members
make unannounced house visits or door-to-door calls
collect money, CPF-related payments, or personal information
request personal login details and passwords
sell financial products or provide investment advice
Should you encounter any of these attempts, do not engage with them and report it via the whistleblowing form.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / CPF Volunteering
Fighting Scams / Stop and check if unsure

questions.title: Why do I need to update my registered bank account with CPF Board to my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account to make PayNow withdrawals if I have already withdrawn via PayNow previously?
questions.text:
With PayNow, you can withdraw CPF savings for immediate retirement needs from age 55 to your bank account almost instantly. As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to better safeguard CPF members against scams, to make a PayNow withdrawal, you will need to do a one-time update of your registered bank account with CPF Board to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account via Account settings. This update will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and may require enhanced authentication, similar to existing safeguards when you update your personal account details. Once your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account has been activated with CPF Board, it will be used to receive your CPF withdrawals and monthly payouts.
This update is required even if you have withdrawn via PayNow previously, as a one-time exercise to strengthen security against scams. We recognise the inconvenience but seek your understanding that this additional safeguard is necessary to provide a greater level of security to CPF members.
topics: Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: Can I make further changes to my contact details while my current request is still in the 12-hour cooling period?
questions.text:
Yes, you can submit further changes to your contact details via the Account settings page with your Singpass.
Please note that your most recent request will supersede the previous submission and the changes will take effect after the 12-hour cooling period.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: How do I update my registered bank account details with CPF Board?
questions.text:
You can update your registered bank account details with CPF Board to receive payments such as withdrawal of CPF savings and monthly payouts via my cpf digital services - Account settings with your Singpass.
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to update your registered bank account details.
To guide you on how to update your registered bank account details with CPF Board, watch the instructional video in your preferred language, or follow the steps below:
Log in to your CPF account with your Singpass.
On the website menu, click on ‘Account services’ > ‘Your account information’ > ‘Update account settings’.
Click the ‘Bank account’ tab and click ‘Update’.
For PayNow, select ‘PayNow NRIC-linked bank account’ and submit the form. The bank account will be updated after 12 hours
For Interbank GIRO, key in your bank account details and submit the form. The bank account will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the bank account belongs to you.
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: I have updated my email address/mobile number with Singpass. Why are my Singpass contact details not updated with CPF Board?
questions.text:
Updates to your Singpass mobile number and email address will not be automatically updated with the Board.
You can update your mobile number and/or email address via my cpf digital services – Account settings with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time PIN (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile or email address for verification before the changes can be submitted.
Please note that any changes to your contact details will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and you may be subject to enhanced authentication measures to verify your identity.
You can also watch the instructional video on how to update your contact details with CPF Board.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Electronic services
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: Does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit affect the total amount that I can withdraw from my CPF account?
questions.text: No, the online Daily Withdrawal Limit does not affect your total withdrawable amount. There is no change to the withdrawal rules under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: I am receiving my monthly payouts. Does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit affect my monthly payout amount?
questions.text: No, the online Daily Withdrawal Limit does not affect the monthly payout amount you are receiving. The online Daily Withdrawal Limit only applies to CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What is the Daily Withdrawal Limit for online withdrawals?
questions.text: The Daily Withdrawal Limit is a limit that all CPF members aged 55 and above can set to determine the maximum daily amount they can withdraw online. The current maximum Daily Withdrawal Limit for online withdrawals is $50,000. There is no change in the current withdrawal rules under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text: The Daily Withdrawal Limit only applies to online CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above. If you need to withdraw an amount above the maximum Daily Withdrawal Limit of $50,000, you may consider doing so online over multiple days. Alternatively, you may also wish to consider booking an appointment (Select ‘Retirement Income’ then ‘Withdrawal above maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit’) to withdraw your preferred amount in person at CPF Service Centres. Generally, the next available appointment would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings in their bank account registered with us generally within five working days. To minimise any potential delay during the withdrawal process, we encourage members intending to make large withdrawals to plan in advance.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What should I do if I need to withdraw more than the online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000?
questions.text: Withdrawal of more than $2,000 can be done by first adjusting the online Daily Withdrawal Limit to your desired amount, then wait for 12 hours for the higher limit to take effect. Find out more about this 12-hour cooling period.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What type of CPF withdrawals does the online Daily Withdrawal Limit apply to and how do I change the online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text:
The Daily Withdrawal Limit applies to online CPF lump sum withdrawals made under withdrawals for immediate needs for members aged 55 and above.
A default online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000 a day is applied to all CPF members aged 55 and above. You can adjust the online Daily Withdrawal Limit up to a maximum of $50,000, at any time under Account settings via Singpass authentication. Please note that any increase to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and may require enhanced authentication.
If you do not plan to withdraw soon, you may wish to consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock or lowering your Daily Withdrawal Limit to better safeguard your CPF savings.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Why do I need to update my contact details to adjust the online Daily Withdrawal Limit or make a CPF lump sum withdrawal?
questions.text: Notifications via SMS or email will be sent to you whenever there are adjustments to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit, or when you make a CPF lump sum withdrawal. As such, you will have to update your contact details under Account settings to receive these notifications. These notifications help provide immediate alerts and prevent any unauthorised adjustments or CPF lump sum withdrawals without your knowledge.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Can I choose to opt-out of the online Daily Withdrawal Limit?
questions.text: As part of CPF Board’s ongoing efforts to safeguard CPF members’ savings against unauthorised online withdrawals, all members aged 55 and above will be subject to the online Daily Withdrawal Limit. You can set the Daily Withdrawal Limit to your preferred amount, from $0 up to $50,000.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: Why is the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit set at $50,000?
questions.text: Since the implementation of the default online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $2,000 in November 2023, the vast majority of CPF members have maintained an online Daily Withdrawal Limit of $50,000 or less. Hence, CPF Board lowered the maximum online Daily Withdrawal Limit to $50,000 on 25 September 2024 to provide more friction against scams and introduce more time between transactions to prevent further losses, while still ensuring minimal inconvenience for the vast majority of members making legitimate withdrawals.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: How do I deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock?
questions.text:
If you would like to deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock, you may increase the online Daily Withdrawal Limit to your desired amount (up to the maximum withdrawal limit), via Account settings; which requires 12 hours to take effect and may require enhanced authentication. Thereafter, you will be able to make online CPF withdrawal applications.
Alternatively, if you wish to make a CPF withdrawal without deactivating the CPF Withdrawal Lock, you can book an appointment to visit us to withdraw your preferred amount in-person at any CPF Service Centre. Generally, the next available appointment for withdrawal transactions would be in a week’s time; subsequently, members will receive their withdrawn CPF savings generally within five working days.
Please visit the FAQ below to find out more on what is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how to activate it:
What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: How do I disable my online CPF withdrawal?
questions.text: You can activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock to instantly disable your online CPF withdrawal. This activation sets the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0. Please refer to the three simple steps to activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
topics: Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: What is the CPF Withdrawal Lock, and how can I activate it?
questions.text:
The CPF Withdrawal Lock allows members aged 55 and above to instantly disable online CPF withdrawals by setting the Daily Withdrawal Limit to $0, and is part of CPFB’s suite of anti-scam measures.
If you do not need to withdraw immediately, you may want to consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock to better safeguard your CPF savings.
You can easily activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock at any time online under Account Settings. Follow the three simple steps below.
Please visit the FAQ below to find out more on how to deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock:
How do I deactivate the CPF Withdrawal Lock?
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Protection against scams
Fighting Scams / Daily Withdrawal Limit and CPF Withdrawal Lock

questions.title: How do I apply for HDB financial assistance measures?
questions.text:
HDB has several financial assistance measures to help homeowners who have difficulties paying their monthly mortgage payments. These measures include:
Loan rescheduling to adjust payment terms
Reducing or deferring payments
Instalment plans for paying outstanding arrears
If you are having difficulty with your mortgage payments, you can get help in two ways:
Approach HDB via their Write To Us on the financial assistance measures that would work best for your situation.
Visit your local HDB Branch Office that manages your flat to speak with an officer directly about available assistance options. Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
The HDB team will provide personalised advice based on your specific financial circumstances and help you find the most suitable solution.

questions.title: What should I do to refinance the housing loan for my property?
questions.text:
To refinance your housing loan, you must authorise your lawyer to submit the online application on your behalf by signing the Letter of Authorisation, Declaration, Consent & Agreement.
Required documents:
Final or latest statement from your existing financier; and
Letter of offer from the new financier stating the type and quantum of the new loan
Important notes:
Your current CPF monthly instalment payment to the existing financier (if any) will cease upon approval of the application submitted by your lawyer.
For HDB flat owners using CPF savings:
If you are not currently covered under the Home Protection Scheme (HPS), you will need to apply for HPS after being informed that your refinancing application has been processed. Your eligibility for HPS cover is subject to approval and you being in good health. You can use your CPF savings to pay your monthly housing loan instalments while your HPS application is being processed.
If you are already insured by HPS or exempted from HPS, you can find out more below:
What will happen to my Home Protection Scheme cover if I have refinanced my housing loan?

questions.title: Why is there a refund of payment made to HDB or the bank for my housing loan instalment every month?
questions.text:
Your CPF monthly deduction for your housing loan could be more than your required monthly instalment.
We encourage you to update your housing monthly deduction amount to avoid overpaying on your monthly instalment and ensure your CPF savings continue earning interest.

questions.title: What are CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplement plans?
questions.text:
CareShield Life (CSHL) and ElderShield (ESH) Supplement plans are plans which complement basic CSHL and ESH plan by offering additional benefits, such as higher monthly payout amounts or higher disability coverage, which enhance your coverage.
Supplement plans are offered by private insurers such as Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance. You need to be an existing policyholder under CSHL or ESH to purchase Supplement plans.
There is no restriction on the number of Supplement plans one can purchase. Supplement plans can be paid using MediSave, up to a limit of $600 per calendar year per person insured. Premiums for Supplement plans range widely and are commensurate with the type of benefits they offer. You may refer to the comparison of Supplement plans for more information.
For more information on your Supplement plans, please contact your insurer or log in to your insurer's web portal:
Singlife
Address: 4 Shenton Way, #01-01, SGX Centre 2, Singapore 068807
Website: singlife.com
Email: cs_life@singlife.com
Hotline: 6827 9933
Great Eastern
Address: 1 Pickering Street #13-01, Great Eastern Centre, Singapore 048659
Website: greateasternlife.com
Email: wecare-sg@greateasternlife.com
Hotline: 1800 248 2888
Income Insurance
Address: 75 Bras Basah Road, Income Centre, Singapore 189557
Website: income.com.sg
Email: healthcare@income.com.sg
Hotline: 6788 1777
You can check your Supplement plans by following these steps:
Log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass.
Click on “CareShield Life/ElderShield” on the anchor links or scroll down to the “Supplements” section.
If you are covered under a Supplement plan, your Supplement plan insurer will be reflected.
No information will be reflected if you do not have any Supplement plan.

questions.title: How do I check the types of CareShield Life and ElderShield Supplement plans I have purchased for myself or dependants?
questions.text:
To check the types of CareShield Life (CSHL) and ElderShield (ESH) supplement plans you have purchased, please contact your insurer directly or log in to your insurer's web portal.
If you are unsure which insurer you are with, you can log in to your Healthcare dashboard using your Singpass to view your supplement plan insurer. Your dependants will need to log in to their own Healthcare dashboard to view their supplement plan insurer.

questions.title: How much CPF savings can I use to buy a property if its lease does not cover the youngest buyer to age 95?
questions.text:
You can use a pro-rated amount of your CPF savings if the property has a remaining lease of at least 20 years, even if it doesn't cover the youngest buyer until age 95.
The pro-rated amount depends on:
The age of the youngest owner
The remaining lease of the property (at least 20 years)
For instance, if two 25-year-old buyers purchase a flat with 65 years of remaining lease for $550,000, they can use up to $495,000 (90% of the purchase price) of their CPF. This is because the lease will only last until they are 90 years old.
To calculate the exact amount of CPF you can use, please refer to the CPF housing usage calculator. This tool factors in:
The owners' ages
The property's remaining lease
This policy reflects Singapore's increasing life expectancy and encourages buyers to:
Purchase properties with sufficient lease coverage
Set aside adequate CPF savings for retirement housing needs (e.g. a replacement property)
Important note: If the youngest co-owner gives up their ownership, the CPF usage limit will be recalculated based on the next youngest co-owner's age.

questions.title: What happens to my existing Supplement plan bought under ElderShield if I decided to join CareShield Life?
questions.text:
Your Supplement plan remains active as long as you continue paying its premiums and maintain coverage under CareShield Life or ElderShield. You can claim from both your Supplement plan and CareShield Life or ElderShield if you fulfil the respective claim criteria.
Since Supplement plans are administered by private insurers, any premiums you have already paid for these policies will not be considered when joining CareShield Life.
When upgrading to CareShield Life, only your paid ElderShield premiums will be taken into account when calculating your CareShield Life premiums.

questions.title: What should I consider before buying a CareShield Life or ElderShield Supplement plan?
questions.text:
If you are covered under CareShield Life or ElderShield, consider whether the current benefits suit your long-term care preferences. If you wish to have additional coverage or benefits on top of the CareShield Life or ElderShield scheme, consider purchasing a Supplement plan. You can purchase CareShield Life supplement plans immediately upon enrolling in CareShield Life - there is no waiting period required.
You may refer to a comparison of Supplement plans offered by private insurers (Singlife, Great Eastern, or Income Insurance). For more information about Supplement plans, you may consider speaking to a financial advisor from one of the private insurers.

questions.title: How do I claim from both CareShield Life or ElderShield and Supplements?
questions.text:
You may submit claims for CareShield Life or ElderShield with Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), and your Supplement plan with private insurers.
Contact your private insurer directly for claims process and payouts details:
Singlife: 6827 9933
Great Eastern: 1800 248 2888
Income Insurance: 6788 1777

questions.title: How do I inform CPF Board if I have changed my contact details?
questions.text:
Notifications will be sent to you whenever you make a transaction. Also, we may contact you to perform further verification checks on your transactions for added security. Hence, it is important to check and keep your contact details updated.
You can update your mobile number and/or email address via the Account Settings page with your Singpass. An SMS or email One-Time Password (OTP) will be sent to your new mobile or email address for verification before the changes can be submitted.
Please note that any changes to your contact details will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and you may be subject to enhanced authentication measures to verify your identity.
You can also watch the instructional video below on how to update your contact details with CPF Board.
Watch it in Chinese, Malay, Tamil
topics: Account Services / Your CPF account and personal particulars
Fighting Scams / Updating your account details

questions.title: How long does it take to process the refund of the excess payment made to HDB or the bank of my housing loan?
questions.text:
Our normal processing time for refunds of excess payments made to HDB or your bank is three to fifteen working days, depending on how the funds are transmitted.
ServiceNormal Processing Time
Process the refund of excess payment made to HDB or the bank
Within three working days if the funds and refund details are transmitted electronically
Within fifteen working days from the date we receive the cheque or cashier’s order if the funds and refund details are manually submitted to us. This includes the time needed to clear cheque or cashier’s orders.

questions.title: I have recently bought an Integrated Shield Plan. Why was there more than one deduction made from my MediSave Account this year?
questions.text:
The first deduction from your MediSave Account (MA) was for the renewal of your MediShield Life (MSHL) coverage, which is mandatory for all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.
When you purchase an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), deductions were made for your IP, which comprises both the MSHL and additional private insurance components.
Since you have paid for your MSHL renewal, you will receive a pro-rated refund of the unused MSHL premiums for the remaining policy year.
For example, your MSHL coverage period was 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2025 and the annual MSHL premium of $435 was deducted in January 2025. You subsequently purchased an IP in February 2025 with an annual premium of $1,035. After you purchase the IP, the unused premium from your MSHL coverage of $398.75, will be refunded back to your MA.
*PMI = Additional private insurance coverage portion of an Integrated Shield Plan

questions.title: What is the Trusted Contact notification service?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact notification service is a digital service that allows you to appoint a trusted individual, such as a family member to receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions and updates occur in your CPF account.
Please refer to the list of notifications that are copied to your Trusted Contact to see what information they can view.

questions.title: Why should I appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
Anyone can fall prey to scams or have their personal devices compromised by malicious software. When life gets busy, it becomes easy to overlook suspicious interactions.
By receiving a copy of your transaction notifications, your Trusted Contact provides an additional layer of scrutiny for your CPF transactions. Your Trusted Contact can spot unusual or unexpected activities that you might miss and alert you promptly, allowing for early intervention to potentially mitigate losses.
Please refer to the list of notifications that are copied to your Trusted Contact to see what information they can view.

questions.title: What can my Trusted Contact view or do?
questions.text:
Your appointed Trusted Contact will receive a copy of the notifications sent to you whenever you perform any of the following transactions and updates in your CPF account. Their role is limited to receiving a copy of your transaction notifications and alerting you when they notice any unusual or unexpected transactions or updates made in your CPF account.
Notifications from the following CPFB services are copied to your Trusted Contact via their registered email address, mobile number, and push notifications (if enabled):
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
You will continue to receive these notifications at your own registered email address and mobile number, and push notifications (if enabled).
Please note that your Trusted Contact cannot view your CPF account details beyond the information included in these notifications, make transactions, or change any account settings on your behalf.

questions.title: What information does my Trusted Contact see in the notifications copied to them?
questions.text:
Successfully appointed Trusted Contacts receive copies of the same notifications that are sent to you when transactions are made. The information in these notifications will differ for each CPF service used and transaction made.
You cannot customise the notifications or information sent to your Trusted Contacts. They will receive copies of the same notifications you receive to ensure they can effectively detect any unusual or unexpected activities in your CPF account. We recommend appointing someone you trust to help monitor important CPF transactions as an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Information included in the notifications:
CPF service Information included
CPF lump sum withdrawals for
immediate retirement needs
Transaction date, withdrawal amount, details of Bank Account used for withdrawal, reason(s) for unsuccessful withdrawal (where applicable)
Contact details update
Transaction date, Transaction time
Bank account update
Transaction number, Transaction date, Transaction time, Update option (PayNow or Interbank GIRO), details of new Bank Account
Daily withdrawal limit update
Transaction date, previous Daily Withdrawal Limit, updated Daily Withdrawal Limit
You can also view a sample of the notification content.

questions.title: Why is my appointed Trusted Contact not allowed to view my CPF account balances / statements? Why are they not allowed to transact using my CPF account?
questions.text:
As the account holder, you maintain complete control over your CPF account. This is of critical importance as your CPF account holds your retirement savings and payout arrangements.
Your Trusted Contact can only receive key transaction information through notifications to help you monitor for suspicious transactions - they cannot view your full CPF account details, make transactions, or change any account settings on your behalf. This ensures your Trusted Contact can help identify suspicious transactions while your account privacy remains protected.

questions.title: How long does a Trusted Contact appointment remain valid for?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact appointments will remain valid until either you or your appointed Trusted Contact terminates the arrangement. The CPF Board will also remove Trusted Contact appointments when either party can no longer use the service, such as upon demise.
Do note that Trusted Contact(s) you have appointed will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity.

questions.title: Will my Trusted Contact(s) be held accountable if they fail to notify me about the unusual or unexpected transactions in my CPF account?
questions.text:
Although your Trusted Contact(s) will receive a copy of your CPF transaction notifications, they cannot be held accountable if they do not alert you to unusual or unexpected activities. You remain responsible for all activities which take place through the use of your Singpass, and for managing your CPF account.
Apart from appointing a Trusted Contact, the CPF Board strongly encourages you to update your contact details so that you can be notified when transactions occur in your CPF account. You can also download CPF Mobile on your mobile device and turn on push notifications to receive alerts on transactions performed in your CPF account.

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact notification service different from CPF nomination?
questions.text:
The Trusted Contact notification service and CPF nomination are two separate CPF services:
The Trusted Contact notification service: Allows you to appoint a trusted individual such as a family member, to receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions occur in your CPF account.
A CPF nomination allows you to specify who will receive your CPF savings and the proportion of your savings each nominee will receive when you pass away.
Appointing a Trusted Contact does not affect your CPF nomination. Likewise, making a CPF nomination does not affect your Trusted Contact appointment(s) too. If you wish, you may appoint the same individual as both your nominee and your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact different from a Court-appointed Deputyship?
questions.text:
A Deputy is an individual appointed by the court to make decisions on behalf of a person who lacks mental capacity. The type of decisions a Deputy can make are specified in the Deputyship appointment court order.
In contrast, a Trusted Contact is a trusted person that a CPF member can appoint, while they have mental capacity, to receive a copy of their notifications whenever important transactions occur in their CPF account. Unlike a Deputy, a Trusted Contact is not legally empowered to make decisions on the person’s behalf.

questions.title: How is the Trusted Contact different from a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?
questions.text:
An Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) allows a person to appoint someone (Donee) to make decisions on their behalf, should they lose mental capacity in the future. A Donee can be appointed to act in the two broad areas of personal welfare and/or property and affairs matters. The LPA also gives the authority to the Donee to sign deeds on the Donor's behalf.
While both Donee and Trusted Contact appointments are initiated by the CPF member, unlike a Donee, a Trusted Contact is not legally empowered to make decisions on the person’s behalf. The Trusted Contact can only receive a copy of their appointer’s notifications whenever important transactions occur in their CPF account.
You should also consider appointing an LPA as part of your legacy planning if you have not done so already.

questions.title: What are the Trusted Contact notification service Terms and Conditions?
questions.text:
You may refer to the terms and conditions for the Trusted Contact notification service below:
Terms and Conditions.

questions.title: What happens to my Trusted Contact appointment(s) if I lose my mental capacity?
questions.text: Your Trusted Contact appointment will not be affected and remains valid even after you lose mental capacity. The CPF Board will uphold any decisions made by members prior to the loss of mental capacity.

questions.title: Can I appoint a new Trusted Contact or remove existing Trusted Contact on someone’s behalf?
questions.text:
No, Trusted Contact appointments or removal of existing Trusted Contact appointments must be made by the CPF member personally.
However, if the CPF member loses their mental capacity, their Deputy or Donee may apply to remove existing Trusted Contacts on their behalf.

questions.title: I am providing caregiving to a loved one with medical conditions. I would like to make changes to their Trusted Contact appointment(s). How can I do so?
questions.text:
Trusted Contact appointments or removal of existing Trusted Contacts must be made by the CPF member personally. Your loved one can make changes to their Trusted Contact appointment online via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form.
As a third party, you cannot make decisions concerning another member’s CPF account unless you have been legally authorised to do so.
If your loved one has lost mental capacity and you are their Deputy or Donee, you can write to us via Singpass to request the removal of appointed Trusted Contacts on their behalf, by providing the following documents:
For Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Submit the LPA document and a medical report certifying your next-of-kin’s loss of mental capacity
For Deputy appointed by the Singapore Court: Submit the Deputyship court order
If your loved one has mental capacity but you wish to act on their behalf, you will need to write to us via Singpass and furnish a court order authorising you to make such changes.

questions.title: How do I appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can easily appoint a Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You will need to log in with your Singpass to access the e-form.
You may also refer to the instructional video below on how to appoint a Trusted Contact.
Before you proceed:
Ensure that you and your appointee’s contact details registered with CPF Board are complete and up to date. You may update your contact details via Account settings before returning to this form.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission of Trusted Contact appointment.
Your appointee has seven days to respond to your Trusted Contact appointment request, after which the request will automatically expire.
If the Trusted Contact appointment request has expired, you will need to submit a new request. We strongly encourage you to personally inform your appointee about the Trusted Contact appointment request to ensure they are aware of it and understand their role as a Trusted Contact.
Steps to appoint:
Select the ‘Add a Trusted Contact’ option at Step 1 of the form.
Provide the following details of the person you wish to appoint:
Full name (as per NRIC)
NRIC number
Relationship to you
Review your input before submitting the e-form.
What happens next:
Both you and your Trusted Contact appointee will be notified upon successful submission. The Trusted Contact appointment will only take effect once your appointee accepts the request. Please remind your appointee to accept your Trusted Contact appointment request within seven days of submission. You may go to the Activities page to view the status of your request.
Once your Trusted Contact appointment request has been accepted, your Trusted Contact will receive a copy of your notifications whenever important transactions occur in your CPF account.

questions.title: Who can appoint a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can appoint a Trusted Contact if you are:
A CPF member aged 21 and above; and
A Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have at least a Singapore-registered mobile number or email address registered with CPF Board.

questions.title: Why do I need to maintain contact details to use the Trusted Contact notification service?
questions.text:
You will receive SMS and email notifications whenever there are changes to the status of your Trusted Contact appointment. To ensure you receive these alerts and can detect any unauthorised modifications, you need to register or update your contact details under Account settings.
Keeping your contact details up to date is crucial for your account security, as it ensures you receive timely notifications for your account activities. Regularly reviewing your contact details, especially after changing phone numbers or email addresses, helps maintain your account security.

questions.title: Who can I appoint as my Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You should only appoint someone you trust, such as a family member, to help monitor important CPF transactions as an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Your Trusted Contact must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 and above;
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board.

questions.title: Is there a limit to the number of Trusted Contacts I can appoint? How many Trusted Contacts can I appoint?
questions.text: You may appoint up to two individuals as your Trusted Contacts. Both Trusted Contacts will have the same role and responsibilities with no primary or secondary designation. If you wish to appoint a new Trusted Contact but have already reached the limit, you must first remove one of your existing Trusted Contacts or withdraw one of your pending appointment requests.

questions.title: Why am I not allowed to appoint more than two Trusted Contacts?
questions.text: Your Trusted Contacts help to protect your CPF account by helping to detect any unexpected activity in your CPF account. The two-person limit is designed to provide optimal protection from potential scams while keeping your CPF information within a close, trusted circle. We encourage you to carefully select your most reliable and trusted contacts, ensuring focused and effective monitoring of your CPF transactions for suspicious activities.

questions.title: Can I appoint someone who is not my next-of-kin to be my Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can appoint a person who is not your next-of-kin to be your Trusted Contact. We highly recommend that you carefully review and only choose someone you trust, as they will help monitor important CPF transactions and provide an additional layer of security against potential scams.
Do note that your appointee will also need to accept the appointment before they become your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: Can I appoint a Trusted Contact who is not based in Singapore?
questions.text:
You may appoint a person who is not based in Singapore as your Trusted Contact as long as they meet the eligibility criteria.
Your Trusted Contact must:
be a CPF member aged 21 and above;
be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board

questions.title: Can I submit more than one Trusted Contact appointment request within the same day?
questions.text:
Yes, you can submit up to two Trusted Contact appointment requests within the same day, which is the maximum number of Trusted Contacts you can appoint.
If you wish to submit a new Trusted Contact appointment request when you already have reached the maximum of two Trusted Contacts, you must first withdraw one of your pending requests or remove an existing Trusted Contact, before submitting a new appointment request.

questions.title: Why do I need my appointee to accept the Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text: A Trusted Contact will receive copies of your notifications when you make important transactions and updates in your CPF account. As the role of Trusted Contact is a voluntary one, your appointee must understand their role before accepting your appointment request.

questions.title: I have submitted my Trusted Contact appointment request. How will my appointee be informed to accept my appointment request?
questions.text: Notifications will be sent to your appointee via email, SMS and push notifications via the CPF Mobile app (if enabled) to inform them of your appointment request. While CPF Board will notify your appointee, we strongly encourage you to personally inform them of your appointment request beforehand. This helps to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: How long does my appointee have to accept my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
Your appointee has seven days to respond to your Trusted Contact appointment request, after which the request will automatically expire. If the request has expired, you will need to submit a new appointment request.
We strongly encourage you to personally inform the appointee about the appointment request to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: Where can I see an overview of my Trusted Contact appointment and appointment requests?
questions.text:
You may view your appointed Trusted Contacts at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Only Trusted Contacts who have accepted your appointment request will be listed under “Your Trusted Contacts”. For pending appointment requests, you may track the status via your Activities page. Pending requests have the “In-Progress” transaction status.
If someone has appointed you as their Trusted Contacts, you will be able to see the pending request(s) under “Added you as a Trusted Contact” in the Account settings – Trusted Contacts section.

questions.title: What should I do if I wish to amend my Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text:
If your Trusted Contact appointee has not accepted your request and you wish to change the appointee, you can do so by withdrawing your appointment request and submitting a new one.
To withdraw the request:
Go to your Activities page and locate the pending request that you wish to withdraw. The “Add or remove Trusted Contact” transaction should still be “In-Progress”.
Click into the “In-progress” transaction record and click the “Withdraw this request” button at the bottom of the page.
If your Trusted Contact request has been accepted, you will not be able to withdraw your appointment. Instead, you will need to remove the existing Trusted Contact appointment first. You may do so via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form before submitting a new appointment request. Your Trusted Contact will be notified of the changes.

questions.title: I received a notification informing me that my Trusted Contact appointment was declined. What should I do?
questions.text:
The notification was sent to inform you that the person you had tried to appoint as your Trusted Contact has declined your appointment request. You should try to contact your appointee to explain your request and help them understand their role as your Trusted Contact before submitting a new appointment request.
Alternatively, you may consider choosing a different person to appoint as your Trusted Contact. We strongly encourage you to personally inform them of your appointment request beforehand. This helps to ensure that they are aware of the appointment request and understand their role as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I received a notification stating my Trusted Contact appointment request has expired. What should I do?
questions.text:
The notification was sent to inform you that the person you had tried to appoint as your Trusted Contact did not respond to your appointment request within seven days of your submission.
Your appointee must agree to be your Trusted Contact by accepting your appointment request at the “Trusted Contact” section under their Account settings via Singpass login. The Trusted Contact appointment will only take effect once your appointee has accepted the Trusted Contact appointment request.
If you wish to appoint the same person as your Trusted Contact, you should personally inform them before resubmitting your appointment request, so that they can respond promptly. You will receive a notification when your appointee accepts the Trusted Contact appointment request to be your Trusted Contact.
Alternatively, you may consider choosing a different person to appoint as your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the name I keyed for my appointee was different from his NRIC/CPF Account Number. How can I resolve this?
questions.text:
You should key in the full name of your appointee as per his NRIC. This includes any punctuation such as the comma (,), hyphen (-), and slash (/).
However, you should exclude the Hanyu Pinyin, Alias and Married name. See examples of NRIC names.
If you are still encountering problems in submitting your Trusted Contact appointment request, we recommend that you check the following:
Check for the correct spacing of characters in the names of your appointee.
For example:
John⎵Tan should not be written as John⎵⎵Tan or John⎵Tan⎵
D/O should not be written as D / O, and likewise for S/O
Avoid copy-pasting the details from another program or app as there might be hidden characters that might get copied. Key in the appointee’s particulars manually instead.
If you are using an iOS device (such as iPhone or iPad), disable the “Smart Punctuation” feature in iOS (iOS device Settings > General > Keyboard > Turn off Smart Punctuation). This feature might create unrecognisable characters in the application form.
Avoid opening multiple browser tabs. Use only one browser tab and clear your browser cache.
Consider using a different device to submit your Trusted Contact appointment request if submission via your original device is still unsuccessful.
If you continue to encounter the same error despite the above, you can write to us via Singpass with the following details for assistance:
A screenshot of the name of your appointee,
The time and date when the error occurred, and
Details of the device that you are using to submit your Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact has reached their appointment limit. What should I do?
questions.text: The person you are trying to appoint is already a Trusted Contact of several other individuals. We recommend appointing someone else for better monitoring of your important CPF transactions or updates. If you still prefer to appoint this person, you can ask them to remove one of their existing appointments. However, do consider that spreading their attention across multiple members might affect their focus and effectiveness in spotting suspicious activities promptly.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact cannot be appointed because their contact details are incomplete. What should I do?
questions.text:
To better safeguard you from potential scams, your Trusted Contact must have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and an email address registered with CPF Board, as they will receive a copy of your transaction notifications whenever important CPF transactions or updates are made in your CPF account.
You should inform the person you are trying to appoint to update their contact details with CPF Board. If this is not possible, you should consider appointing a different person as your Trusted Contact instead.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that the person I intend to appoint as my Trusted Contact is not eligible. What should I do?
questions.text:
The person you are trying to appoint as your Trusted Contact is not eligible to use the service.
Your Trusted Contact must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 and above
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board
Please consider appointing a different person as your Trusted Contact instead.

questions.title: Why do I need to provide the Name and NRIC number of my appointee in the Trusted Contact appointment form?
questions.text: Providing the Name and NRIC number of your appointee helps CPF Board correctly identify the person you wish to appoint as your Trusted Contact. CPF Board will also check if your appointee is eligible to be a Trusted Contact.

questions.title: How can I make a Trusted Contact appointment if I failed the enhanced authentication verification?
questions.text:
If you failed the enhanced authentication when trying to submit a Trusted Contact appointment request, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre with your intended appointee for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: My appointed Trusted Contact is not receiving a copy of my notification when I perform CPF transactions. Why is this so?
questions.text:
The Trusted Contact service only sends notifications to your Trusted Contact for transactions below:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
If your Trusted Contact did not receive a notification, it may be because the transaction you performed is not covered by the Trusted Contact service.
However, if your Trusted Contact is not receiving notifications for any of the above transactions, please write to us via Singpass with the following details:
Name of your Trusted Contact
The type of transaction you performed, including the time and date
Screenshot of the notifications sent to you

questions.title: How do I remove my appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can easily remove a Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You will need to login with your Singpass when you begin the e-form.
Before you proceed:
Verify that your contact details registered with CPF Board are correct. If you need to update your contact details, you can do so via Account settings before returning to this form.
Steps to remove:
To remove a Trusted Contact, select the ‘Remove a Trusted Contact’ option at Step 1 of the form.
Next, select the Trusted Contact you wish to remove.
Review your input before submitting the form.
What happens next:
The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect.
Notifications will be sent to both you and the Trusted Contact you have removed.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that I cannot remove my appointed Trusted Contact because their contact details are incomplete. What should I do?
questions.text:
Please inform the person you are trying to remove as your Trusted Contact to register both a Singapore-registered mobile number and an email address with CPF Board. Once your Trusted Contact has successfully updated their contact details, you may proceed to remove the Trusted Contact via the e-form.
If this is not possible, you may write to us via Singpass with the following details:
A screenshot of the error page,
The name and NRIC number of the Trusted Contact you wish to remove
You may also visit any CPF Service Centre to remove the Trusted Contact in person. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre, as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: How long does it take to remove an appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text: The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect upon the successful submission of the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to remove an appointed Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your Trusted Contact removal application via your Activities page using your Singpass.
The removal of your Trusted Contact will take immediate effect upon successful submission of the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form. You may also refer to the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings and check that the Trusted Contact you have removed is not shown under “Your Trusted Contacts”.

questions.title: How can I remove a Trusted Contact appointment if I failed the enhanced authentication?
questions.text:
If you fail the enhanced authentication when trying to remove a Trusted Contact, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: I did not perform any removal for my Trusted Contact appointment. Why was my Trusted Contact appointment / appointment as a Trusted Contact removed by CPF Board?
questions.text: The CPF Board may remove your appointed Trusted Contact or your appointment as a Trusted Contact when either you or your Trusted Contact are no longer eligible to use the service. You are advised to check with your appointer or your Trusted Contact if there has been a change in their circumstances affecting their eligibility. You may refer to our FAQs on Member eligibility and Trusted Contact eligibility for more information.

questions.title: What happens to my Trusted Contact appointment(s) upon my demise?
questions.text: CPF Board will revoke your appointed Trusted Contact(s) as well as your appointment(s) as a Trusted Contact upon your demise.

questions.title: I am a deputy/donee for a CPF member. How can I remove their Trusted Contact appointment(s)?
questions.text:
As a deputy/donee, you can write to us via Singpass to request the removal of Trusted Contact on a member’s behalf, by providing the following documents:
For Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA): Submit the LPA document and a medical report certifying your donor’s loss of mental capacity
For Deputy appointed by the Singapore Court: Submit the Deputyship court order

questions.title: What happens if my appointed Trusted Contact loses their mental capacity?
questions.text:
You should revoke their Trusted Contact appointment via the Add or remove Trusted Contact e-form when your appointed Trusted Contact loses their mental capacity.
You may also wish to submit a new appointment request to appoint a different person to be your Trusted Contact.

questions.title: What is my role as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
As an appointed Trusted Contact, you play a role in helping to protect your appointer from potential scams. You will receive a copy of the notifications sent to your appointer when important transactions and updates occur in their CPF account. By monitoring these notifications, you can help to spot and alert them to any suspicious activities in their CPF account that may not be performed by them.
Notifications from the following CPF services will be copied to you when triggered by transactions in your appointer’s CPF account:
CPF lump sum withdrawals for immediate retirement needs
Contact details update
Bank account update
Daily withdrawal limit update
Your appointer will still receive notifications at their own registered contact.
It is important to note that as a Trusted Contact, you cannot transact or make changes to your appointer’s CPF account on their behalf as your appointer has sole control of their CPF account. Your role is limited to receiving a copy of their transaction notifications and alerting your appointer when you notice any unusual or unexpected transactions or updates made in their CPF account. Learn how to differentiate notifications you receive as a Trusted Contact from notifications meant for your own CPF account.

questions.title: I am a Trusted Contact. Why am I not allowed to transact on my appointer’s behalf or view the CPF account balances and statements?
questions.text:
As a Trusted Contact, you serve as an extra pair of eyes to help safeguard your appointer from potential scams. To meet this objective, you will receive a copy of the notifications whenever important transactions occur in your appointer’s CPF account.
We strike a balance between enabling you to support your appointer and protecting their privacy. You can only receive key transaction information through notifications to help you monitor for suspicious transactions - you cannot view your appointer's full CPF account details, make transactions, or change any account settings on their behalf. This ensures you can help identify suspicious transactions while your appointer's account privacy remains protected.

questions.title: How can I differentiate the notifications I receive as a Trusted Contact from notifications for my own CPF account?
questions.text:
You can look out for the label in the notifications sent to you:
SMS Notifications: Begins with “(To Trusted Contact)”
Email: Contains “You are receiving this notification as an appointed Trusted Contact”
Push Notifications via CPF Mobile app (if enabled): Contains “You are receiving this notification as an appointed Trusted Contact of <Name of your appointer>”

questions.title: How do I become a Trusted Contact for a loved one?
questions.text:
Your loved one can appoint you as their Trusted Contact via the Add or remove Trusted Contact
e-form. They will need to login with their Singpass when they begin the e-form.
To be a Trusted Contact, you must:
Be a CPF member aged 21 or above; and
Be a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident (with Singpass account); and
Have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board.
Before accepting the role of a Trusted Contact, please review the Terms and Conditions of the Trusted Contact service and understand the role of a Trusted Contact. Please refer to the Trusted Contact information page for more details.

questions.title: Why do I need to have both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address registered with CPF Board to be a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
As an appointed Trusted Contact, you play an important role in helping to protect your appointer from potential scams. You will receive a copy of the notifications sent to your appointer when they make important transactions and updates to their CPF account.
It is crucial for Trusted Contacts to spot and flag any unusual or unexpected activities in your appointer’s CPF account. As such, you would need to maintain both a Singapore-registered mobile number and email address with CPF Board, so that you can receive your appointers’ notifications via both channels and take timely action.

questions.title: I received a notification informing me of a Trusted Contact appointment request. What should I do?
questions.text:
Someone has requested you to be their Trusted Contact. Please verify that this appointment was correctly made by checking the requestor’s name.
You can accept or decline the appointment request at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings. Please note that the Trusted Contact appointment request will expire seven days after your appointer made the request, after which you will no longer be able to accept or decline it. Your appointer will be notified after you accept or decline the Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: A loved one has appointed me as their Trusted Contact. How do I accept?
questions.text:
You can accept the appointment request under “Added you as a Trusted Contact” in the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.
You may also refer to the instructional video below on how to accept a Trusted Contact request.

questions.title: An unknown party has appointed me as their Trusted Contact. What should I do?
questions.text: If you have received a Trusted Contact appointment request from a person not known to you, you can decline the request at the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.

questions.title: Can I be a Trusted Contact for someone who is not my next-of-kin?
questions.text: Yes. You can be the Trusted Contact for someone who is not your next-of-kin if they appoint you. You must also meet these eligibility criteria to be a Trusted Contact.

questions.title: I received a notification informing me that a pending Trusted Contact appointment request has been withdrawn. What should I do?
questions.text: No further action is required from you as the pending appointment request has been withdrawn by the appointer.

questions.title: Will the appointer be informed when I accept or decline their Trusted Contact appointment request?
questions.text: Yes, the person who has appointed you as their Trusted Contact will be notified via email, SMS and push notifications (if enabled) when you accept or decline their Trusted Contact appointment request.

questions.title: I am the appointed Trusted Contact of someone who has lost their mental capacity. Will my appointment as the Trusted Contact be affected?
questions.text:
If a person who appointed you loses their mental capacity, your appointment as their Trusted Contact will not be affected and remains valid.
A Court-appointed Deputy or Donee appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) are legally empowered to manage the affairs of your appointer (who has lost his mental capacity). They may remove you as the Trusted Contact if they deem it necessary and you will be informed accordingly. If you wish to remove yourself from the Trusted Contact’s list, you may do so via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form.

questions.title: I no longer wish to be appointed as a Trusted Contact. How do I remove my appointment?
questions.text:
You can easily remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form. You will need to login with your Singpass when you begin the e-form.
Before you proceed:
Verify that your contact details registered with CPF Board are correct. If you need to update your contact details, you can do so via Account settings before returning to this form.
How to remove yourself as Trusted Contact:
Select the person from whose Trusted Contact list you wish to remove yourself.
Review your selection before submitting the form.
What happens next:
The removal will take immediate effect after successful submission.
Both you and your appointer (from whom you have removed your appointment as Trusted Contact) will be notified.
Important notes:
You may need to verify your identity using enhanced authentication measures to complete the submission.

questions.title: I encountered an error informing me that I cannot remove my appointment as Trusted Contact because my appointer’s contact details are incomplete. Can CPF Board assist to remove my appointment?
questions.text:
Please inform your appointer to update their contact details with CPF Board. Once your appointer has successfully updated their contact details, you may proceed to remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form.
If this is not possible, you may write to us via Singpass with the following details:
A screenshot of the error page,
The name and NRIC number of the appointer you wish to remove
You may also visit any CPF Service Centre to remove your Trusted Contact appointment in person. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: How long does it take to remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text: You will be removed as a Trusted Contact with immediate effect upon a successful submission.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my application to remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your application to remove your appointment as a Trusted Contact via your Activities page using your Singpass.
Upon successful submission of the Remove yourself from your appointer's Trusted Contact list e-form, your name will be removed from the “Trusted Contacts” section under your Account settings.

questions.title: How can I remove my appointment as a Trusted Contact if I failed the enhanced authentication?
questions.text:
If you failed the enhanced authentication when trying to remove yourself as a Trusted Contact, please try again later.
Otherwise, you may visit any CPF Service Centre for assistance. Please schedule a visit to any CPF Service Centre as counter services are available by booking only.

questions.title: As a Trusted Contact, what should I do upon receiving notifications regarding transactions on my appointer’s CPF account?
questions.text:
As a Trusted Contact, you will receive copies of your appointer’s notifications whenever important transactions occur in your appointer’s CPF account. When you receive these notifications, check with your appointer to confirm they made the transaction.
If unsure whether your appointer may have fallen for a scam, STOP and CHECK with 24/7 ScamShield anti-scam helpline via 1799. To learn more about common scam signs and scam types, please visit the ScamShield website.
If your appointer has fallen victim to a scam, advise or guide them to take the following steps immediately:
Alert the bank to freeze any affected bank account(s)
Call Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533 to reset their Singpass
Activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock to disable online CPF withdrawals (applicable for members aged 55 and above)
Lodge a police report and inform CPF Board

questions.title: Why is the Trusted Contact notified when the appointer makes a withdrawal transaction?
questions.text:
Scammers may deceive victims into withdrawing their CPF savings or attempt to withdraw victims’ CPF savings if they obtain unauthorised access to the victims’ CPF accounts. Therefore, it is crucial for Trusted Contacts to be alerted when such a transaction is made.
Learn more about scammers’ latest tactics, and tips to help your loved ones safeguard themselves against scams.

questions.title: Why is the Trusted Contact notified when the appointer updates their bank account, contact details or daily withdrawal limit?
questions.text:
Scammers may deceive victims into updating their bank account, contact details or daily withdrawal limit. They may also attempt to update this information if they obtain unauthorised access to the victims’ CPF accounts. Therefore, it is crucial for Trusted Contacts to be alerted when such transactions are made.
Learn more about scammers’ latest tactics and tips to help your loved ones safeguard themselves against scams.

questions.title: Can CPF Board notify Trusted Contacts about other types of transactions made by their appointers?
questions.text: Only notifications for critical transactions or updates that may expose an account to higher scam risk (e.g. when a withdrawal is made, or when bank account information is changed) are copied to Trusted Contacts. This avoids overwhelming Trusted Contacts with less critical notifications regarding their appointer’s account.

questions.title: What is the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
CPF Safety Switch is a security feature that allows you to immediately secure your CPF account if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam.
Upon activation, the CPF Safety Switch will stop in-progress withdrawals meant to be credited to your Registered Bank Account, and prevent any future withdrawals from your CPF account, while disabling access to CPF online services through the CPF website and mobile app.

questions.title: When should I activate CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text: Please activate the CPF Safety Switch only if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam. Activating the CPF Safety Switch will stop in-progress withdrawals meant to be credited to your Registered Bank Account, and disables online access to your CPF account. This would help to mitigate monetary losses and safeguard your personal data. Do note that deactivation of Safety Switch will take around three to five working days.

questions.title: I am not a scam victim. Should I still activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You should only activate the CPF Safety Switch if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam.
If you wish to protect yourself against scams and do not need to withdraw immediately, consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock instead. Activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock will maintain your online access to your CPF account while disabling online CPF withdrawals. Find out more about the CPF Withdrawal Lock.

questions.title: Who can activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text: The CPF Safety Switch is available to members aged 55 and above, as it is meant to help members who are eligible to withdraw their CPF savings safeguard their CPF savings when they suspect they have fallen victim to a scam.

questions.title: How do I activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You may activate the CPF Safety Switch by calling the CPF hotline at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) and selecting option ‘8’ after choosing your preferred language.
Should you require any assistance in activating the CPF Safety Switch, you may make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours.
Please note that we will require members to verify their identity before activation.

questions.title: What transactions/services are affected when the CPF Safety Switch is activated?
questions.text:
While the CPF Safety Switch is active:
Access to your CPF online services will be disabled
All in-progress withdrawals will be stopped, and you will not be able to make any further withdrawals
Disbursements to your registered bank account will be stopped
You can only obtain information related to your CPF account at CPF Service Centre
Please note that CPF contributions and recurring payments to third-party organisations will not be affected by the CPF Safety Switch. In order to regain access to these services, find out more about deactivating the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: How do I know if my CPF Safety Switch activation request is successful?
questions.text:
You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you of the outcome of your activation request. Note that we will not be able to reach you if you have no registered contact details with us.
If you wish to update your contact details, you may do so via the Account settings page on CPF website, before activating CPF Safety Switch.
SMS notifications from CPF Board will only be sent from the “gov.sg” sender ID, and the email address will end with @cpf.gov.sg or @e.cpf.gov.sg.
After CPF Safety Switch has been activated, you will not be able to log in to your CPF account.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, activate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No, the CPF Safety Switch requires members to verify their identity before activation. CPF Board staff may also contact members via their registered contact details by the next working day to better understand their situation and provide further support as required.

questions.title: Is there a time limit for how long the CPF Safety Switch remains active?
questions.text:
No. The CPF Safety Switch will remain activated until we receive your instruction to deactivate it.
However, we recommend that you deactivate the CPF Safety Switch after you have performed the necessary actions to secure your CPF account. We will send periodic email and SMS reminders to members who may have forgotten to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.

questions.title: How do I deactivate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
You may request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch through one of the following methods:
Call the CPF hotline at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) and select option ‘8’ after choosing your language during operating hours
Make an appointment to visit any of the CPF Service Centres during operating hours
Note that your deactivation request will take around three to five working days to process, after we successfully verify your identity.

questions.title: How do I know if my deactivation request is successful?
questions.text: You will receive an email and SMS to your registered contact details notifying you once your deactivation request is successful. Generally, this may take three to five working days, and we may contact you for more information during this period.

questions.title: What should I do after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
For security reasons, the bank account you previously registered with CPF Board would be removed when the CPF Safety Switch was activated. Your bank account will not be automatically reinstated after deactivating the CPF Safety Switch, as your bank account may also have been compromised.
In order to receive CPF payments to your bank account again, you will need to register your bank account with CPF Board. You may also wish to review your registered contact details to ensure that they are up to date. If you are not intending to withdraw soon, you may consider lowering your Daily Withdrawal Limit or activate the CPF Withdrawal Lock.
Find out more about updating your registered bank account, Daily Withdrawal Limit, and activation of CPF Withdrawal Lock. Please note that increasing the Daily Withdrawal Limit, updating your contact details and registering a PayNow-NRIC linked bank account will require a 12-hour cooling period. All other bank account updates will generally take up to two working days to be activated after your bank confirms that the account belongs to you.

questions.title: Can anyone else, including Trusted Contacts, request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch on behalf of a member?
questions.text: No. Deactivation can only be performed by the member, who must complete our authentication process.

questions.title: What happens if I genuinely need to make an urgent withdrawal after activating CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
We understand that members may have legitimate urgent transactions even after activating the CPF Safety Switch. Members can call the CPF hotline or make an appointment to visit any CPF Service Centre during operating hours to request to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch. During this process, CPF Board staff will work with the member to verify their identity, understand their situation and provide guidance on safe practices before reactivating access to CPF online services.
Deactivation of the CPF Safety Switch can only be performed by CPF Board staff after the member’s identity has been verified. This ensures that only the genuine account holder can regain access to their account and helps safeguard members' CPF savings from scammers who might otherwise pressure victims to deactivate the CPF Safety Switch.
Do note that after deactivation, you will still need to update your bank account, which will take 12 hours for a PayNow NRIC-linked bank account or two working days for Interbank GIRO.

questions.title: I received a notification indicating that my CPF Safety Switch activation request is not successful. What should I do next?
questions.text: If you have been scammed, please call us at 1800-227-1188 (+65-6227-1188 if calling from overseas) for assistance. You should also contact your bank to freeze your bank account immediately, and reset your Singpass (for assistance, call Singpass helpdesk at +65 6335 3533).

questions.title: What information do I need to prepare to activate the CPF Safety Switch?
questions.text:
If you are calling the CPF hotline to activate the CPF Safety Switch, you will need to provide your personal details for us to verify your identity.
If you have made an appointment to CPF Service Centre, please be reminded to bring your identification documents (such as NRIC).

questions.title: What is the difference between CPF Safety Switch and CPF Withdrawal Lock?
questions.text:
While both measures effectively disable online CPF withdrawals, the CPF Safety Switch also prevents online access to your CPF account and stops all disbursements to your registered bank account from our records.
Hence, we encourage you to only activate the CPF Safety Switch if you suspect you have fallen victim to a scam. Doing so will immediately cease any unintended monetary outflows and prevent informational loss in the event that your Singpass has been compromised.
If you wish to protect yourself against scams and do not need to withdraw immediately, consider activating the CPF Withdrawal Lock instead which will allow you to maintain your online access to your CPF account.
