questions.title: I wish to apply, retain, or renew a business registration or licence with my business partners. Do all of us need to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for our MediSave payable?
questions.text:
Yes, all owners or partners who wish to apply, retain, or renew their business registration or licence are required to have fully settled or be on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable.
Existing business registrations and licences may be subject to cancellation if any of the owners or partners have not fully settled or are not on a monthly instalment plan for their MediSave payable. The relevant licensing agency (e.g., ACRA) will send a notice to all owners or partners to inform them of any early business registration or licence cancellations.

questions.title: What is Quarantine Order Allowance (QOA)? Who is eligible and how can I apply?
questions.text:
The QOA is set up to mitigate financial impact for those who have been served QO, and completed their QO without any breaches.
Claims of $100 per day can be made by self-employed Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, or Singapore-registered companies whose employees under QO are Singaporean Citizens, Permanent Residents or Work Pass Holders.
As of 1st July 2021, approved caregivers of a Person-Under-Quarantine (PUQ) can apply for the QOA, subject to the same eligibility requirements. Applications can be submitted by self-employed Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents, or by Singapore-registered companies whose employees are Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents or Work Pass Holders.
For employer whose employee is issued with a QO, you can only apply for the QOA after your employee has completed the quarantine and application must be sent to MOH within 90 days.
To apply for Quarantine Order Allowance, click here https://go.gov.sg/moh-qoa-app-form
For enquiries, please write in to MOH_QOA@moh.gov.sg.

questions.title: How do I make a partial repayment or full repayment of my housing loan?
questions.text:
Before making any repayment, check that you have sufficient CPF Ordinary Account (OA) savings and verify that you have not exceeded the maximum amount of CPF savings allowed for your property. You can view your Home ownership dashboard to find your latest housing usage and usage limit (if any).
You can use your CPF savings to make a partial repayment or full repayment of your housing loan through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan:
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Make Partial Repayment of Housing Loan/Make Full Repayment of Housing Loan
Processing time: generally within three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches require prior appointments.
If you are making a full repayment of your housing loan, your HPS cover (if any) will be automatically terminated when we are notified by HDB that you have fully repaid your loan. You do not need to inform the Board to terminate your HPS cover. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF OA.
If you have a bank loan:
Seek approval from your housing loan financier
Submit an online application with your Singpass
For full repayment of housing loan, upload a copy of these documents in the application:
The bank’s redemption statement and
A copy of your lawyer’s legal bill (if any)
Processing time: generally within five working days
If you are making a full repayment of your housing loan, your HPS cover (if any) will be automatically terminated when we are notified by the bank that you have fully repaid your loan. You do not need to inform the Board to terminate your HPS cover. Any unused HPS premium will be paid to your CPF OA.

questions.title: If I did not apply to use my CPF savings when I bought my property that is financed with a bank loan, can I now use my CPF savings for monthly instalments?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF savings for the monthly instalments of your property.
If you own an HDB flat with bank loan:
Submit an online application with your Singpass
Include your financier’s details and your outstanding housing loan amount in the application
If you own a private property with bank loan:
Submit your request through your lawyer
A conveyancing lawyer is required when using your CPF savings for the first time. For more information, please visit this FAQ.
Tips for sustainable housing payments:
While your CPF savings can help with housing payments, remember that these savings are primarily for your future retirement needs. For a sustainable approach, consider the following:
ensure your monthly instalment does not exceed your monthly Ordinary Account (OA) contributions
use a mix of cash and OA savings for housing payments
retain an amount in your OA equivalent to six months' worth of monthly instalments for emergencies
This approach allows you to service your housing loan during unexpected situations while ensuring your OA savings continue earning attractive interest rates.

questions.title: I do not have enough funds in my CPF Ordinary Account for my housing instalment payment because my CPF contributions are credited after the instalment deduction date. What should I do?
questions.text: If your CPF contributions are consistently credited after the deduction date, you may consider making a one-time cash payment to cover one month's instalment. This builds up your account balance, ensuring you have sufficient funds for future deductions before new contributions are credited each month. Once you have made this cash payment, your subsequently monthly instalments should be deducted successfully using your existing Ordinary Account savings.

questions.title: I have withdrawn my CPF savings under the Reduced Life Expectancy scheme. Do I need to refund the CPF principal amount and accrued interest when I sell my property?
questions.text:
Yes, you must refund the principal CPF amount withdrawn for your property and the accrued interest to your CPF account when you sell your property. The refunds will be used to top up your Retirement Account up to your Reduced Retirement Sum (RRS), and any remaining refunds in excess of the RRS will be credited to your Ordinary Account (OA). Check the amount that you have to refund in the “What happens if” section on your Home ownership dashboard.
Withdrawing additional CPF savings after refunds are credited
Once the refunds from your property sale have been credited to your CPF account, you can submit an online request using your Singpass for CPF to assess your eligibility for further withdrawal under the RLE scheme.
We will review your request and inform you of your eligibility status.

questions.title: Why do I need to refund the accrued interest on the amount of CPF savings used for my property?
questions.text:
CPF savings are primarily designed for your retirement needs. When you use these savings to purchase property, the money stops earning interest in your CPF account.
Accrued interest is the interest your CPF savings would have earned if they had remained in your account rather than being used for property purchase.
Refunding both the principal amount and accrued interest ensures your retirement savings are fully restored to what they would have been if they had remained in your CPF account. Without this refund, your retirement funds would be permanently reduced.
The calculation of accrued interest runs from the date you first used your CPF savings until you make the refund. It uses CPF's prevailing interest rates, compounded annually throughout this period.

questions.title: The Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) policy is auto-issued to me. Why do I need to declare my health to be covered under DPS?
questions.text:
Eligibility for Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage is subject to you being in good health at policy commencement.
As with any life insurance, Dependants’ Protection Scheme (DPS) coverage may be declined or deferred if a member has serious pre-existing medical conditions prior to policy commencement. This underwriting practice is essential to ensure the scheme’s viability and maintain affordable premiums for all insured members.
The DPS insurer will not consider claims from members who have serious pre-existing medical conditions, or have provided false or misleading statements or withheld relevant information in their health declaration.
Please refer to Great Eastern Life for further information regarding examples of serious pre-existing medical conditions that may affect your eligibility for coverage.
topics: Account Services / Insuring to protect your dependants

questions.title: Will employers receive support for the increase in CPF contribution rates from 1 January 2027??
questions.text:
The CPF Transition Offset (CTO) will provide transitory wage offsets to help mitigate the rise in business costs due to the increase in CPF contribution rates for senior workers in 2027. This offset is equivalent to half of the increase in employer CPF contribution rates for every Singaporean and Permanent Resident worker they employ who is aged above 55 to 65.
Find out more about CPF Transition Offset.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: How do I apply for an LPA without fees? Is the application process different now?
questions.text: There is no change to the application process. You are encouraged to submit your LPA online at Office of the Public Guardian Online (OPGO) - MSF by logging in with your Singpass. You may refer to the Quick Reference Guide on the OPG website for step-by-step instructions to submit an LPA.
topics: Office of the Public Guardian / LPA Fee Waiver

questions.title: Will I receive CPF Contributions during my traineeship?
questions.text: Trainees are not considered employees during their training period with the agencies and there is no employment relationship, thus Trainees will not receive CPF contributions.

questions.title: As a platform worker, do I still need to declare my income to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore?
questions.text:
For tax purposes, you will need to declare your income derived from platform work and any non-platform work in the year to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). You should declare each source of income separately when filing your tax return to IRAS. Each trade should be reported under its own distinct nature of business category.
For example, if you earned income as a freelance tutor and a private hire car driver, you should declare these sources of income separately, under “Tutor/Lecturer” and “Taxi/Private Hire Car Driver” respectively. This will allow the consolidated statement/Form B from IRAS to display your income from self-employment and platform work as separate items, to facilitate the computation of the mandatory MediSave contributions for your income as a freelance tutor. You may refer to IRAS’ website for more information on reporting your income.
Refer to IRAS’ step-by-step guide to declare your income(s).
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from self-employment and platform work. Why is my net trade income in the notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons not the same as the Notice of Assessment from the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore?
questions.text:
You will need to declare your net trade income (NTI) from both self-employment (non-platform work) and platform work to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). The Notice of Assessment (NOA) issued by IRAS will inform you of the assessable NTI from both self-employment and platform work, as you need to pay income tax on both sources of income.
For work year 2025 onwards, your self-employed MediSave contributions are computed on the NTI after excluding net earnings from platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). This is because CPF contributions on your net earnings from platform work are payable by your platform operator(s). The notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions for your other income earned as a self-employed person.
Learn more about how MediSave contributions are computed. You may use this calculator to compute the mandatory MediSave contributions under the Self-Employed Scheme.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I have already made CPF contributions as a platform worker. Do I still need to contribute MediSave in the following year for my other self-employed work?
questions.text:
For work year 2025 onwards, if you are only receiving platform earnings in the year, platform operators would have deducted and paid the CPF contributions on your platform earnings for you every month. Therefore, you do not need to make your own MediSave contributions on such platform earnings in the following year.
If you derive self-employed income from non-platform work (e.g. giving tuition, or taxi street-hail jobs), you will still need to make MediSave contributions on these incomes in the following year on your own, as per status quo, after you have declared your net trade income (NTI) to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS). Your MediSave contributions are computed on your NTI after excluding net earnings from your platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s). CPF Board will inform you of your mandatory MediSave contributions once IRAS has assessed your income.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from self-employment and platform work. How can I check that the MediSave contributions in my notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons are only for my self-employment income and have excluded my platform work earnings?
questions.text:
In computing your self-employed MediSave contributions, we will first take your annual net trade income (NTI) assessed by IRAS [A], and deduct your net earnings from platform work as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) [B]. The remaining income [C]* is stated in your notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons, and will be used to compute your mandatory MediSave contributions.
* [C] = [A] – [B]
To verify the income stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C], you should first ensure that you have declared each source of income from self-employment and platform work separately to IRAS. Refer to IRAS’ guide for details. You can then download your consolidated statement from IRAS to verify the income shown in your notice of CPF contributions:
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
Your consolidated statement will show the breakdown of your income (in the “Adjusted profit/loss” row), by nature of business.
E.g. assume you are a freelance tutor and private hire car driver. You can verify the NTI stated in your notice of CPF contributions [C] against the “Adjusted profit/loss” reflected under “Tutor/Lecturer” in your consolidated statement.
If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, you can follow the same steps above and verify against your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
If you have difficulties accessing the tax portal, locating notices issued by IRAS, or need to redeclare your income for self-employment and platform work separately, please contact IRAS.
If the income reflected in your notice of CPF contributions [C] differs from the “adjusted profit/loss” stated in the consolidated statement (for the nature of businesses not relating to platform work), please Write to Us and provide us with:
Your consolidated statement (or Form B if you are on paper returns for tax filing); and
All your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s) for the year
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: I earned income from platform work only and my platform operator(s) is/are making CPF contributions on my behalf. Why did I receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed person informing me to make mandatory MediSave contributions?
questions.text:
You will receive a notice of CPF contributions for self-employed persons if your annual net trade income (NTI) exceeds $6,000, after excluding net earnings from platform work declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards.
For work year 2025 onwards, if you only earned income from platform work and received a notice of CPF contributions, please Write To Us so that we can assist with your case. Please provide us with your tax filing consolidated statement issued by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) and your earning slips issued by your platform operator(s). If you are on paper returns for tax filing and are not issued a consolidated statement, please provide us with a copy of your paper individual Income Tax Return (Form B) instead.
You may refer to the following steps or the steps to download notices issued by IRAS (including consolidated statement):
Log in to IRAS’ tax portal
Navigate to Inbox > View notices > Individual
Select the notice that you wish to download, and click “Download selected”
If you encounter any difficulties accessing the tax portal or locating notices issued by IRAS, please contact IRAS for assistance.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Saving as a platform worker with CPF contributions

questions.title: Can I enjoy tax relief as a self-employed person when I make mandatory MediSave contributions or make voluntary top-ups to my CPF accounts?
questions.text:
As a self-employed person (SEP), you can enjoy full tax relief on your mandatory MediSave contributions.
You can also enjoy tax relief as an SEP for the following voluntary contributions:
MediSave contributions made to offset future MediSave payable, made via the Manage your MediSave Payable form; and
Voluntary top-ups to 3 CPF accounts
The tax relief for these voluntary contributions will be capped at the lowest of:
37% of your net trade income1 2 or
CPF annual limit of $37,7402 or
Actual voluntary amount contributed by you
1Excludes net earnings from platform work (if any) as declared to CPF Board by your platform operator(s) for work year 2025 onwards if you are a mandatory or opt in platform worker
2Amount less tax relief allowed on mandatory MediSave contributions
Please visit the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) website for more information.

questions.title: Do Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions qualify for tax relief?
questions.text:
Similar to other forms of self-employed CPF contributions, Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contributions made in a calendar year will qualify for tax relief in the following year. For example, relief on CAYE contributions made between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025 will qualify for tax relief in the Year of Assessment (YA) 2026.
Please refer to this FAQ for more information on the tax eligibility of your contributions.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: I have applied for CareShield Life and my application has been approved. Why does it not show up on the Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section?
questions.text:
Your CareShield Life policy details will only be displayed on your Healthcare dashboard – “CareShield Life/ElderShield” section after successful deduction of your first premium.
Please be assured that your coverage has already commenced from the date your application was approved. You will be eligible to claim if the onset of severe disability falls on or after this date.

questions.title: How do I calculate the CPF contributions based on net earnings of a platform worker?
questions.text:
The CPF contribution is calculated based on platform workers’ net earnings (after fixed expense deduction amount) and the contribution rate applicable to their age, earnings and opt-in status.
Illustration
Step 1: Determine a platform worker’s gross earnings: $3,000
Step 2: Apply the Fixed Expense Deduction Amount (FEDA): 60% expense for cars
Step 3: Compute the net earnings: $3,000 x (1-60%) = $1,200
Step 4: Key in the net earnings into platform worker CPF Contribution Calculator to find out the contributions.
topics: Employer - Platform Operator / How much CPF contributions to contribute

questions.title: Do I need to update my PayNow NRIC-linked bank account as my registered bank account with CPF each time I make a withdrawal or switch to another PayNow-linked bank account?
questions.text:
No, you only need to perform the update of your registered bank account to your PayNow NRIC-linked bank account once and wait 12 hours for it to be activated. You can do so via Account settings. Thereafter, you may apply for retirement withdrawals for immediate needs via PayNow anytime to receive your CPF withdrawals almost instantly.
There is no need to update the Board if you have linked your PayNow-NRIC to a different bank account. Your CPF payments will automatically be made to whichever bank account you have linked to your PayNow-NRIC.

questions.title: What happens to my Retirement Account (RA) savings if I used it to purchase annuity(ies) under the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS), after my renunciation of Singapore Citizenship/ Permanent Residency?
questions.text:
If you are no longer a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, and have previously purchased annuity(ies) using your Retirement Account savings under the Retirement Sum Scheme, any surrender value arising from the termination of such annuities will be paid directly to you by the respective insurer.
In the event of your death, any benefits payable will be paid to your beneficiary in accordance with the terms and conditions of the annuity policy by the insurer.
topics: Account Services / Account closure for non-Singapore Citizens and non-PRs

questions.title: If I have housing arrears, how do I apply to use my CPF savings to pay for it?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to pay for housing arrears through the following methods:
If you have an HDB loan:
Online Application
Visit HDB's website and log in with your Singpass
Navigate to: e-Services > Residential > Servicing your HDB Housing Loan > Pay Overdue Housing Loan or Upgrading Cost with CPF
Processing time: generally within three working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
Please note that all in-person services at HDB Branches require prior appointments.
If you have a bank loan:
Submit an online application with your Singpass at least five working days before the monthly instalment deduction date
Processing time: generally within three working days

questions.title: Where can I check the status of my voluntary housing refund application?
questions.text:
You can check the status of your voluntary housing refund application online via Activities.
Once your application has been successfully processed, the refunded amount will be credited to your CPF account. You can then view the details in your 15-months Transaction History by logging in to my cpf digital services or CPF Mobile app using your Singpass. You will also receive an email notification once your application has been processed.
Please note that the amount refunded will be used to reduce the principal amount withdrawn for your property, followed by its accrued interest.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Voluntary Housing Refund

questions.title: Am I eligible for CPF Housing Grants?
questions.text: CPF Housing Grants (CHG) are administered by HDB. Please visit HDB’s website for the detailed eligibility criteria and application information.

questions.title: What is the difference between joint-tenancy and tenancy-in-common?
questions.text:
The key differences lie in how ownership shares are held and what happens to a co-owner's share when they pass away.
Joint-tenancy
All co-owners have equal interest in the property, regardless of how much each person paid towards the purchase. When a joint tenant dies, their share automatically goes to the remaining co-owner(s), even if they have made a will stating otherwise.
Tenancy-in-common
Each co-owner holds a separate and definite share in the property while having rights to use the entire property. Unlike joint tenancy, owners can hold different ownership percentages. For example, one owner may hold 50% while two others hold 25% each.
When a tenant-in-common passes away, their share does not automatically transfer to the other owners. Instead, it will be distributed on according to their will. If no will exists, the share will be distributed according to the Intestate Succession Act.

questions.title: How can I get my title deed for my property?
questions.text:
You can obtain your title deed after fully paying off your housing loan. The process varies depending on your property type and earlier loan arrangement.
If you own an HDB flat with HDB loan
Contact HDB directly to retrieve your title deed.
If you own an HDB flat with a bank loan
Contact your bank to retrieve your title deed.
If you own a private property
When you use CPF savings to purchase a private property, a CPF charge is created on your property to secure repayment of the amount used plus accrued interest when the property is sold. This CPF charge may remain on the property even after your housing loan is fully paid off.
Once your mortgage and all other charges (including the CPF charge and other registered charges) are fully discharged, please contact SLA to issue your title deed.

questions.title: I obtained an overdraft facility to buy a private property. Can I use my CPF savings to redeem the overdraft?
questions.text:
Yes, you can use your CPF savings to repay the overdraft, provided it was used solely to purchase the private property.
Application Process
You must authorise your lawyer to submit an online application on your behalf by signing the Letter of Authorisation, Declaration, Consent & Agreement.
Required Documents
Your lawyer will need to attach the following documents in the application:
Financier's letter of offer.
Financier's letter to confirm that the overdraft was used strictly to buy the property or was partially used to buy the property. If the overdraft was used partially to buy the property, please attach the monthly statement of account of the overdraft account from the time it was disbursed for payment of the property to the date of application to use CPF savings.
Financier's statement showing the current outstanding amount of the overdraft.
Final Step
Once the application is approved, you will need to arrange for your financier to convert the overdraft facility to a housing loan.

questions.title: I plan to purchase my next property before receiving the CPF refunds from the sale of my current property. How can I proceed if I do not have enough cash or CPF savings to cover the purchase?
questions.text:
You can consider taking a bridging loan from any bank, provided that HDB and/or the bank approve the arrangement.
Important condition to note
The total amount of CPF savings withdrawn plus all loans (including the bridging loan) cannot exceed the lower of the purchase price or the valuation price of the property at the time of purchase.
After selling your existing property
Your CPF savings will be refunded to your CPF accounts. You can then use these funds to pay off the bridging loan once you have completed the legal documentation and settled any outstanding cash amount.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a Small Office Home Office unit?
questions.text:
You can use your CPF savings to purchase a Small Office Home Office (SOHO) unit only if the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) has approved it for residential use. If the unit is approved for office use, you cannot use your CPF savings for the purchase.
SOHO developments are approved by the URA for either office or residential use, but not for both. It is important to verify the approved use of the property before committing to any purchase.

questions.title: What should I do if I would like to use the CPF Housing Top-Up Grant for my HDB flat?
questions.text:
The process depends on your loan type:
If you have an HDB loan
In-person at HDB Branch
Complete the CPF withdrawal form (PHS9)
Book an appointment via the e-Appointment system before visiting
Processing time: generally within three to five working days upon the receipt of your request from HDB
If you have a bank loan
Submit an online application with your Singpass
Processing time: generally within five working days

questions.title: If someone who had used CPF savings for a property passes away, must we repay the CPF housing refund to the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold?
questions.text: No, you do not have to refund the CPF savings used by the late owner’s CPF account when the property is sold.

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property or to pay for the housing loan of my existing property?
questions.text:
If you are buying an HDB flat
You can use your CPF savings to buy an HDB flat or pay the housing loan of your existing HDB flat, provided you are the owner of the HDB flat. You will need to contact HDB directly regarding this matter.
If you are buying a private property
You will need to obtain consent from the Official Assignee before you can use your CPF savings to buy a private property or pay the housing loan of your existing property.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: I am a bankrupt. Can I request to make a partial repayment and leave some monies in my CPF Account for my housing loan?
questions.text: Yes, you can request to make a partial repayment of your housing loan from your CPF account even if you are a bankrupt. This arrangement allows you to retain some funds in your account to continue servicing for your housing loan.
topics: Other Schemes / Matters affecting undischarged bankrupts

questions.title: Where can I check the number of discounted Singtel shares I have?
questions.text: You can login to my cpf Online Services with your Singpass and check the "Discounted Singtel shares" section in the Investment dashboard.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: How can I retrieve my Healthcare payments and claims statement online?
questions.text:
You can view your healthcare payments and claims details (containing information such as the name of patient, hospital registration number (HRN), hospitalisation period, etc), with transaction dates within the last 15 months at cpf.gov.sg/healthcare:
Log in to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass
Proceed to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' and select 'View past 15 months'
Select the period you require and click 'Search'.
Select the PDF icon at the top-right-hand corner of the page to save/print the statement.
Here is a step-by-step guide on how you can retrieve the Healthcare payments and claims statement. To find your downloaded documents on mobile devices, refer to this FAQ.
Please note that your claim details are available on your Healthcare dashboard for up to 15 months, after which they will no longer be retrievable. Download your statement in a timely manner to ensure you always have a copy for your own records or future use.
When submitting reimbursement claims to your employer or insurer, a digital copy should be sufficient.

questions.title: How will the Ordinary Wages (OW) and Additional Wages (AW) that I have submitted to CPF Board be shown at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text: OW and AW will be shown as 'Salary' and 'Bonus' respectively.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: Will donation information submitted to CPF Board be shown at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text:
Donations deducted through employees' salary for CDAC, SINDA and Eurasian Community Fund will be pre-filled under the 'Donations' field.
However, contributions/donations to Mosque Building Fund, Mendaki Fund and Community Chest will not be pre-filled. Employers must manually input these amounts under the respective fields.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: If the contribution details were not e-Submitted to CPF Board by 14 Jan, will the information be pre-filled at the 'Submit Employment Income Records' digital service?
questions.text:
Submissions made after 14 Jan will not be pre-filled and employers will have to manually add the income information which have been submitted to CPF Board after 14 Jan at IRAS' digital service.
For example
If the CPF contribution for the month of Dec 2025 is submitted after 14 Jan 2026, the data for Dec 2025 will not be pre-filled for the YA 2026 submission. You will have to manually add the income information for Dec 2025 at IRAS' digital service.
topics: Individual Income Tax / AIS - Sign up for AIS Data Link-up Service

questions.title: 1. There is a change in my personal particulars. How do I update IRAS?
questions.text:
Find out how to update your personal particulars (e.g. name, marital status,
contact details, residential/mailing address).
topics: Individual Income Tax / Tax Season 2026 - About your tax bill

questions.title: Where can I find information regarding the exercise to transfer Singtel Special Discounted Shares (SDS) to SDS holders?
questions.text: You may refer to sds.singtel.com for information on the exercise to transfer Singtel SDS from CPF Board to SDS holders.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Can I transfer my discounted Singtel shares when I reach 55 years old?
questions.text:
You are required to set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account (RA), before you can transfer your discounted Singtel shares. The FRS can be set aside fully with cash, or with cash (i.e. at least the Basic Retirement Sum) and property.
Have you met your CPF withdrawal conditions?
Yes
Log in to my cpf Online Services with your Singpass > Select my cpf > My dashboards > Investment, look under “Discounted Singtel Shares” section and click on “Withdraw your shares”.
We will process your application within 15 working days once we receive your application.
After your discounted Singtel shares have been transferred to your Central Depository Pte Ltd (CDP) securities account, they will no longer be protected from any claims by your creditors and/or the Official Assignee.
No
You can only transfer your discounted Singtel shares if you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum (FRS) in your Retirement Account at age 55. However, you can sell your discounted Singtel shares, in which the sale proceeds will be credited into your CPF Ordinary Account.
To sell, please log in to my cpf Online Services with your Singpass > Select my cpf > My dashboards > Investment, look under “Discounted Singtel Shares” section and click on “Sell your shares”.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will my discounted Singtel shares be sold or liquidated when I apply to transfer my discounted Singtel shares upon meeting CPF withdrawal conditions?
questions.text: Transferring your discounted Singtel shares will not result in liquidation of your shares. It is a request to the Board to transfer the discounted Singtel shares to your Central Depository Pte ltd (CDP) securities account. Once the shares have been transferred, you will receive a statement from CDP and the Board.
topics: Growing Your Savings / CPF Investment Schemes

questions.title: Will I be notified if my application is unsuccessful?
questions.text:
We aim to update applicants on the outcome of their application where possible.
Shortlisted candidates will be contacted with further details on the next steps.

questions.title: Why am I unable to log in to CPF EZPay?
questions.text:
You must first be appointed as an Administrator or Editor for CPF EZPay before you can access the CPF EZPay.
If you have been appointed the Administrator for CPF EZPay via Corppass for an UEN-registered entity but still cannot log in, please check the error message you received:
Error: “You do not have a valid CSN to log in to the system. Please contact your Corppass Admin for access.”
Contact your Corppass Admin or Sub-Admin to set up and assign “CPF EZPay” e-Service to you for that CSN in Corpass portal.
Error: “You have not been assigned access to the CPF EZPay e-service, or your access has expired.”
Contact your Corppass Admin or Sub-Admin to assign or renew the “CPF EZPay” e-Service for your account in Corppass portal.
If you continue to experience login difficulties after following these steps, please write to us for further assistance.
topics: Employer - Making CPF Contributions / CPF EZPay
Employer - Platform Operator / Submission via CPF EZPay

questions.title: Can I get the Public Trustee’s assistance in resealing in Singapore, Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that was obtained overseas
questions.text:
The Public Trustee does not assist in resealing in the Singapore Courts for Letters of Administration / Grant of Probate that were obtained overseas. You will have to engage a Singapore lawyer to assist you.
You can search for a Singapore law practice or lawyer using the Legal Services Regulatory Authority's online search function athttps://eservices.mlaw.gov.sg/lsra/search-lawyer-or-law-firm/. Please note that the search results are based on information provided by law practices and lawyers. The Ministry of Law does not make any warranty or representation as to their accuracy, completeness or reliability.

questions.title: Do I need to pay CPF contributions for my foreign employee who has recently obtained Singapore Permanent Residence status?
questions.text:
Yes, CPF contributions are payable once your foreign employee obtains his Singapore Permanent Resident (SPR) status. Please ensure that your employee informs you of his SPR status.
For the first two years of obtaining the SPR status, to help your employee adjust to the lower take-home pay, both you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at graduated rates (refer to Tables 2 and 3). From the third year onwards, you and your SPR employee will contribute CPF at the full rates (refer to Table 1).
Determining your employee’s year of SPR status
The year of SPR status determines your employee’s CPF contribution rates.
First-year rate: Applies from the day your employee obtains his SPR status until the last day of the month of his first anniversary. The SPR status date is shown on his Entry Permit (Form 5/5A) issued by the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA).
Second-year rate: Applies from the month following his first anniversary as an SPR until the last day of the month of his second anniversary.
Third-year rate: Applies from the month following his second anniversary as an SPR onwards.
Example
If your employee obtained his SPR status on 15 January 2026, the start and end dates for first, second and third year of obtaining SPR status are shown in the table below:
Years of obtaining SPR statusStarts fromEnds on
First year15 January 202631 January 2027
Second year1 February 202731 January 2028
Third year1 February 2028Not applicable
Computing CPF contributions
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Example
Assuming your employee obtains his SPR status on 15 March 2026 and he receives OW and AW for March 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is required on the pro-rated wages from 15 to 31 March 2026.
For AW
• CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable while the employee was a foreigner i.e. before 15 March 2026.
• CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable on or after 15 March 2026.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Can I nominate a foreign person?
questions.text:
If you are nominating someone who is not a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, please provide the nominee’s full name, foreign identification number and mailing address in your nomination form so that the Board can contact him swiftly when distributing your CPF savings.
Please note that if you are nominating a foreigner or a Singapore Citizen / Permanent Resident residing overseas, there may be inheritance tax implications in the country of residence. You are advised to seek your own legal or tax advice in the country of residence before making your nomination.

questions.title: How often should I review or update my nomination?
questions.text: Members are encouraged to review their nomination annually or more regularly if experiencing key life milestones, such as marriage, childbirth, divorce, death of a nominee, or entering their golden years. Reviewing and updating CPF nominations allows their CPF savings to be distributed according to their latest bequeath intentions.

questions.title: I made my CPF nomination many years ago. Why can't I view it online?
questions.text:
CPF nominations made many years ago were typically handwritten on hardcopy forms. Such old nominations may contain illegible handwriting, and this makes accurate transcription of the details for online viewing challenging. As such, these old nomination details cannot be made available online.
You are encouraged to make a new CPF nomination. Once you make a new nomination, you will be able to view your latest nomination details online.

questions.title: How can I get a referral for subsidised care at public SOCs?
questions.text: A referral for subsidised care at public SOCs can be obtained from either CHAS clinics or polyclinics. Do note that you will need to be a PG/MG/CHAS cardholder to obtain subsidised SOC referrals from CHAS clinics.

questions.title: Can I take a vaccination if I am currently unwell, such as having the flu?
questions.text:
It is generally recommended to postpone vaccinations if you are experiencing moderate to severe illness, such as a high fever or significant flu symptoms. However, if your symptoms are mild, you may still be able to take the vaccination.
To ensure your safety, consult your doctor or healthcare provider for advice tailored to your specific health condition before proceeding with the vaccination.

questions.title: I’m allergic to the flu vaccine but received a push notification from the HealthHub app. Does this mean I can now take the vaccine?
questions.text: Receiving a push notification from the HealthHub app does not necessarily mean that you are now suitable to take the flu vaccine if you are allergic to it. The notification is a general reminder for flu vaccination. If you have a known allergy to the flu vaccine, consult your healthcare provider before proceeding. They can assess your medical history and advise if the vaccination is suitable for you or whether alternative flu vaccine options are available.

questions.title: When will I know if my proposal will be supported?
questions.text: Evaluation outcome letters will be sent out to operators who have submitted proposals by Oct 2026. Operators are expected to implement proposals from Nov 2026 onwards and complete them within a year. Final reports will need to be submitted by Jan 2028.

questions.title: If one or all of my nominees pass away before me, what will happen to their share of monies?
questions.text:
If your nominee passes on before you, his/her share will be given to the surviving nominee(s) in the same proportion you have specified.
For example, a CPF member made the following nomination:
Nominee A: 60%
Nominee B: 30%
Nominee C: 10%
Nominee A passed on and the CPF member did not make a new nomination. Nominee A's 60% share will be redistributed between the surviving nominees (i.e. Nominee B and Nominee C) in proportion to their original allocations. The distribution outcome will be as follows:
Nominee B will receive 75% (30% of 40%* = 75%)
Nominee C will receive 25% (10% of 40%* = 25%)
*40% is the total shares originally allocated to Nominee B and C.
If there are no surviving nominee(s), your nomination is considered revoked and your savings will be transferred to the Public Trustee’s Office for distribution under the intestacy or Muslim Inheritance laws.

questions.title: Can I use my CPF savings to buy a property with a lease of less than 20 years?
questions.text: No. To use your CPF savings for property purchase, the property must have a remaining lease of more than 20 years. This requirement ensures the prudent use of your CPF savings and aligns with HDB loan eligibility criteria.

questions.title: Who is responsible for reimbursing my MediSave Account for hospitalisation expenses?
questions.text: Third parties with a contractual obligation (e.g. your employer or insurer) are required to reimburse your MediSave Account for your hospitalisation expenses.

questions.title: How can I check the status of my reimbursement if I have already submitted a claim to my insurer after using my MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses?
questions.text:
You can check your reimbursement status on cpf.gov.sg/healthcare.
Simply login to your Healthcare dashboard under my cpf digital services with your Singpass, and go to 'Latest healthcare payments and claims' to view the recent transactions. You can also click on 'View past 15 months' to see additional transactions.
For reimbursed claims, you will see the message "You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details". Click 'View details' to see the reimbursement details.

questions.title: Can an overseas insurance company disburse the approved reimbursement to my MediSave Account via telegraphic transfer, or is it only by cheque?
questions.text: Your insurer may submit reimbursements to MediSave and/or MediShield Life electronically via the MediSave/MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service.

questions.title: How can I apply for reimbursements for my MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text:
If you have utilised your MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, and your employer or insurer has contractual obligations to reimburse you for your medical expenses, please approach them to find out how they can reimburse to your MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
Your employer or insurer may require you to provide the following supporting documents:
i. Finalised medical bill - showing the itemised charges and the source of payment (e.g. cash, MediSave, Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life).
ii. Healthcare payments and claims statement - showing the payment information including the Hospital Registration Number (HRN) used to identify the claim details for reimbursement purposes. The HRN is a 13-character alphanumeric registration number (e.g. 522016A02QL6E). You can retrieve this statement online from your Healthcare dashboard.
For claims that have been reimbursed, you will see the message 'You have been reimbursed for this claim. View details'. Click 'View details' to view the reimbursement details on the Healthcare payments and claims statement.
If you do not have Singpass, you can register for an account online.

questions.title: If I used cash, MediSave and MediShield Life for my medical bill, is there a specific order in which my employer or insurer should perform the reimbursement?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, your employer or insurer should reimburse you in the following order:
i. Cash reimbursement - For the amount you paid in cash.
ii. MediSave reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your payer's or your MediSave Account.
iii. MediShield Life reimbursement - For the amount utilised from your MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life.
This order minimises your cash outlay and restores the balances in your MediSave Account.

questions.title: I am making a reimbursement claim from my employer or insurer for my medical bills. Is it compulsory to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement?
questions.text: CPF Board does not require any documents from your employer or insurer to process the reimbursement. You are not required to provide a hardcopy Healthcare payments and claims statement when making a reimbursement claim. If your employer or insurer requests a statement, they should accept a digital copy.

questions.title: When do I need to apply for reimbursement to my MediSave and/or MediShield Life from my third-party-payers for my healthcare expense?
questions.text:
Please submit your reimbursement request to your employer or insurer once your MediSave and/or MediShield Life claims have been processed and reflected in your Healthcare payments and claims statement. Your employer or insurer may need your Healthcare payments and claim statement to assess your request. Find out more on how to retrieve your Healthcare payments and claims statements and apply for reimbursement.
Please note that your Healthcare payments and claims statement will no longer be available for retrieval once it is older than 15 months.

questions.title: How do I apply to use Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay my outstanding CPF education loan?
questions.text:
You may log in to the Student Finance System (SFS) via the Ministry of Education (MOE) website using your Singpass and apply for the use of your Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) funds to repay your outstanding CPF education loan.
Please note that your request will be submitted directly to MOE for processing.
topics: Other Schemes / CPF Education Loan Scheme

questions.title: My employee has renounced his Singapore Citizenship/Singapore Permanent Resident status. Do I need to pay his CPF for the entire month?
questions.text:
If your employee has renounced his Singapore Citizen/Singapore Permanent Resident (SC/SPR) status, you would need to pay CPF contributions for him for the period when he is still a SC/SPR. CPF contributions are not required from the day your employee becomes a foreigner.
For Ordinary Wages (OW), you will need to pay CPF contributions on the pro-rated OW. For Additional Wages (AW), CPF contributions are required depending on when the AW is payable to your employee.
Please ensure your employee informs you when he renounces his SC/SPR status.
Example
Assuming your employee renounces his SC/SPR status and becomes a foreigner on 10 January 2026 and he receives OW and AW for January 2026.
For OW
CPF contribution is only required on the pro-rated wages for the period 1 to 9 January 2026.
For AW
CPF contribution is required on the AW if it is payable to the employee between 1 to 9 January 2026.
CPF contribution is not required on the AW if it is payable on or after 10 January 2026.
topics: Employer - Employer Obligations / How much CPF contributions to pay

questions.title: Who can I contact if I have further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement?
questions.text: For any further enquiries about MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement, please write to us and we will assist you with your enquiries.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Are there any charges for the MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service?
questions.text: The MediSave and/or MediShield Life Internet Reimbursement service is provided free of charge.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: In what order should I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds if they have paid for medical expenses using cash, MediSave and MediShield Life?
questions.text:
Subject to contractual obligations, the reimbursement order should be as follows:
Amount paid in cash
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave
Amount utilised from your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave-approved Integrated Shield Plan or MediShield Life
This order minimises your employees, platform workers or insureds' cash outlay, and preserves their MediSave for future use.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I was notified by the Medical Institution that my employee, platform worker or insured's medical bill was cancelled or amended. How can I make changes to the reimbursement I submitted earlier?
questions.text: If you need to amend the MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursement you previously submitted, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: I need to submit a reimbursement to my employee, platform worker or insured's MediSave and/or MediShield Life. How do I go about doing it?
questions.text:
You can submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements to your employee, platform worker or insured quickly and easily via CPF's online reimbursement system, also known as the Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
Learn more about how to submit a reimbursement via the IR service.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Do I need to reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life within a specific time period?
questions.text: We strongly encourage you to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds promptly. Timely reimbursement is particularly helpful if they need their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for further treatments.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Can I reimburse my employees, platform workers or insureds in cash for a medical bill paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life?
questions.text: You cannot reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds in cash if the medical bill was paid using their MediSave and/or MediShield Life. The reimbursement for the utilised amount must be made directly to the employees, platform workers or insureds’ MediSave and/or MediShield Life.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: Apart from the Internet Reimbursement service, are there other ways to submit MediSave and/or MediShield Life reimbursements?
questions.text:
To support our go green program and the Smart Nation initiative, we only accept reimbursements via our Internet Reimbursement (IR) service.
If you encounter any difficulties while submitting reimbursements via this IR service, please write to us for assistance.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: If my employees, platform workers or insureds have used their MediSave and/or MediShield Life for medical expenses, do I need to reimburse them?
questions.text: As an employer, platform operator or insurer, you are required to reimburse your employees, platform workers or insureds' MediSave and/or MediShield Life if you have a contractual obligation to cover their medical expenses.
topics: Employer - Business Partners / MediSave/MediShield Life reimbursement

questions.title: What happens if the amount of MediSave contributions the self-employed person has made via Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) is lower than his MediSave payable for the year?
questions.text:
The self-employed person (SEP)’s MediSave payable for income earned in the year will be computed after the SEP has declared his actual income in the following year.
If the SEP’s total Contribute As You Earn (CAYE) contribution is lower than his MediSave payable for the latest year, he will be required to top up the shortfall.
Example:
Sam has made a total contribution of $2,100 via CAYE in 2023. The following year, Sam is informed that his MediSave payable for his work done in 2023 is $3,000. Sam will have to top-up the shortfall of $900.
This example is illustrated within the table below:
Estimated 2023 NTI
$21,000
CAYE contributions in 2023
$2,100
(After 2023 NTI declaration)
Declared 2023 NTI
$30,000
MediSave payable for work done in 2023
$3,000
Shortfall Sam has to top up
$900
(i.e. $3,000 - $2,100)
topics: Employer - Corporate Service Buyers / Contribute As You Earn

questions.title: What is CPF at Your Service?
questions.text:
CPF at Your Service is an initiative that brings CPF services directly to seniors in the community, instead of requiring them to visit CPF Service Centres.
Through partnerships with selected Active Ageing Centres across Singapore, CPF officers and volunteers will provide this personalised assistance at locations where seniors already gather and are familiar with. The initiative is part of CPF Board’s commitment to reaching seniors who may benefit from guidance on their CPF matters.
CPF at Your Service can help you with:
Checking your CPF retirement, housing and healthcare scheme status
Updating your contact details or registered bank account
Understanding your CPF top-up eligibility and how to make top-ups
Understanding your retirement withdrawal eligibility and the withdrawal process
To find out when CPF at Your Service will be at an Active Ageing Centre near you, please check for event announcements at your Active Ageing Centre.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / General information on CPF Board

questions.title: How do I know if my refund for PayNow QR, Apple Pay or Google Pay has been completed?
questions.text:
Refunds will be credited back to the original payment method used:
PayNow QR: refunded to the bank account linked to the PayNow transaction
Apple Pay / Google Pay: refunded to the underlying card linked to the digital wallet
A separate notification may not be sent when the refund is processed. We recommend checking your bank or card statement to confirm.
To check whether your refund has been completed, please refer to:
Your bank account statement or banking app transaction history (for PayNow QR refunds), or
Your credit or debit card statement linked to Apple Pay or Google Pay
Refund processing time may vary depending on your bank or card issuer.

questions.title: Why is there no breakdown of the deceased member’s CPF balances in the Deceased CPF Member Dashboard?
questions.text:
You can view the overall amount left in the deceased member’s CPF account under “Outstanding CPF balance”. This shows the combined total of all monies across the deceased member’s CPF accounts.
You may click on "View Transactions" to see a more detailed transaction history of the deceased's CPF accounts.

questions.title: I am an employee and/or platform worker, while also earning income as a self-employed person (SEP). How much Workfare Income Supplement will I receive in the same year?
questions.text:
You are considered a dual or multi status worker if you have more than one work status in the same year (employee, platform worker, self-employed person).
There are two parts to the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) payment:
Monthly payments: Based on your employee and/or platform worker income if you meet the eligibility criteria.
Additional payment: After you declare your self-employment income (if any) and contribute the required MediSave in full, we’ll assess your eligibility.
You may receive additional WIS if your average monthly combined income qualifies for a higher WIS amount than what you already received and does not exceed the $3,000 threshold per month.
How much you receive will depend on your total income across all work types. Please refer to this FAQ for the maximum WIS amounts.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How can I access my next-of-kin's CPF account information if I cannot obtain their legal authorisation to receive it?
questions.text:
The Board, as a trustee of CPF monies belonging to CPF account holders, has a legal duty to maintain the confidentiality of their account information.
CPF Board will release account details — such as transaction history or a Yearly Statement of Account — only if one of the following applies:
The CPF member makes the request themselves
You have a Court Order authorising you to receive the information
You hold an activated Lasting Power of Attorney that covers this
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: I am the primary caregiver for my next-of-kin. How do I request Transaction History on their behalf?
questions.text:
There are three ways to help your next-of-kin to access their Transaction History as their primary caregiver:
Option 1: Next-of-kin accesses Transaction History via Singpass
Your next-of-kin can log in with Singpass on the CPF Mobile app or my cpf digital services to view, save or download their Transaction History. Please refer to this FAQ for a step-by-step guide.
If your next-of-kin does not have a Singpass, they can visit the Singpass website to obtain one.
Option 2: Caregiver assistance through Singpass Multi-User SMS 2FA
If your next-of-kin needs help with government digital services, they can set you up as a trusted caregiver through the Singpass Multi-User SMS 2FA. This is a one-time setup, which allows you to help your next-of-kin access their CPF account information online more conveniently in future.
Please refer to Singpass FAQs for more information on Multi-User SMS 2FA.
Option 3: Appointed donee/deputy
If you are the appointed donee/deputy for your next-of-kin under the Mental Capacity Act, you can access their CPF information directly using Singpass Multi-User SMS 2FA.
Please refer to this FAQ for the process and required documents.
If you are unable to access your next-of-kin’s Transaction History through the options above, please refer to this FAQ for more information.
topics: General Information & Useful Tips / Statement of account

questions.title: Is mediation compulsory before I am able commence a claim at the Employment Claims Tribunals?
questions.text:
Mediation at the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) is compulsory before claims can be filed at the Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT).
Additionally, you may only file a claim at the ECT if both of the following applies:
(a) Your dispute is unresolved after mediation at TADM.
(b) You have been issued a Claim Referral Certificate by an approved TADM mediator.
If you have yet to file a mediation request, you may do so at this link: https://www.tal.sg/tadm/eservices
topics: Employment Claims Tribunals / Commencing an Employment Claim: Prerequisities

questions.title: What is Service? / What does Service mean?
questions.text:
"Service" refers to the delivering of the document to the Respondent. This can be done by Personal Service (delivering hard copies of the document physically to the Respondent), by Registered Post to their last known residential or registered address or ACRA registered address (for businesses), or by any other means as directed by the ECT.
For more information, you may visit https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/civil/how-to-file-serve-employment-claim - under the "How to file and serve" section.
topics: Employment Claims Tribunals / Commencing an Employment Claim: Service

questions.title: Why are platform workers who have not opted in to the increased CPF contributions ineligible to receive Workfare Income Supplement aligned to that of employees from 2029?
questions.text: Platform workers who have not opted in to increased CPF contributions will continue to contribute to their Medisave Account only, like self-employed persons (SEPs). Thus, the Workfare Income Supplement for these eligible platform workers are aligned with SEPs.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: How will the monthly per capita household income be determined for assessing one's eligibility for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
The monthly per capita household income is calculated by dividing the total gross household monthly income by the total number of family members living together. Gross monthly household income includes basic employment income, trade/self-employed income, overtime pay, allowances, cash awards, commissions, and bonuses.
The monthly income of each member will be determined based on the following:
Salaried Employees:
1. Monthly income as declared to CPF Board by the member’s employer(s), averaged over 12 months; or
2. The latest available annual income assessment by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) within the last two calendar years.
Self-Employed Persons:
1. Monthly income as declared to CPF Board by the member as a self-employed person, averaged over 12 months; or
2. The latest available annual income assessment by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) within the last two calendar years.
Platform Workers:
1. Monthly income as declared to CPF Board by the member’s platform operator(s), averaged over 12 months; or
2. The latest available annual income assessment by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) within the last two calendar years.
If there have been recent changes to your circumstances that may affect your eligibility, please write to us for a reassessment and we will work with the HOusehold Means Eligibility System (HOMES) team to have your household means tested.

questions.title: How can I change my mode of payment to receive cash benefits from the Government?
questions.text:
There are two options to update the mode of payment for your government cash benefits:
Option 1: Link your NRIC to PayNow
You are encouraged to link your NRIC to PayNow as government cash benefits will be credited to your PayNow-NRIC-linked bank account. To find out more on how to link your NRIC to PayNow, please refer to this FAQ.
If your NRIC is linked to your PayNow, there is no need for you to provide your bank account details.
Option 2: Provide your bank account details
You can submit your bank account details by logging in to our e-services with your Singpass. The bank account that you provide will only be used if you do not have a PayNow-NRIC linked bank account.
Bank crediting is available only via the three local banking groups DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB, and your bank account must be a personal or joint account linked to your NRIC number.
The Government will verify the bank account details you have registered with your bank. If you have closed your bank account, ceased being a joint account holder, or provided incorrect bank account details, you will be asked to update your bank account details. A letter will be sent to your NRIC address.
No further action is required if you have already linked your NRIC to PayNow with a participating bank.

questions.title: How is the Annual Value (AV) requirement for Workfare Income Supplement scheme determined and which address is used to calculate it?
questions.text:
The Annual Value (AV) threshold for Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) covers all HDB flats and some smaller private residences. In general, Singaporeans staying in larger properties with an AV above the threshold tend to have greater access to household wealth, making them ineligible for WIS.
The AV of a property is the estimated market rental of similar properties in the area, as determined by IRAS.
To assess your WIS eligibility, we use your NRIC address to check the AV of your place of residence. For accurate assessment, please ensure your NRIC reflects your current place of residence.
Under the National Registration Act, you are required to report any change of address within 28 days at the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority (ICA) website.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is my spouse's Assessable Income for the previous Year of Assessment used to determine my Workfare Income Supplement in the current work year?
questions.text:
This is to allow for quicker assessment of Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) eligibility. As Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) needs time to process Income data for the current work year, we use the latest Assessable Income (AI) data to determine eligibility.
The AI for the previous Year of Assessment (YOA) is used to assess one's WIS eligibility for the current year. For example, we will use your spouse's AI for YOA 2025 to assess your eligibility for 2026 WIS.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why will the Workfare Income Supplement for platform workers be aligned with that of employees only in 2029, when their increased CPF contributions were implemented in 2025?
questions.text:
CPF contributions rates for platform workers will gradually increase from 2025 to 2028, and will fully align with those of employees in 2029. Correspondingly, the Workfare Income Supplement will be aligned with employee rates only from 2029, for platform workers who are mandated or have opted in to the increased CPF contributions.
During this period, the Platform Workers CPF Transition Support (PCTS) will provide monthly cash payments to support lower-income platform workers who make increased CPF contributions. The PCTS will fully cover the increase in CPF contributions in 2025 and will gradually taper off before ending in 2029.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is my Workfare Income Supplement amount different from previous months?
questions.text:
For employees and platform workers, your Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) amount may differ monthly as it depends on your income. It is assessed monthly based on your total gross income as declared by your employer or platform operator in the CPF submissions. If you have more than one source of income, income from all sources will be considered. Any change in your total income can result in a different WIS payment.
You can use the online WIS calculator to estimate your payment.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: When will I get my Workfare Income Supplement payment?
questions.text:
This depends on your employment type.
For an employee and/or platform worker1,2
We usually pay your Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) two months after the month you worked. You will receive WIS for every month you work.
If you worked inYou will receive the WIS in your bank account or via GovCash
PayNow-NRIC / Bank CreditingGovCash
JanEnd Mar1st week of April
FebEnd Apr1st week of May
MarEnd May1st week of June
Month xEnd of month (x+2)1st week of the following month (x+3)
You can log in to our e-services with your Singpass to check your payment details after the payment has been made to your bank account or via GovCash.
For a self-employed person (SEP)
You will get WIS payment yearly for work done in the previous Work Year (WY).
To get the earliest payment by end April of the following WY (WY + 1), you need to complete these by 31 March of the following year (WY + 1):
Declare your net trade income (NTI) to IRAS
Make your corresponding MediSave contributions in full based on your declared NTI earned in the WY without accounting for previous years’ losses
If you declare your income and make your MediSave contributions after 31 March of the following year (WY + 1), you will get your WIS within two months after you complete making your MediSave contributions.
1For Work Year 2024 and earlier, platform workers receive WIS as SEPs. Please refer to the 'WIS for self-employed persons' for more information.
2If you have also worked as a SEP in the same work year, you may get additional WIS as a dual status worker.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: What if I prefer not to receive payments via GovCash?
questions.text:
If you prefer not to receive your payments via Govcash, there are two options available:
Option 1: Link your NRIC to PayNow with a participating bank
We encourage you to link your NRIC to PayNow with a participating PayNow-GIRO bank.
The list of PayNow-GIRO-participating banks are: Bank of China, CIMB, Citibank, DBS Bank / POSB, GXS Bank, HL Bank, HSBC Bank, ICBC, MariBank, Maybank, OCBC Bank, RHB Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, State Bank of India, Trust Bank and UOB Bank.
If your preferred bank is on this list, contact your bank for details on how to link your NRIC to PayNow.
Once you link your NRIC to PayNow, future Government benefits you are eligible for will be automatically credited to your PayNow-linked bank account.
Option 2: Register your bank account details
Alternatively, you can choose to receive your payments via crediting to your bank account. To do so, log in to the e-services using your Singpass, select “Bank Account Submission” and update your POSB/DBS, OCBC or UOB bank account details.
Bank crediting is available only via the three local banking groups DBS/POSB, OCBC, UOB, and your bank account must be a personal or joint account registered with your NRIC number.
The Government will verify the bank account details you have registered with your bank. If you have closed your bank account, ceased being a joint account holder, or have provided incorrect bank account details, you will be asked to update your bank account details. A letter will be sent to your NRIC address.
topics: Growing Your Savings / Workfare Income Supplement Scheme

questions.title: Why is monthly per capita household income used as an indication of my family support for the Silver Support Scheme?
questions.text:
The Silver Support (SS) Scheme is targeted at seniors who had low incomes during their working years and now have little or no family support and resources in their retirement.
To automatically identify seniors who are eligible for SS, the Government has to rely on available data as broad indicators of an individual’s ability to save for retirement, access to resources and family support.
We have relied on the monthly per capita household income as a broad indicator of the level of family support available.

questions.title: Can I use CPF savings for my full-time subsidised local degree course if I have previously used CPF savings for my first subsidised diploma course?
questions.text: You can use CPF savings for your degree course as long as it is an approved full-time subsidised course under the CPF Education Loan Scheme, subject to the available withdrawal limit.

questions.title: What is the SGSHARE Programme?
questions.text:
SGSHARE is the national regular-giving programme that supports communities in need. It is an initiative by Community Chest, the philanthropic arm of the National Council of Social Service, to provide sustained funding for programmes and capability-building for social service agencies serving communities in need.
The CPF Board collects your employees’ SGSHARE donations on behalf of Community Chest, from the employees’ wages made through the company payroll.

questions.title: How do I pay my employees' SGSHARE donations?
questions.text: You are expected to deduct the SGSHARE donations from your employees’ wages and pay the SGSHARE donations together with the CPF contributions.

questions.title: My employees do not wish to contribute to the SGSHARE programme. What can they do?
questions.text: Your employees can contact the HR department to cease the payroll deduction if they do not wish to contribute to SGSHARE programme.

questions.title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for dental treatments?
questions.text:
You can use your MediSave for selected complex dental procedures that involve surgery and are performed for medical reasons, subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries.
If you are aged 60 or older, you can also use your available withdrawal limit under Flexi-MediSave for selected non-surgical dental procedures such as permanent crowns and root canal treatments.
Please check with your dentist whether your dental treatments are MediSave-claimable.

questions.title: Can I use MediSave to pay the MediShield Life deductible for outpatient treatment?
questions.text: Yes, you can use your MediSave to pay for your MediShield Life outpatient deductible. There is also MediFund to help those who are unable to afford their bills even after subsidies, MediShield Life, and MediSave. Nobody will be denied appropriate care due to an inability to pay.

questions.title: I was told by my dentist that Flexi-MediSave does not cover all dental treatments. Why is that so?
questions.text:
Flexi-MediSave is meant to help with recurrent outpatient medical expenses, which many older Singaporeans have raised as a key concern due to significant accumulated bill sizes over the longer term.
Flexi-MediSave can be used for select restorative dental procedures, i.e. permanent crowns and root canal treatments which can be relatively more costly. Other dental expenses are not covered under Flexi-MediSave and patients can benefit from generous government subsidies to cover costs – for example, at CHAS dental clinics and public institutions such as the polyclinics and National Dental Centre.
Nevertheless, you can use MediSave under the MediSave withdrawal limits applicable for day surgeries for selected complex dental procedures.

questions.title: I can't find my Year-in-Review. How do I access it?
questions.text:
As part of our ongoing efforts to improve our services and better engage our members, we have heard your feedback for more forward-planning tools and have recently launched PLAN with CPF – your one-stop financial guidance platform that helps you make informed financial decisions as you navigate through life. We have discontinued the Year-in-Review pilot from June 2026.
You may continue to view your annual CPF balances, inflow and outflow using the Yearly Statement of Account (YSOA) or check Transaction history for recent activities.
